title: BREAKING: Dhurandhar to OPEN Indian Panorama at 57th IFFI Goa 2026 while Ramayana to open BRICS segment; The Kerala Story 2 enters PRESTIGIOUS International Competition
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Curtain Raiser Press Conference of the 57th International Movie Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, held at Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon, Goa, on November 13, was inaugurated by the Chief Minister of Goa, Dr Pramod Sawant, who unveiled the festival’s expansive programme celebrating Indian and international cinema. Expressing pride in Goa’s association with IFFI, he described the festival as an integral part of the state’s cultural identity and calendar. He also highlighted the state government’s preparations to welcome the global movie fraternity, with arrangements for screening venues, transport, hospitality and public facilities.

Adding to this, The Curtain Raiser Press event was also attended by M Delilah M. Lobo, Vice Chairperson, Entertainment Society of Goa, Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, Krishna Kumar, Chairperson, NFDC, and Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director, IFFI 2026, Prabhat, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; Madhur Bhandarkar, Chairperson, Feature Movie Jury; Himanshu Shekhar Khatua, Chairperson, Non-Feature Movie Jury; Deepak Mandekar, CEO, Entertainment Society of Goa; and Dheeraj Singh, Managing Director, NFDC, & Smita Vats Sharma, DG West Zone PIB.

Meanwhile, The opening movie, Fatherland , directed by Paweł Pawlikowski, follows Nobel laureate Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika as they travel through post-war, divided Germany in 1949, exploring the political and personal divisions of the time. The movie received the Best Director Award at the 2026 Cannes Movie Festival and was also nominated for the Sydney Movie Prize 2026.

Notably, The 57th International Movie Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will showcase I Matter , directed by Alina Șerban, as its Mid-Fest Movie. A 101-minute movie co-produced by Romania, Germany and Belgium, it features dialogues in Romanian and Romani, bringing a diverse European cinematic perspective to the festival.

As per the latest buzz, The Gala Premieres segment will feature 14 screenings, with participation from 87 countries showcasing a curated selection of films and providing audiences an opportunity to experience diverse cinematic stories and acclaimed filmmaking.

In further updates, The 57th International Movie Festival of India (IFFI) highlights Spain as the Country of Honour, showcasing four Spanish films: The Bad Son , directed by Jaime Lorente; Trinidad; Bitter Christmas , directed by Pedro Almodóvar; and Persegiuiendo a Michael , directed by Jaime Machia. The selection celebrates Spanish cinema and its diverse storytelling, bringing Spanish filmmakers and cinematic perspectives to the international platform of IFFI.

On top of that, The 57th International Movie Festival of India (IFFI) presents Russia as the Partner Country, with a special showcase of four films representing the diversity and creative richness of Russian cinema. The featured films include Four ( Четыре ), New Home, Bo Bo , directed by Anastasia Kuzina, and Sidney Lumet’s Birthday . The showcase provides Indian and international audiences with an opportunity to discover contemporary Russian filmmaking, engage with its evolving cinematic landscape and appreciate the cultural and artistic exchange between India and Russia through the medium of cinema.

The 57th International Movie Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 has introduced two new segments this year to broaden its cinematic offerings and celebrate diverse forms of storytelling. The first segment, Animation, will feature five outstanding films, showcasing creativity and innovation in animated cinema. The second segment, Films About Films, will also present five films and has been introduced in response to suggestions from renowned filmmakers, with the objective of bringing the art and craft of filmmaking to the forefront.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 9: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer crosses ₹600 crore, beats lifetime haul of Chhaava
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana , starring Ranbir Kapoor , Yash and Sai Pallavi, rolled out in theatres on November 5. The movie did great business on its opening day, setting a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. After a dip, the movie showed a sharp growth over the extended Diwali holiday period. It crossed ₹ 500 crore rupees within 6 days of rollout.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor portrays Ram in the movie Ramayana Ramayana ticket-window update Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 days before rollout. By the time of its rollout, the movie had already sold tickets worth ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. The movie went on to collect ₹ 64.85 crore rupees in India on its first day of rollout, becoming the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. Friday saw a dip, and the movie collected only ₹ 48.05 crore rupees. The movie picked up on Saturday with a haul of ₹ 69.80 crore rupees. The movie then collected ₹ 107 crore rupees net on Monday and ₹ 94 crore rupees net on Tuesday, both the highest in Indian cinema history.

Meanwhile, Ramayana entered the elite 500-crore rupees club on Wednesday. The latest update from Sacnilk states that Ramayana collected ₹ 39.67 crore rupees, taking its ticket-window earnings to ₹ 604.27 crore rupees . The movie has seen a dip again but maintained momentum after the Diwali holidays, crossing the ₹ 600 crore rupees mark. It remains to be seen how the movie performs on its second weekend, and is able to improve more to cross the ₹ 700 crore rupees mark.

Notably, Ramayana has now surpassed the lifetime haul of Chhaava , starring Vicky Kaushal and rolled out last year, which stood at ₹ 601.57 crore rupees. Previously, it had crossed lifetime hauls of Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan (which stood at ₹ 544.28 crore rupees) and Ranbir Kapoor's previous theatrical rollout Animal (which stood at ₹ 556.36 crore rupees).

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu and his battle against the asura king Ravana after the latter abducts his wife, Sita.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Game Changers announces The Writer Series; Rajkumar Hirani, Javed Akhtar among featured writers
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Staying behind the scenes, the series is now all set to explore, perhaps, one of the most essential elements in bringing a feature movie to life: the writing. After all, what would a big motion picture or a web series look like if its writing wasn't up to the mark? Be it dissecting some of the most iconic lines, the most heartwarming scenes or the story as a whole, Game Changers with Komal Nahta: The Writer Series will bring together some of the most legendary pens of Indian cinema.

Adding to this, From the likes of Rajkumar Hirani and Abhijat Joshi ( Munna Bhai M.B.B.S., Lage Raho Munna Bhai, 3 Idiots, PK, Sanju, Dunki ) to Javed Akhtar, the series will also feature key names like Niren Bhatt, who is making waves with his writing in the Maddock horror comedy universe ( Bhediya, Munjya, Stree 2 ), and Sriram Raghavan ( Andhaadhun, Badlapur ), among others.

Meanwhile, From Juhi Chaturvedi, who has worked closely with Shoojit Sircar to create memorable scripts like Vicky Donor, Madras Cafe, Piku, October and Gulabo Sitabo , to Rumi Jaffrey, whose screenwriting credits span over three decades, the series will also feature Karan Vyas, who has been making waves with his writing prowess on OTT through projects like Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story, Scoop and Made in India: A Titan Story, among others.

Notably, As has been the case with every edition so far, Komal Nahta will dive deep into engaging conversations with some of the brightest minds in the industry, who form the backbone not just of filmmaking but of the entertainment industry itself.

As per the latest buzz, We are all set and rolling to witness yet another special series that promises a never-before-heard deep dive into the craft of writing, exploring everything from the germ of an idea to its eventual fruition on screen.

title: Samay Raina takes a dig at the box office performance of Toxic in front of Huma Qureshi on India's Got Latent
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Toxic: A Fairytale for Grown-Ups was supposed to be Yash’s grand comeback to the big screen. The Geetu Mohandas movie saw the ‘Rocking Star’ of Kannada cinema return to the silver screen for the first time in four years, following the KGF films. Made on a massive budget with a huge star cast and a grand scale, the movie had everything going for it. But the movie underperformed at the ticket-window and wind up under ₹ 350 crore rupees.

Adding to this, Huma Qureshi was a guest on Samay Raina's India's Got Latent. What Samay told Huma Huma Qureshi played Elizabeth in Toxic. The star was one of the star guests who appeared on Samay Raina 's India's Got Latent. During the episode, Samay did not miss the opportunity to mention Toxic and took a dig at its ticket-window performance. He shared, "Usually people come on India's Got Latent, and then their movie flops. You're the first one to flop a movie and then show up here."

Meanwhile, Huma quipped, "Dude, I just acted in a movie named Toxic, you're literally toxic in life." Samay playfully added, "But at least people watch me." Huma then shared that nowadays there's also hate-watching that gets a high metric these days so no wonder India's Got Latent is on top. Samay giggled and shared the same will apply for Toxic, and recalled watching a lot of sex scenes in the trailer itself. Huma laughed and shared that when Samay calls the guests to come on the show he is very well spoken but during the show he is always spitting out poison!

Notably, Toxic, directed by Geetu Mohandas, also stars Nayanthara , Kiara Advani, Rukmini Vasanth, and Tara Sutaria in the lead roles. The movie was rolled out in theatres on August 26. Toxic has been in the news for its steamy, intimate scenes and sequences that appear to show women in a not-so-favourable light through imagery and dialogue. The movie was cleared by the CBFC with no cuts and an A-rating.

As per the latest buzz, The movie was criticised for its violence, sensual scenes and lack of emotional depth after its rollout. Hindustan Times’ review of Toxic reads, “Yash and Geetu will want you to believe that Toxic is the antithesis of glorifying violent and problematic characters. They want you to believe that this movie is about a man who becomes his own undoing. An anti-hero, or an outright villain, who faces the consequences of his actions. But this moment comes after over 3 heroes of babying, coddling and pandering to the whims of a man.”

title: Dhindora Season 2 trailer out: Bhuvan Bam-led series to premiere on November 20; Sanjeeda Sheikh joins cast, Anup Soni, Udit Narayan and Orry make cameo appearances
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The second season follows Titu Mama as he deals with an Rs 11 crores loss and attempts to mend his relationship with his in-laws. However, his efforts appear to lead to more complications. Alongside Titu Mama, Bhuvan will reprise his roles as Babloo ji, Janki, Sameer and Bancho.

Adding to this, Sanjeeda Sheikh joins the cast as Kavita Mami, a character who is familiar with Titu Mama’s ways. Talking about her role, she shared, “What drew me to Kavita was that she can hold her own with Titu Mama. He’s always got an explanation ready, and she’s usually the one person in the room who can see right through it. I had a lot of fun playing that equation with Bhuvan. Audiences have known Titu Mama for years, and I’m excited for them to finally meet the woman who knows him best.”

Meanwhile, The new season is directed by Sneha Shetty Kohli, who is making her directorial debut with the project. She spoke about expanding the show's setting while retaining its established humour. “One of the most exciting aspects of directing this season was bringing a fresh scale, energy and vibrancy to an already much-loved world. Making my directorial debut with this project made the experience even more special. From bizarre action sequences to colourful song-and-dance moments, every day brought something exciting. Introducing new characters and exploring their dynamics with familiar favourites was equally rewarding. Above all, capturing Bhuvan’s inimitable humour while retaining the essence of this beloved universe was an absolute joy for me.”

Notably, Dhindora Season 2 is written by Bhuvan Bam, Abbas Dalal, Hussain Dalal, Chetan Dange, Gopal Dutt, Shubham Dubey and Anant Dubey. It is produced by Rohit Raj and Bhuvan Bam and will premiere on Netflix on November 20.

title: Anupam Kher explains why Yash's Ravana appears stronger than Ranbir Kapoor's Ram in Ramayana, says makers needed to establish the villain
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Anupam Kher , who lent his voice to Jatayu in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana , of late spoke about the depiction of Ranbir Kapoor's Ram and Yash's Ravana in the movie. When asked why some viewers found Ravana's sequences more engaging than those featuring Ram, the star shared that director Nitesh Tiwari needed to establish the villain in Part 1 of the movie so that the eventual triumph of good over evil in the second part would have a greater impact.

Adding to this, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana. ‘Nitesh needed to establish the villain’ He told The Hollywood Reporter India, "I believe Nitesh knew from the beginning that he was making the movie in two parts. It wasn’t an accidental decision. He needed to establish the villain as someone much bigger, so that the triumph of good over evil in the second part would feel much larger. Once you establish the villain, you understand the scale of what has to be overcome. From Sholay to Karma, Hindi films always establish how frightening and powerful the villain is. So when the hero finally defeats him, you feel a high. I think that’s the strategy here."

Meanwhile, Anupam also disagreed with the suggestion that Ravana was more interesting than Ram in the movie. He explained that Ravana's larger-than-life portrayal worked because of the character of Ram and the journey that would unfold in the remaining story.

Notably, He shared, "No, I don’t think so. Instead, I think Ravana is interesting because Ram is interesting. Ravana feels larger than life and dramatic, but Ram is different. Ram shows himself through various sequences that will come in the rest of the story. He will kill Vali, he will confront Meghnad. We’re too impatient to understand the whole thing at once. In this part, when you see the scene between Jatayu and Ram, and watch Ram break down, that's when people are moved by his humanity. Nobody knows this movie better than Namit Malhotra and Nitesh Tiwari. There are people who spend their life criticising things. There are cynics, and then there are people who actually do things."

As per the latest buzz, During the same interaction, Anupam also opened up about his experience of dubbing for Jatayu. He opened up that the movie's producer, Namit Malhotra, had approached him for the role. The star recalled postponing his dubbing session by a day after the makers showed him a nine-minute clip from the movie. He was so overwhelmed by what he saw that he felt he wasn't prepared to record his lines immediately. Anupam further opened up that he spent around five to six hours dubbing just 10-12 lines of dialogue for Jatayu.

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotraand Yash, Ramayana features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The first part of the movie was rolled out on November 5, while the second part is expected to arrive in 2028.

title: Farah Khan says Faisal Shaikh aka Faisu directed his own reception ceremony, brought wife Tanya to click pictures with guests
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Social media star Faisal Shaikh, popularly known as Mr Faisu, revealed his wedding to Tanya, last month. The newlyweds shared dreamy pictures from the nikah ceremony in Madinah, Saudi Arabia, on Instagram. Later, they also held a reception in Mumbai, which was attended by Farah Khan . Both Faisu and Tanya appeared in the latest episode of Farah's YouTube channel, where they spoke about their marriage.

Adding to this, Farah Khan met Mr Faisu and his wife Tanya. What Farah shared Farah spoke to the two and shared that she had the best time at their reception. She added, “Faisu was directing the whole reception. Just like a director who takes a mic and speaks, he told everyone to stand at their places and all the A-list guests were there with their glasses. We first took pictures, who knows if there would be time later on! Then Faisu told everyone to join them and then revealed to dim the lights! He was the director and star!”

Meanwhile, Faisu giggled and added that he did the same amount of detailing when he got married in Madinah. Faisu also added that he learnt a lot from watching Farah direct everything when she visited his house for a previous vlog. Faisu shared that he was motivated after seeing her dedication and wanted to do something similar with his own vlogs.

Notably, Last month, Faisu had shared photographs from his wedding day to express gratitude for being able to get married in the holy city. Faisu wrote in the caption, “And We created you in pairs” (Quran 78:8) Alhamdulillah for a dream turned into reality. Nikah in the beautiful city of Madinah, with my entire family by my side. A blessing beyond words.”

As per the latest buzz, He further sought blessings and prayers as he embarked on this new chapter of his life, adding, “Please keep us in your duas as we begin this beautiful journey together. May Allah bless our marriage with endless love and barakah. Ameen.”

In further updates, Faisu rose to fame through short video platforms, and established himself as one of India's popular digital creators. He expanded his presence through music videos and television appearances, including his stint on Khatron Ke Khiladi 12.

On top of that, Farah Khan's YouTube channel currently has over 3 million followers. In her vlogs, Farah visits the homes of celebrities to cook new dishes with them in their kitchens, gives viewers a tour of their homes, and indulges in fun conversations over food. Her quirky banter with her cook Dilip has become the highlight of the videos, helping him rise to social media fame. In one of the vlogs, the filmmaker also admitted to having increased Dilip’s salary since they began their YouTube journey.

Farah made her directorial debut with Main Hoon Na in 2004. It starred Shah Rukh Khan and Sushmita Sen. She then directed Om Shanti Om with Shah Rukh Khan, and Tees Maar Khan with Akshay Kumar. Her last directorial was Happy New Year, which rolled out in 2014.

title: Parivarik ManuRanjan review: Pankaj Tripathi, Aditi Rao Hydari's slice of life film is too run-of-the-mill to leave an impact
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Can merely casting talented actors save a weak movie? Not really. And Parivarik ManuRanjan is proof.

Adding to this, After all, in a small town, a single man and a woman living under the same roof are enough to set tongues wagging. Both insist there is nothing between them, even as Ranjan finds himself falling for her. But Helen has a past of her own. What happens to their budding romance when the truth comes out?

Meanwhile, The movie, written by Brijendra Kala, Varun V Sharma, and Ali Abbas Zafar , starts off breezily enough, aided by Tripathi's trademark dry wit and comic timing. In fact, he is perhaps the only engaging aspect of the movie. There is a charm to the way he plays Ranjan, a man who has spent so much time fulfilling his responsibilities that he has forgotten what it means to have a life of his own. The star, however, has played variations of this character many times before, making it difficult to find anything fresh here. Aditi Rao Hydari brings a certain cuteness to Helen, and the sequences involving the two discovering their feelings for each other have some sweetness.

Notably, Unfortunately, the movie soon runs out of steam. The small town comedy genre desperately needs to move beyond its collection of quirky characters. Sunita Rajwar for instance plays the kind of neighborhood nosy aunty we have seen countless times before, poking her nose into other people's lives. Her character also makes vlogs for her grand follower count of nine, which the makers try to turn into a plot progression point later. Instead of being amusing, it becomes exasperating.
As per the latest buzz, Mukesh Tiwari is here as an antagonist, while no prizes for guessing what role Brijendra Kala plays. Yep- a friend/co worker of the lead who exists for some comic relief.

In further updates, The screenplay also struggles to give its central romance enough emotional depth. While the premise has the potential to explore loneliness and companionship, these ideas remain superficial. The movie hints at the sacrifices Ranjan has made for his family and the possibility of finally putting himself first, but never digs deep enough. Similarly, Helen's backstory could have added an interesting emotional dimension to the narrative, but the treatment lacks the impact required to make it truly impactful.
On top of that, Also, there's the song Chhaap Tilak (which has only been used a million times before in films) inserted for no good reason here. The music by Shamir Tandon is okay.

Overall, what should have been a charming, funny drama instead becomes a familiar collection of situations that rarely surprise. There are moments when Tripathi's performance manages to make you chuckle, but even his talent cannot compensate for a screenplay that struggles to find its footing.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Believing that a child's abilities should not be judged by their family background, the principal gives Raghu an opportunity to study alongside children from privileged families. Through this story, the movie explores the importance of providing every child with equal opportunities and the freedom to pursue their dreams.

Adding to this, Talking about what attracted him to the project, Suniel Shetty shared, "Nanhey Dil is a movie about children, about giving equal opportunities to everybody and how important it is for us to make sure everybody is comfortable. It has a beautiful message and could definitely be an eye-opener for modern-day parents. I think this generation believes in equality, and that you have to live your dream and not live the dream of your parents. I'd want my children to live their dream, not mine. I think today's parents are all about honesty, and taking care of their parents and children. So hats off to this generation. I took this movie on because it was a simple story to tell and I am glad that such stories are being heard and are finding global platforms."
Meanwhile, A post shared by Swarupraj medara (@swarupraj_medara)

Notably, Shot over 37 days, the movie is titled Fly High Little Hearts for international audiences. title: Aditi Rao Hydari reveals the family tradition she shares with husband Siddharth: “It's common that everyone laughs together”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Talking about one tradition that is common to both families, Aditi opened up that they believe in finding reasons to laugh together, regardless of the circumstances. She shared, “I think in our family, with Siddharth and in his family as well, it's common that everyone laughs together. No matter what happens, to find something to laugh about, I like that a lot.”

Adding to this, The star further explained that maintaining a sense of humour becomes particularly important when families go through challenging situations. According to her, being able to find something positive even during difficult moments can help people stay connected. Elaborating on this, she added, “Sometimes, if something is difficult, or if there's a problem in the family, no matter what happens, at the end of the day, to be able to find something to smile about, something to laugh about.”

Meanwhile, Aditi also spoke about the role food plays in bringing people together. Agreeing with a thought shared by Pankaj Tripathi, she highlighted how sitting down for a meal and sharing food can create a sense of belonging, even among people who are not related by blood. She shared, “I heard this from someone else as well, that eating together, the food that people sit together and share, whether it's your team or a family of blood, it becomes a family. Very true. So, that eating and sharing food is very, very important.”

Notably, Through her observations, Aditi emphasised that family bonds are often strengthened through small, everyday gestures. For her, laughing together during difficult times and making time to share meals are among the simple ways people can build meaningful relationships. Her thoughts also reflect how family extends beyond blood relations and is shaped by shared experiences, affection and companionship.

As per the latest buzz, Meanwhile, Aditi will next be seen in Parivarik ManuRanjan , which premiered on SonyLIV from today November 13. Directed by Varun V Sharma, the movie also features Pankaj Tripathi, Sunita Rajwar, Brijendra Kala and Mukesh Tiwari in key roles.

title: Dhurandhar and Ramayana to feature at IFFI leading Indian Panorama, BRICS segments
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Indian Panorama section of the 57th edition of the International Movie Festival of India will open with the popular Bollywood movie Dhurandhar , while the special focus on films from BRICS countries will open with the of late rolled out Indian movie Ramayana .

Adding to this, Ranveer Singh in a still from Dhurandhar (left); Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in Ramayana (right). Addressing a press conference, NFDC Managing Director, NFDC Dhiraj Singh shared that the programming committee and juries selected the films to lead their respective sections. “Dhurandhar will be the opening movie of the Indian Panorama’s feature movie section and ‘Becoming’ (a Ladakhi movie), will open the non feature movie section,” Singh shared.

Meanwhile, The Indian Panorama Section is one of IFFI’s flagship sections and includes the best of Indian cinema, with a special focus on films outside the mainstream and from regional languages and cultures otherwise hidden from the mainstream.
Notably, The section includes 25 feature length films and 20 non-feature films.
As per the latest buzz, According to Ashutosh Gowarikar who has been appointed festival director, this year’s festival will be held on the theme: ‘Stories without borders.’

In further updates, “Borders today are not only lines on a map, they are also habits. A story is one of the few things that can cross such a line without a passport. The distance shrinks. That is what cinema does best and that is the thought behind our theme. Today, it has become very easy to stay within our circle, our language, our own screen and our own point of view,” Gowarikar shared.

On top of that, The festival, which runs from November 20 to 28, begins with Fatherland, a 2026 Polish language biographical movie directed by Paweł Pawlikowski and will conclude with We are all Strangers from Singapore.
The festival received 1900 entries from 137 countries for selection and will ultimately showcase 159 international films from a total of 87 countries and 76 Indian films in 18 different languages.

title: Pankaj Tripathi calls out Hindi films for promoting chest-thumping masculinity, says 'alpha male' needs to be woke | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Pankaj Tripathi is in his romantic hero era. The star is turning over a new leaf with Parivarik Manuranjan, a romantic comedy opposite Aditi Rao Hydari . The movie, which rolled out on SonyLiv today (November 13), sees Pankaj play a small-town loner with a difference. In a conversation with Hindustan Times, the National Award-winning star spoke about the movie, doing ‘ordinary’ films and how cinema has changed the definition of alpha male.

Adding to this, Pankaj Tripathi talks about his new movie Parivarik Manuranjan. ‘Nobody wants to make an ordinary story’ Pankaj says he decided to do the movie immediately after reading the script. “I received the script at night, read it at night, and called them (the makers) first thing in the morning saying I’m doing it, because I had no doubts about it,” he tells us.

Meanwhile, Talking about what compelled him to sign the movie, he adds, “I felt it's the kind of story I think about—very close to real life, slice-of-life—and without any gimmicks or screenplay show-offs trying to shock the audience. It’s simple, ordinary storytelling. I call it ordinary because nobody wants to make an ordinary story nowadays; everyone wants to make something extraordinary.”

Notably, The star says that the entry of gimmicks into storytelling has made such simple films rarer today. “It's not that simple films don't come at all now, but they come very rarely. They don't get marketed well, and they are very rare because the medium of storytelling has changed. Gimmicks have entered; everyone wants shock value,” he argues.

As per the latest buzz, In Parivarik Manuranjan, Pankaj plays Ranjan Dubey, a middle-aged bachelor whose life transforms for the better when a beautiful housekeeper enters it. The romantic comedy explores their unconventional love story. Pankaj says that he likes his character, but portraying him posed a rather unusual challenge.

In further updates, “The way Ranjan Dubey reacts, his thoughts match mine. I think the same way. I thought, great, I don't have to act in this! Now, our thoughts are aligning. But in fact, that becomes even more risky. When you have to act like who you already are, it makes you anxious. Because that doesn't usually happen in the world. People keep what they really are hidden inside. So when a character matches your own thoughts, delivering it becomes even more challenging,” the veteran star says.

On top of that, The movie marks a rare occasion when the 50-year-old is romancing on screen. But he shared he never aspired to be a ‘romantic hero’. He explains, “No, I didn't have a craving to become a typical romantic hero. The romance in this movie is of a different kind, not like traditional films. It's not the over-the-top romance we usually see in cinema.”

The movie’s trailer features a line of dialogue that has intrigued audiences: Pankaj’s character says he has had enough of being the beta, and now it’s time to be alpha. The line, in Hindi, includes wordplay on the word beta (son) and also takes a dig at the alpha-male stereotype in mainstream Hindi cinema. Talking about his idea of an alpha male, the star says it has to be ‘someone who is a leader, without chest-thumping masculinity’.

title: Mahesh Manjrekar says Nana Patekar suffered for no reason because of Tanushree Dutta row, says people on set told him nothing had happened
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and filmmaker Mahesh Manjrekar of late remembered his late friend and star Nana Patekar . The filmmaker expressed regret over not being able to meet Nana one last time before his death on October 8. He also revisited the Tanushree Dutta row involving the late star, claiming that it was brought back into the spotlight without any reason.

Adding to this, Mahesh Manjrekar opened up on Nana Patekar's death. 'The row was highlighted for no reason' In conversation with News18 Marathi, Mahesh shared he was familiar with everyone who was present on the sets of the movie Horn Ok Pleassss and knew what had transpired during the shoot. He claimed that the row was unnecessarily highlighted. He shared, "Some people are like that. Even if everyone supports them and one person doesn't, they will not like it. It is okay. But then they bring up an old matter. I know what happened that day. Everyone on the set was known to me, and I also know who was present there. It was highlighted for no reason."

Meanwhile, Mahesh further claimed that he had spoken to people who were present on the sets and that they had told him nothing had happened. He expressed sadness over the impact the row had on Nana. He shared, "Everyone I knew on the sets had told me that nothing had happened. Nothing at all had happened. Nana suffered a lot for no reason. One should ignore such things. But because of social media, everybody has their own opinion, and there is no cure for this."

Notably, In 2018, Tanushree Dutta accused Nana Patekar of sexual harassment and inappropriate behaviour on the sets of the 2008 movie Horn Ok Pleassss. She alleged that the star touched her inappropriately while shooting a song sequence in March 2008. She further claimed that her car was attacked by a mob when she tried to leave the shooting location.

As per the latest buzz, The allegations resurfaced in September 2018, when Tanushree spoke about the incident in an interview, helping trigger India's #MeToo movement in the entertainment industry. In October 2018, she filed an FIR against Nana, Ganesh, Rakesh and Samee. Nana consistently denied the allegations.In June 2019, Mumbai Police filed a B-summary closure report, citing insufficient evidence to support Tanushree's allegations.
In further updates, After Nana's death, Tanushree again spoke about the row and shared videos on social media, bringing the allegations back into public discussion.

On top of that, Veteran star Nana Patekar died on October 8, 2026, at the age of 75. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him with CPR for around 45 minutes but could not save him. He passed away at a hospital in Goa. His postmortem report later verified that he died of a heart attack.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Actors who played lead roles in Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, including Sunil Lahri and Dipika Chikhlia , have been vocal about their views on Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana ever since the movie was revealed. From commenting on the casting of Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi to questioning the costumes and creative liberties, the actors have reacted to different aspects of the movie. Now, writer and lyricist Varun Grover has reacted to the original show's cast commenting on Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's movie, calling out what he described as their 'entitlement'.

Adding to this, Dipika Chikhlia and Sunil Lahri have shared their review of Ramayana. Varun Grover calls out 'entitlement' of Ramayan's cast Taking to X (formerly Twitter), Varun called out the entitlement of the actors from the television show while commenting on the new movie. He wrote, "Actors from Ramanand Sagar’s Ramayana commenting on the new movie with the entitlement as if they are actual avatars."

Meanwhile, In an earlier conversation with Variety India in July, ahead of the movie's rollout, Dipika Chikhlia, who played Sita in Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, had questioned Sai Pallavi's casting in the role. While praising the star's talent, she shared she was unsure how she would look as Sita.

Notably, She also spoke about how the popularity of the legendary television show could weigh heavily on the movie. She shared, “I have seen her work. She’s a phenomenal star. But I don’t know how she’ll look like Sita. Once we see her, we’ll know. Sitaji with curly hair is not mentioned in Ramayan. I think our Ramayan will weigh very heavily on the Ramayana movie. Our Ramayan was also watched by the new generation when it aired on Doordarshan during the pandemic. So, it’s very difficult to erase that.”

As per the latest buzz, However, more of late, while in conversation with paparazzi, Dipika lauded the movie and shared she had predicted its success. Reacting to its box-office performance, she shared, “See, I told you right that the movie is well-made and is bound to be a hit. It has so many big stars. See how it crossed 900-1000 crore rupees in just 4-5 days. Superb. The movie is good, and so many big stars and VFX, all of it is so beautiful.”

In further updates, Sunil Lahri, who played Lakshman in Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, of late shared a video review of Ramayana, offering a mixed reaction. While he lauded the movie's VFX, visuals and performances, he shared it lacked the devotional sentiment and divinity associated with the epic.

On top of that, The star also pointed out certain sequences that he felt could have been handled better, including the Parashurama episode. He shared the Ahalya episode was missing and questioned the way Shurpanakha and Sita address Lord Ram in the movie.

He shared, "I did not like the way Shurpanakha addresses Lord Ram during their conversation. The way Sita Ji addresses Lord Ram also did not feel appropriate to me. There are several other sequences that I felt were weak and lacked the devotional sentiment and divine essence that are integral to the story of the Ramayana.”

title: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana is a hit in all countries where the epic is ‘history’; sets records in Indonesia, Vietnam, Nepal
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana has been a roaring success at the ticket-window in its opening week. After a subpar start for a movie of its scale, Ramayana took off in the post-Diwali break in India, soaring to ₹ 1000 crore rupees in eight days. However, while the performance in India was always expected to be big, Ramayana has hit it out of the park in many Asian territories where the epic is part of culture and history.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor is portraying Ram in the movie Ramayana The Ramayana originated in India, with Valmiki ’s version being the most popular and among the first to descend from the original oral traditions. But worldwide, there are 300 versions of the epic, including localised versions in parts of Southeast Asia and Sri Lanka. Valmiki’s Ramayana and Tulsidas’ Ramcharitmanas are also popular in Hindu-majority Nepal. In all these countries, the new movie adaptation has taken a record start.

Meanwhile, The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash -starrer had its premiere in Indonesia on November 11, six days after its worldwide rollout. According to local trackers, the movie minted $100k (just under ₹ 1 crore rupees) through its premiere, the best start for an Indian movie in the country. title: Johnny Walker found happiness beyond fame: son Nasirr Khan
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai, For legendary star Johnny Walker, fame was just a milestone, never the destination as his priorities in life were to lead a simple and quiet life surrounded by family and friends, says son Nasirr Khan.

Adding to this, Johnny Walker found happiness beyond fame: son Nasirr Khan Remembering his father in the week of his 100th birth anniversary, Nasirr shared his father loved to lead a simple life away from showbiz.
Meanwhile, Johnny Walker was born as Badruddin Jamaluddin Kazi on November 11, 1926.

Notably, "He led an ordinary life despite his achievements. You won't find any controversies or negativity, affairs, ruckus or anything like that. If you look for interviews and information, you will find very little because he was just a private person. If he is still being remembered, it is a great achievement," Nasirr, who is also an star, told PTI in an interview.

As per the latest buzz, Walker, who started life as a bus conductor and even sold vegetables and ice-cream before finding his footing in the movie industry with Guru Dutt's 1951 movie "Baazi", was a gentle father who ensured that all his children are educated well.
In further updates, A teetotaler in real life, Johnny Walker was rechristened after a famous whisky brand by Guru Dutt because of his convincing acting as a drunkard.

On top of that, He gained popularity for his comic roles, and went on to feature in over 300 films. Despite being typecast as a hapless drunkard, he enjoyed a successful career spanning the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

Some of his popular films are "Pyaasa", "Mr. & Mrs. 55", "CID", "Aar-Paar", "Taxi Driver", "Madhumati", "Chaudhvin Ka Chand", "Anand", "Devdas", "Pratigya", and "Raja Jani", among others. He made his final screen appearance in Kamal Haasan's "Chachi 420" , playing an inebriated make-up artist.

title: Student of the Year After Dark director Reema Maya defends show amid comparisons with Class, calls it an original take
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Karan Johar's Student of the Year franchise has long been synonymous with campus romances and youthful drama. However, it has now undergone a makeover, with Student of the Year: After Dark turning the familiar campus setting into the backdrop for a murder mystery. Ever since the series' trailer was rolled out, it has drawn comparisons with the Netflix show Class. Now, in an interview with Times Now, the series' director, Reema Maya , has reacted to the comparisons.

Adding to this, Reema Maya reacts to comparisons between Student of the Year: After Dark and Class. Reema Maya says Student of the Year: After Dark is an original show Reema shared, “Class is a wonderful show, and Ashim Ahluwalia is an amazing filmmaker. There are certain genres that have certain expectations. If you are making a young adult murder mystery, there will be a murder, there will be a high school, there will be teenage characters and interpersonal dynamics. That is the expectation of the genre.”

Meanwhile, She further described the series as an original take on the genre, saying, “One must understand the difference between something being derivative and something belonging to the genre. This is a young adult murder mystery and competition series. So, the fun of all those genres we have tried to bring on the table and say it in our original and unique way.”

Notably, Class is a 2023 Indian teen crime drama on Netflix, directed by Ashim Ahluwalia. An adaptation of the popular Spanish series Elite, the eight-episode show is set at Delhi's prestigious Hampton International School, where three students from modest backgrounds receive scholarships and navigate a world of privilege, wealth, and discrimination. Starring Gurfateh Pirzada, Piyush Khati, Anjali Sivaraman, Ayesha Kanga and Madhyama Segal, the show offers a dark and unfiltered look at the lives of privileged teenagers and the inequalities that exist beyond the walls of their elite school.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Reema Maya, the series stars Shanaya Kapoor in a double role, alongside Abhinav Singh, Divik Sharma, Manya Grover, Deeya Damani, Adi Malik, Sheeba Chaddha and Vivek Gomber. The trailer shows Shanaya entering the cutthroat Student of the Year competition to find the killer of her twin sister. As she investigates, she must also navigate competition and betrayal.

In further updates, In an interview with Hindustan Times, director Reema Maya , who has a knack for making thrillers and horror, adds that there was no pushback from Karan when she told him about her vision for the show. “There was none (pushback); only excitement and encouragement,” she shared, adding that KJo told her to ‘just push it and have fun’.

On top of that, Reema shared she was both surprised and honoured for being chosen to reimagine a franchise that Karan himself started: “I’m very honoured that Karan sir decided to put his faith and trust in my voice and my vision. He allowed me to reimagine a franchise that is so close to his heart.”

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 8: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's juggernaut sails past ₹1000 crore; outpaces RRR, KGF 2, Jawan
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana may have lost the festive momentum at the ticket-window, but the movie refuses to slow down even on weekdays. On Thursday, its final day during its extended week, the movie again crossed ₹ 50 crore rupees net in India and barely missed the ₹ 100-crore rupees mark worldwide. It did, however, cross the ₹ 1000 crore rupees mark at the global ticket-window.

Adding to this, Ramayana stars Yash as Ravana alongside Ranbir Kapoor as Rama. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash -starrer had seven consecutive days where it grossed over ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide. That run came to an end on Thursday. But by no means was the day disappointing for the movie. Ramayana collected a staggering ₹ 53.50 crore rupees in net ticket-window in India on the day. The movie set new records for the best Monday and Tuesday in Indian cinema history earlier this week, before closing out the week strongly as well. After eight days, Ramayana’s domestic haul now stands at ₹ 564 crore rupees net ( ₹ 675 crore rupees gross).

Meanwhile, The issue with Ramayana was its overseas earnings. Sony Pictures distributed the movie internationally, giving it a rollout in 59,000 screens worldwide, almost six times the size of any big Indian rollout. But the opening weekend saw returns of less than $25 million. But here, too, the tide turned after Monday as the movie maximised its earnings on weekdays. As of now, Ramayana has collected $38 million in the overseas markets. This takes the movie’s worldwide gross to ₹ 1033 crore rupees after eight days. On Thursday, Ramayana became the 11th Indian movie to enter the 1000-crore rupees club and the third-fastest overall.

Notably, Ramayana reached ₹ 1000 crore rupees in just eight days. This is bettered only by Pushpa 2: The Rule and Dhurandhar: The Revenge, both of which reached the mark in seven days. Ramayana beat the pace set by Baahubali 2 (10 days), RRR (16 days) and KGF Chapter 2 (18 days). It was also way ahead of the pace of Shah Rukh Khan’s two 1000-crore rupees hits - Jawan (18 days) and Pathaan (27 days).

As per the latest buzz, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part is running in theatres, while the second part is set for a Diwali 2028 rollout.

title: 200 shows added for Pyre after row, director Vinod Kapri thanks audience for ‘standing by little film’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Pyre is back, exclaimed director Vinod Kapri , as he opened up that the critically acclaimed independent movie is seeing a revival of shows. Pyre is as per reports adding 200 shows in theatres across India from today (November 13). This comes after a huge row over a 75-80% reduction in the movie's shows following the rollout of Ramayana.

Adding to this, Vinod Kapri's Pyre features Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, both first-time actors from Uttarakhand. Pyre gets 200 additional shows On Thursday, Vinod Kapri took to social media to express his gratitude to the audience for the love and appreciation towards his independent movie, which led to the addition of the screens. “PYRE IS GETTING ITS SHOWS BACK! Over 200 shows of PYRE are being added from Friday, 13th November. A heartfelt thank you to our audiences for standing by this little independent movie and making this possible. Your love, trust and support have brought us back to more screens,” he wrote.

Meanwhile, The filmmaker also thanked exhibitors and cinema chains for backing the movie. He added, “A big thank you to @IndiaCinepolisand @_PVRCinemas for supporting PYRE and giving more audiences an opportunity to experience Amma and Bubu’s story. This journey belongs to all of you.”

Notably, Pyre rolled out two weeks ago to critical acclaim. The independent movie was initially screened in 400 screens, but the number dropped to below 100 after Ramayana , the big-budget Hindi movie rolled out last week. Director Kapri alleged that theatres removed his movie despite houseful shows and appealed for fairness. His demand was backed by the All India Cine Workers Association, which wrote to the Information and Broadcasting Minister for intervention.

As per the latest buzz, Set in the Kumaon Himalayas, the movie follows Padam Singh and Tulsi, an ageing couple who live together while waiting for their children, who have moved away in search of better opportunities.

title: Lara Dutta defends Sai Pallavi's warrior Sita in Ramayana amid backlash, asks critics to stop being ‘small-minded’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana has been making waves at the ticket-window ever since its rollout on November 5. However, Sita's portrayal as a warrior who fights demons in the movie has raised eyebrows and drawn criticism from a section of viewers. Now, Lara Dutta , who essays the role of Kaikeyi in the movie, has defended the portrayal and urged people not to be small-minded.

Adding to this, Lara Dutta reacts to backlash over Sai Pallavi's warrior Sita in Ramayana. Lara Dutta defends Sai Pallavi's warrior Sita in Ramayana In an interview with NDTV, Lara defended Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita as a warrior amid the backlash, insisting that audiences should simply enjoy the cinematic experience. She pointed out that there are several versions of the Ramayana. She also noted that, considering the cultural practices of those times, boys and girls born into royal families were trained in both the arts and the use of weapons.

Meanwhile, She added, “So when you look at things like that, there are so many possibilities of what could have happened, should have happened, whatever. So I think it's not that far off or it's not that far-fetched to think that Sita was also possibly very much trained in the art of warfare. And especially, I mean, I just say that when you're put into a situation like that also as a woman, you're not going to be a helpless woman.”

Notably, Lara further shared that a character like Sita, who chooses to spend 14 years in exile in the forest, would also have to be resilient. “At some point, she will pick up something to defend herself. You have to stop being so small-minded, you know, and also embrace the cinematic experience,” she shared.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana shows Sita wielding a sword and fighting demons alongside Lord Rama. She is also shown training children and local youths in combat. The portrayal of Sita as a warrior in Nitesh Tiwari's movie sparked a debate among viewers, with some questioning the creative liberties taken with a character deeply rooted in religious beliefs and mythology. However, the makers had earlier opened up that they had drawn inspiration for Sita's portrayal as a warrior from the Adbhuta Ramayana.

In further updates, The Adbhuta Ramayana depicts Sita's fierce and divine aspect, in which she assumes a powerful form, often associated with Goddess Kali, to defeat Sahasra Ravana, a thousand-headed demon. On the other hand, Indian audiences have largely grown up watching adaptations of Valmiki's Ramayana, including Ramanand Sagar's television series Ramayan.

On top of that, Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari and backed by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The movie has crossed the ₹ 1,000-crore rupees mark worldwide within its first week. Made on a massive budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees, the movie is scheduled to rollout in two parts, with the second instalment set to arrive in 2028.

title: Sai Pallavi recalls crying on Ramayana sets after dialect coach touched her feet
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Playing mythological characters on the big screen comes with its own set of challenges, especially when the character is widely revered. In a recent interaction, Sai Pallavi , who plays Goddess Sita in Ramayana , spoke about an emotional moment on the movie's sets. She recalled how she broke down after her dialect coach touched her feet following a scene in which she portrayed Sita.

Adding to this, Sai Pallavi recalls get overwhelmed on Ramayana sets. 'Was a bit overwhelmed when my dialect coach touched my feet' In a conversation with content creator Pallavi Raj, Sai Pallavi opened up about a moment that left her feeling “a bit overwhelmed” while shooting the movie.

Meanwhile, “The moment when I was a bit overwhelmed was when my dialect coach, she actually touched my feet after a scene, and I was taken aback because she saw me making phone calls, getting ready and all of that. She (the dialect coach) knows I am Sai Pallavi, but sometimes when you play a character that you worship every day, when you have a connection with it like your mother, and when somebody embodies it, you do not care about whether that's an star or any other human being. You just want that love.”

Notably, She added, “So when she did that, even before she started to cry, I started to cry. I shared, 'What are you even doing?' So it's just that moment made me feel the character speaks so much more to so many people. I was very humbled and overwhelmed to experience that amount of love.”

As per the latest buzz, Earlier, during her appearance on Kaun Banega Crorepati with Ravi Dubey and Ranbir Kapoor, Sai spoke about playing the role of Maa Sita. She shared, “I didn’t want to use my head this time. Every time when I play a character, I think what can I give to that character, but this was the first time when I thought - 'What can I get for playing a role like that of Sita Maa? Like what knowledge will I gain from this?' So, I wanted to keep the process transparent. I didn’t want to think anything about it. I prayed to Sita Maa and went forward with it.”

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The movie, produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, has crossed ₹ 1000 crore rupees mark worldwide at the ticket-window.

title: Netflix announces Pushpak Vimaan: Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee, and Barun Sobti headline Sudip Sharma’s new crime comedy
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:
The Kohrra creator reunites with Netflix for a genre-bending series that marks his departure from intense crime dramas and ventures into comedy.

Adding to this, Co-created and written by Sudip Sharma and Abhishek Banerjee, Pushpak Vimaan is produced by Movie Squad Productions LLP. The series revolves around a crime caper in which humour emerges from an eclectic mix of characters and a chain of events that gradually spirals beyond everyone's control.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the project, creator and director Sudip Sharma shared, “With Pushpak Vimaan, I wanted to explore a very different creative space. It is a crime caper, but one in which the humour comes from the characters, their circumstances and the sheer unpredictability of the situations they find themselves in. Netflix is where I choose to experiment, and it was the natural home for a story of this nature. It provided the space to explore the genre freely and to bring this unusual ensemble of characters to life.”

Notably, Tanya Bami, Series Head, Netflix India, also expressed excitement about the collaboration, highlighting the platform's continued association with the filmmaker. She shared, "Pushpak Vimaan is a show we are very excited to announce. Firstly this is our next franchise with Sudip Sharma whose distinct style of combining a compelling story with a deep commentary on society has always found critical as well as audience love. With Pushpak Vimaan, we’re happy to champion Sudip’s creativity once again, this time with a comedy series he wrote, showran and directed and it’s an unputdownable caper. It’s one hell of a fun ride that we can’t wait for our audiences to experience."

As per the latest buzz, Pushpak Vimaan marks the second creative collaboration between Sudip Sharma and Netflix, following their association on Kohrra. With the new series, the filmmaker ventures into a different genre while bringing together three familiar faces from the streaming space.

In further updates, The series is directed by Sudip Sharma, with Sudip Sharma and Abhishek Banerjee credited as its creators and writers. Saurabh Malhotra serves as producer, while Movie Squad Productions LLP is the production house behind the project.
On top of that, Further details about the series, including its rollout date, are awaited.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 8: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film remains steady, crosses ₹560 crore to beat Pathaan, Animal lifetime hauls
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana Part 1 rolled out in theatres on November 5. The Nitesh Tiwari movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana. Even with the Diwali festivities behind it, the movie showed no signs of slowing down at the ticket-window as theatres returned to regular weekday schedules. Ramayana has surpassed the lifetime collection of big-budget blockbusters such as Animal and Pathaan.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in Ramayana. Ramayana ticket-window update Ramayana began with houseful shows on day 1, netting ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net in India on its opening day. The figure was low given the movie’s scale, but it was still the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. But the movie recovered mightily on Monday and Tuesday, when the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer went on to shatter records. The movie collected ₹ 107 crore rupees net on Monday and ₹ 94 crore rupees net on Tuesday, both the highest in Indian cinema history. Before Ramayana, the record for the biggest Monday on a holiday belonged to Salman Khan’s Tiger 3, which collected ₹ 58 crore rupees on its first Monday, the day of Diwali 2023.

Meanwhile, Ramayana entered the elite 500-crore rupees club on Wednesday. The latest update on Sacnilk states that Ramayana collected ₹ 53.55 crore rupees on Thursday, bringing the net earnings to ₹ 564.65 crore rupees . It has now surpassed the lifetime hauls of Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan (which stood at ₹ 544.28 crore rupees) and Ranbir Kapoor's previous theatrical rollout Animal (which stood at ₹ 556.36 crore rupees).

Notably, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi portrays Sita and Yash plays Ravana. The cast also includes Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, with music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu (played by Ranbir Kapoor), and his battle against the asura king Ravana (played by Yash) after the latter abducts his wife, Sita (played by Sai Pallavi). Surpanakha is Ravana's sister. Her insult at the hands of Rama's brother Lakshman leads to the Rama-Ravana war.

Eetha narrates the story of a woman who defied conventions and challenged the odds to chart an unforgettable place in history.

title: Sharad Kelkar says dubbing for Yash's Ravana in Ramayana was difficult because of his 'phenomenal' performance
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Sharad Kelkar , who has been receiving appreciation for dubbing Yash's voice in the Hindi version of Ramayana , of late spoke about his experience working on the movie. Speaking at the trailer launch of Kaali Kheti on Thursday, Sharad thanked the audience for their praise but admitted that dubbing for Yash was a little challenging because of the star's phenomenal performance.

Adding to this, Sharad Kelkar, who dubbed for Yash's Ravana in the Hindi version of Ramayana, lauded the star. 'I must give a compliment to Yash' At the trailer launch, when he was lauded for his dubbing, Sharad smiled and delivered one of Yash's dialogues from the movie, but with his own twist - “Teeno lokon mein sirf ek hi raj hoga, Kelkar raj (There shall be only one rule across the three worlds: the Kelkar rule).”

Meanwhile, He went on to praise Yash for his performance as Ravana, saying, “I must give compliment to Yash. The way he has performed in the movie, I think nobody could have done it. He is such a brilliant star. Jis tarah se unhone kiya hai woh role (The way he has performed that role), I think he is phenomenal. Isliye unko itna appreciation mil raha hai movie ke andar (I think that is why he is getting so much appreciation).”

Notably, Sharad also admitted that dubbing for Yash was not easy, given how well he had performed the role. “Mere ko thodi mushkil hui dub karne mein woh (I had some difficulty doing that), because he was so good in the movie. But, thank you, you all loved the movie, and loved the voice,” he added.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Press Trust of India (PTI) (@ptinews_multimedia)

In further updates, Earlier, while in conversation with IGN, Yash spoke about the pressure of playing Ravana. He shared, “If you know the character and everybody is aware of it, then it becomes challenging. If it's a new movie where you are telling a new story, whatever you do, that will become the character. But if people already have some image about it since so many people have played it in different ways, then it's extra pressure for an star. But I stuck to very simple basics to understand what made him do such kind of things. The intent was important.”

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The movie is co-produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios and DNEG, along with Yash's Monster Mind Creations. On Thursday, the movie crossed ₹ 1,000 crore rupees in worldwide ticket-window collections.

title: Daayra OTT release: Kareena Kapoor and Prithviraj Sukumaaran film to arrive on Netflix in Hindi and Malayalam
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Meghna Gulzar ’s directorial Daayra, which brings together Kareena Kapoor and Malayalam star Prithviraj Sukumaran for the first time, is finally getting its OTT premiere. On Thursday, it was opened up that Daayra will rollout on Netflix.

Adding to this, Daayra stars Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran together for the first time on screen Daayra rollout date Netflix India South took to their X account and shared a new post, revealing the rollout date of Daayra on the platform. Daayra will rollout on Netflix on November 13.

Meanwhile, Daayra will be able to seen on the platform in two languages: Hindi and Malayalam. The movie is about two police officers who find themselves in a moral conflict following a controversial encounter killing linked to a brutal rape and murder case.

Notably, Daayra revolves around Ajooni (Kareena Kapoor), who heads an SIT investigating a police encounter. It involves multiple men accused of gang-raping a young girl and then burning her to death. The encounter was carried out by DCP Raman Kumar ( Prithviraj Sukumaran ) and his team, who claim they all tried to flee during custody. What Ajooni uncovers during the investigation forms the crux of the story.

As per the latest buzz, Hindustan Times’ Rishabh Suri gave the movie 3 stars and wrote, “The first half is deliberate rather than gripping. The subject is important, and what works in the movie’s favour is its willingness to let the investigation breathe. The procedural drama is given room to play out instead of being rushed from one revelation to another. The trade off, however, is that the movie sometimes lacks the urgency one would expect from such a disturbing case. "

In further updates, He added, "The second half picks up pace and moves towards its climax. While the conclusion may not come as a complete surprise, there are enough compelling moments along the way to keep you invested. The movie’s strength lies less in shock value and more in the questions it raises about institutions and accountability.”

On top of that, Kareena addressed the contrast between her role in Daayra and her association with Rohit Shetty's cop universe, where police characters are presented in a larger-than-life commercial setting. “Every director operates in a different universe,” she shared, describing Rohit Shetty's cop universe as “larger-than-life” and Meghna's world as “grounded, realistic, and complex.” “As an star, I feel fortunate to straddle both worlds comfortably,” Kareena told news agency ANI.

title: 'Indra Dev' Kunal Kapoor finds new fan-following in Thailand following cameo in Ramayana, fans write poems for his 'divine beauty'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

It has been a week since Ramayana rolled out worldwide, and already, its cultural impact is visible. The movie, an adaptation of Valmiki’s epic, has found takers not just in India but also overseas. While Westerners are enthralled by its scale and visuals, many in Southeast Asia have been praising the adaptation and the actors. And while there are many scene-stealers like Yash, Ravie Dubey, and Ranbir Kapoor, it is Kunal Kapoor who seems to have struck a chord with followers in Thailand. Kunal, who has a three-scene cameo in the movie, is the new darling of Thai followers, many of whom are flooding his social media with invitations to come to the country.

Adding to this, Kunal Kapoor imagined as Indra Dev in a concept poster for Ramayana by District Movies. Kunal Kapoor in Ramayana Kunal appears as Devraj Indra, the king of devas in Ramayana. He appears in two pivotal battle sequences, first defeating the asura king Sumali, and later getting beaten himself by Ravana after he attains the boon from Lord Brahma. The star then appears in a long sequence where he urges Lord Vishnu to take an avatar to fight Ravana. The cameo was well received, with followers calling his casting perfect. Last year, while speaking with Hindustan Times, Kunal had called the opportunity to work in Ramayana ‘a great honour and pleasure,’ saying he was blown away by the makers’ vision and scale. That scale is visible in his scenes, with his entrance on the flying elephant Airavata, which is called one of the highlights of the movie.

Meanwhile, But even as desi followers are praising Kunal for the cameo and many saying the star is getting due recognition, he has made new followers now, many of them overseas. In Thailand, especially, Kunal has become something of a sensation since the movie’s rollout. Twitter (now X) and Instagram are flooded with posts of Thai viewers sharing his screengrabs and stills from the show.

Notably, One shared BTS shots of Kunal filming his scenes and wrote, “Found him! The golden-skinned one. His beauty is like Indra, descended from heaven to Earth, radiant as the moon, above the land of heaven, above all other men. The Indra of Thai people's dreams.” Another quote tweeted a selfie from the star and wrote in Thai, “Does he know his good looks are a weapon!! One that's just as f***ing powerful as Indra's thunderbolt.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by GENZY CLUB (@genzyclub)

title: Ramayana crosses ₹1000 crore at the box office in 8 days, Ranbir Kapoor, Yash-starrer is the third fastest Indian film to do so
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Barely a week after its rollout in theatres, Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana has entered the 1000-crore rupees club. On Thursday, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer crossed ₹ 1000 crore rupees in worldwide gross on the back of a strong opening weekend, followed by all-time record-setting weekdays. Ramayana is only the third Indian movie to reach the ₹ 1000-crore rupees mark in its opening weekend and also the third fastest to the milestone.

Adding to this, Ramayana rolled out worldwide on November 5. Ramayana’s journey to ₹ 1000 crore rupees Ramayana opened in theatres on November 5, three days before Diwali. It had a good, but not great, start, earning ₹ 128 crore rupees worldwide on its opening day. Positive reviews and early reactions led to positive word of mouth, helping the movie take off overseas. At home, however, the movie was curtailed by the Diwali festivities. Regardless, Ramayana managed ₹ 507 crore rupees in its four-day opening weekend.

Meanwhile, The real mayhem began on Monday as the movie capitalised on the Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj breaks to rack up back-to-back ₹ 150-crore rupees days. Ramayana then continued the trend with an exceptionally strong Wednesday, ending with ₹ 935 crore rupees gross in seven days. The movie finishes its extended eight-day opening week. The movie then added ₹ 29 crore rupees in advance bookings for Thursday in India and about $1.5 million overseas, bringing the haul to around ₹ 980 crore rupees as Thursday began. According to trade estimates, Ramayana had crossed the ₹ 1000 crore rupees mark on the back of Thursday spot bookings by late afternoon, entering the club in its eighth day in theatres.

Notably, Baahubali The Conclusion was the first Indian movie to reach the ₹ 1000 crore rupees mark in May 2017, just over a week after its rollout. Dangal joined it later that month, propelled by its belated rollout in China. Since then, eight other Indian films have grossed over ₹ 1000 crore rupees worldwide, with Ramayana becoming the 11th overall. However, Ramayana is the third-fastest to reach the mark, doing so in eight days.

As per the latest buzz, This is bettered only by Pushpa 2: The Rule and Dhurandhar: The Revenge, both of which reached the mark in seven days. Ramayana beat the pace set by Baahubali 2 (10 days), RRR (16 days) and KGF Chapter 2 (18 days). It was way ahead of the pace of Shah Rukh Khan’s two 1000-crore rupees hits - Jawan (18 days) and Pathaan (27 days).

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part is running in theatres, while the second part is set for a Diwali 2028 rollout.

title: Karan Johar is shocked at actors trying to be box office gurus and demanding alpha characters: 'When are you acting exactly?'
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Filmmaker Karan Johar has raised concerns about what he sees as Bollywood's growing herd mentality, questioning why actors are increasingly keen to involve themselves in every aspect of filmmaking instead of focusing on their performances. In a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter India, the filmmaker shared he has encountered actors who want to have a say in casting, budgets and promotional campaigns, and are more concerned about box-office trends than the characters they are playing.

Adding to this, Karan Johar questions actors for trying to become ticket-window gurus. Karan Johar slams Bollywood's herd mentality When asked if he was worried about the way the movie industry was functioning, Karan shared he was more concerned about the herd mentality among artists. He shared many actors no longer follow their instincts as they once did, choosing instead to conform to what they believe will work at the ticket-window.

Meanwhile, He opened up that he had encountered lead actors questioning their characters during narrations because they were not aggressive, alpha or dominant enough. Citing Shah Rukh Khan's character in Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge as an example, Karan pointed out that Raj was a gentle and passive romantic hero, proving that a successful leading man need not always be aggressive or dominant. He acknowledged the success of films such as Kabir Singh, Animal and Dhurandhar, which feature more aggressive male protagonists, but also highlighted the success of Saiyaara, which had an empathetic romantic hero.

Notably, Karan then questioned why actors were chasing a particular kind of protagonist and asking questions that had little to do with their performances. He shared, "I’ve had actors ask me if the movie has anything deeply rooted. What does that mean? Rooted in what? I hope it’s rooted in a great script. I hope it’s rooted in great content. We are making a Hindi-language movie or an Indian movie which is rooted in the language and the syntax of our cinema. Isn’t that enough? I’m being asked, ‘What is your VFX budget?’ How is that your problem? Will I make a tacky-looking movie because I want to make money off a bad movie? No, I’ll obviously do my best."

As per the latest buzz, He added that he was surprised to see actors wanting to be involved in every aspect of filmmaking, from casting and box-office predictions to promotional campaigns, instead of concentrating on their acting. He shared, "I’m flummoxed with people’s insecurities. Maybe it’s vulnerabilities, but I’m reading them as insecurities. I’m surprised and shocked that they want to do everything but act. They want to become box-office gurus, trade analysts, perception setters, campaign makers, trailer cutters and poster makers. When are you acting exactly?"

In further updates, The filmmaker also admitted that directors and producers were "deeply complicit in the creation of this monstrosity" by giving in to actors' demands to avoid stressful situations and ensure smoother working conditions on sets. Karan added that he valued the opinions of actors such as Shah Rukh Khan and Amitabh Bachchan because of their experience and understanding of the craft, but was not in favour of interference from younger actors.

On top of that, Karan is currently awaiting the rollout of his soon-to-release series, Student of the Year: After Dark. Backed by Dharma Productions, the series stars Shanaya Kapoor in a double role, alongside Divik Sharma, Manya Grover and Mannat Duggal, among others. Directed by Reema Maya, the series is set to premiere on JioHotstar on November 13.
