title: Imtiaz Ali's O Saathi Re starring Aditi Rao Hydari, Avinash Tiwary and Arjun Rampal, to Premiere on Netflix on December 4
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Produced by Imtiaz Ali, Mohit Choudhary and Shibasish Sarkar, O Saathi Re follows layered characters as they navigate the different dimensions of love and relationships. From understanding individual identities and personal desires to examining power dynamics and the difficult process of letting go, the series looks at romance beyond conventional notions of togetherness. At its centre is a relationship in which affection exists, but the balance of love is not necessarily equal.

Adding to this, Speaking about the series, Imtiaz Ali shared, “O Saathi Re is a modern romantic show with a vintage heart. Sometimes, love surprises you by showing itself in the most unexpected corners. This is the story of the growth of affection in a divorcing couple. Affection has a throbbing heart, love is beautiful, but a relationship can be unequal. To be a matched couple can often be a burden. In O Saathi Re, we see that while love is yearning, dreaming, and getting together, it can also be the process of letting go. The characters are multi-layered and lifelike, which is why we went for the highest grade of actors. The cast, headlined by Aditi Rao Hydari, Avinash Tiwary, and Arjun Rampal, negotiates steep curves and sensitive moments in the captainship of Arif Ali, the director. We’ve had a wonderful run of partnership with Netflix with the experiences of She and Amar Singh Chamkila. We couldn’t have conceived this series without them. We present O Saathi Re with love and hope people like it.”

Meanwhile, Tanya Bami, Series Head, Netflix India, also spoke about the soon-to-release show and the platform's plans for the romance genre. She shared, “Romance is such a loved genre and yet so under served in the series format. After Musafir Cafe, we are extremely excited to bring our next offering in the romance genre - Imtiaz Ali's O Saathi Re. The complexity of this romance is what sets it apart as it takes something as familiar as love and sees it through the lens of a dynamic that always exists in a love story, raising a never asked question - is all love truly ever equal?

Notably, Imtiaz has always had a wonderful understanding of people and the emotions that drive them and this love story through his lens of finding the deeper meaning in the everyday is something we can't wait for the audience to discover. After our wonderful partnership with him for Amar Singh Chamkila , there is something very special about seeing him bring his distinct storytelling sensibility to his next long-form series. With an incredible cast comprising Aditi Rao Hydari, Avinash Tiwary and Arjun Rampal, Imtiaz has created a world where every character brings a unique perspective to the story.”

As per the latest buzz, Imtiaz Ali has previously explored different facets of romance and human relationships through films such as Jab We Met, Rockstar, Tamasha, Love Aaj Kal and Main Vaapas Aaunga . With O Saathi Re, he returns to the genre in a long-form series format, bringing his storytelling approach to a narrative centred on modern relationships. Arif Ali directs the series, which aims to explore the emotional complexities of love, affection and separation.

In further updates, The series is written by Imtiaz Ali, Amogh Kanaskar and Nidhi Sethia, with Nidhi Sethia also serving as the creative producer. Vishal Bajaj and Pratik Nandkumar More of Shoot at Site are the executive producers.

title: Kareena Kapoor Khan faces legal notice over Quranic verse on 30-carat emerald pendant worn for Diwali 2026
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The star's festive look featured a silver kaftan paired with a matching turban and the statement emerald pendant. While her outfit and jewellery caught the attention of social media users, the religious inscription on the heirloom soon became a subject of debate. The pendant is associated with the Begums of Bhopal and has as per reports been passed down through Saif Ali Khan's family.

Adding to this, Stylist Rhea Kapoor shared details about Kareena's appearance in a social media post, explaining the history and significance of the pieces she wore. Describing the ensemble, she wrote, "Real movie star, real chandi, real heirlooms and real personal style. Kareena in a pure chandi kaftan and turban by @punit.balana,wearing a 200-year-old kalgi from the Nawab of Bhopal and the Begum of Bhopal’s 30-carat emerald, carved with the Ayat-ul-Kursi. Outfit: @punitbalanaofficial Jewelry: Heirlooms of the Bhopal royal family, Kareena’s own. These pieces come through Saif’s family: his grandmother, Sajida Sultan, was the daughter of the last ruling Nawab of Bhopal."

Meanwhile, However, Abbas Hafeez objected to the use of the Quranic verse as part of a fashion accessory. According to him, the pendant represents the Islamic heritage of the Begums of Bhopal and was commissioned as an expression of religious faith rather than for fashion purposes.

Notably, Clarifying his position, Hafeez shared that his objection was not related to Kareena celebrating Diwali or choosing to wear a particular outfit. He told FPJ, "Let me make it very clear: people are free to celebrate whichever festival they wish and wear whatever clothes they want. Our objection is only to the Quranic verse. Even if she had worn it on Eid, it would still have been objectionable," he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Advocate Mohammad Zafar further explained that the legal notice demands the removal of Kareena's social media photographs. He also shared that if the request is not addressed, further legal remedies could be considered. While the row continues to draw attention, the Hindu Utsav Samiti's support for the star has added another dimension to the debate surrounding her Diwali appearance.

title: Babil Khan reveals getting trolled for being himself doesn't affect him anymore, says he's emotional but not weak
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Babil Khan , son of late star Irrfan Khan , has often found himself at the receiving end of social media trolling for his emotional behaviour, which some people have labelled as 'overacting'. In a recent conversation with Rachit Singh, Babil opened up about being trolled for being himself and opened up that, after six years in the industry, he has learnt to detach himself from the negativity and move on.

Adding to this, Babil Khan on navigating trolling and online negativity. Babil Khan talks about facing a lot for being himself In 2024, Babil faced criticism after a video of him repeatedly apologising to a woman for accidentally photobombing her at an event went widely shared. Some social media users called him 'fake' and 'pretentious'. Talking about the trolling, the star opened up that his reaction to 'stealing' someone's moment on the red carpet was "natural". He admitted that, at the time, his instinct was mixed with self-doubt and that he was aware people might think he was overacting just by looking at him.

Meanwhile, In May 2025, another video of Babil breaking down while talking about Bollywood went widely shared, leading to further criticism. His team later clarified that his comments had been taken out of context and that he was having a difficult day.

Notably, The star opened up that, over his six-year journey as an star, he has learnt to be unapologetic about who he is. Responding to his critics, he shared, "I will be myself. I have faced a lot for being myself, but finally I don't care. It still hurts, but that power of hurt is very little. I still wear my heart on my sleeves. I can just understand my relationship with the hurt, have a detachment from the experience, and move forward."

As per the latest buzz, During a rapid-fire round, Babil also spoke about how people often mistake his emotional nature for weakness. He shared that people assume he is 'weak' and does not have the strength to endure difficult situations because he is emotional, but that is not the case.

In further updates, Babil began his career as a camera assistant before making his acting debut. He worked as a camera assistant on his father Irrfan Khan's movie Qarib Qarib Singlle. He eventually made his acting debut in 2022 with Qala, alongside Triptii Dimri and Swastika Mukherjee. The movie received positive reviews from critics.

On top of that, He followed it up with a performance in the series The Railway Men (2023), which collected him praise. In the same year, he also featured in the coming-of-age comedy Friday Night Plan, alongside Juhi Chawla. In 2025, he appeared in the movie Logout, after which he took a break and stepped away from the spotlight and social media.

In October 2025, Babil returned to social media, and in May 2026, he resumed work on an soon-to-release project. Details of the project are yet to be revealed. While he has verified that he is working on a series without sharing further details, he is also as per reports preparing to make his debut in South Indian cinema with a movie by Babu Janardhanan. However, the star is yet to confirm the news.

title: SHOCKING: Amitabh Bachchan's Jalsa at centre of family DISPUTE; sister-in-law Ramola challenges gift deed transferring iconic bungalow to Jaya Bachchan
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramola, the wife of Amitabh's brother Ajitabh Bachchan, has as per reports filed multiple complaints with registration authorities over the past seven months. She claims that she was neither aware of nor had consented to the transaction. The matter is currently under examination by the authorities.

Adding to this, As per Mumbai Mirror, Jalsa was originally recorded in Ramola's name before being transferred to Jaya's name. The dispute resurfaced following alleged attempts to remove Ramola's name from the government's Property Card and replace it with Jaya's. Interestingly, while records of Kapol Housing Society as per reports show Jaya as the owner, the Property Card continues to carry Ramola's name.

Meanwhile, The report further states that questions have been raised about the manner in which the 1993 gift deed was executed. According to the complaints, the document was prepared on plain paper without stamp duty being paid at the time and allegedly did not have witnesses. Ramola has also questioned its subsequent registration and regularization under the Abhay Yojana scheme.

Notably, The matter has now reached the office of the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Andheri. Confirming receipt of the complaint, Deputy Registrar Faiyaz Mulani told Mumbai Mirror that a hearing had been initiated and the other parties had been asked to submit their responses.

As per the latest buzz, Jalsa, one of Mumbai's most famous star residences, has been associated with Amitabh Bachchan for decades. Jalsa was originally named Mansa and was owned by producer N C Sippy. As per reports, it is shared that it was given to Amitabh Bachchan as remuneration for his 1982 movie, Satte Pe Satta . The superstar has previously spoken about purchasing, selling and later reacquiring the property.

In further updates, Meanwhile, Amitabh Bachchan did not respond to Mumbai Mirror's queries. Jaya Bachchan could not be reached, while a spokesperson for Abhishek Bachchan declined to comment, describing it as an internal family issue.
On top of that, The allegations remain disputed, and the authorities are yet to determine the validity of the documents and ownership-related claims.

title: Lara Dutta defends Kaikeyi's look in Ramayana amid costume debate, says people should not 'nitpick'
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana : Part One is enjoying a strong run at the ticket-window, with the movie nearing the ₹ 1,000 crore rupees mark in worldwide collections. While the movie has found acceptance among audiences, a section of viewers had debated the costumes worn by some of its characters. Sai Pallavi's look as Sita and Lara Dutta's portrayal of Kaikeyi were among the most discussed, with some viewers calling their outfits too modern for the Treta Yuga. Lara, for instance, was seen wearing a saree with a long sleeves blouse in the trailer.

Adding to this, Lara Dutta's Kaikeyi look divided internet and sparked 'modern saree' debate. Now, in an interaction, Lara has spoken about the costume debate for the first time and explained the thought behind the choices. She also shared that audiences should not nitpick over minor details when a project is mounted on such a large scale.

Meanwhile, Lara admitted that she understood the reasons behind the costume choices and the way the characters were presented. She told News18, “I know what the reason was for us to pick certain kinds of garments and the way that we wanted those to be depicted. It’s such a vast project that you’re undertaking and one nitpicked on such tiny things."

Notably, Lara also spoke about her conversations with director Nitesh Tiwari regarding her costumes and explained why Kaikeyi's sartorial sensibilities were suppose to be different from those of the other queens, Kaushalya and Sumitra.

As per the latest buzz, She shared, “One of my first conversations with Nitesh sir was that if Kaikeyi came from the kingdom of Kekaya, wouldn’t her jewellery be very different from the other two queens? Wouldn’t she bring her own stree-dhan? But if you want to get into such minute details, then you’re opening up a Pandora’s box and then you would’ve historians and other experts coming up and saying, ‘Oh, how can this be shown and depicted?’ So, there was a standardisation that was decided to be adopted across all three kingdoms – Mithila, Ayodhya and Lanka – to differentiate between those cultures."
In further updates, The star admitted that she completely submitted to the makers' vision and believed in looking at the larger picture rather than questioning every creative decision.

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana is the first instalment of a planned two-part cinematic adaptation of the Hindu epic. The movie features Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana.

The movie brings together a large international team of technicians, with music composed by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer and visual effects handled by DNEG. Ramayana rolled out in theatres on November 5, 2026. Its second instalment is planned for a Diwali rollout in 2028.

title: From Kismet to Dhurandhar and Ramayana: How Bollywood box office grew from ₹1 crore lifetime hauls to ₹100 crore in a day
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

When Dhurandhar The Revenge did a hat-trick of ₹ 100-crore rupees days at the Indian ticket-window earlier this year, it was seen as an oddity, an anomaly. Trade pundits argued that the combination of high ticket prices and hype would be hard to emulate. Ramayana proved them wrong in just eight months. On its first Monday, the Nitesh Tiwari movie minted ₹ 107.50 crore rupees in India.

Adding to this, Dhurandhar and Ramayana have rewritten box-office collection rules for Bollywood. The two films have set and solidified this new standard for what a Hindi movie can and should make at the domestic ticket-window to be a red-letter day. It is remarkable that just over a decade ago, this figure was considered good enough for a movie’s lifetime run. But the evolution of Hindi cinema’s box-office fortunes has always been that rapid. This evolution has seen the industry's blockbusters grow from earning ₹ 1 crore rupees in their lifetime to ₹ 100 crore rupees in a day.

Meanwhile, Box-office tabulation wasn’t always systematic in Indian cinema. In the pre-independence era, footfalls were counted. Sometimes, films’ runs were measured by how long they ran in theatres. Dadasaheb Phalke’s Lanka Dehen, considered the first ‘hit’, ran for 23 weeks upon rollout in 1917. But it wasn’t until 1940 that independent bodies and movie journalists began to calculate films’ earnings.

Notably, Three years later, Kismet emerged as Hindi cinema’s first smash hit. The Gyan Mukherjee movie, starring Ashok Kumar, rode the nationalistic wave and the thriller genre's appeal to mint ₹ 1 crore rupees. It is estimated the movie sold 3.75 crore rupees tickets in India at the time (the same as Dhurandhar 1). Kismet held the record for five years until the Tamil movie Chandralekha minted ₹ 1.55 crore rupees in 1948, snatching the crown. But it laid the foundation for ‘crore rupees’ to be used as a common term for Indian cinema’s box-office earnings.

As per the latest buzz, For the longest time, Indian films’ box-office earnings were measured solely by their domestic box-office takings. That is because most Indian films did not have a wide rollout overseas. There were exceptions. Awara and Sangam were hits in Russia, while Caravan had a great run in China. But the measure of a movie’s success remained what it did in India. By that metric, Mithun Chakraborty ’s Disco Dancer was a moderate success. It collected ₹ 6 crore rupees in India upon rollout in 1985. Two years later, it rolled out in Russia and became a cultural phenomenon. It remains one of the most-watched films in Russia even four decades later. After its rollout in Russia, Disco Dancer’s worldwide earnings grew to ₹ 100 crore rupees. In the 90s, Indian films began to rollout overseas as the diaspora opened new markets for Bollywood. Hum Aapke Hain Koun and Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge rode on this overseas wave to cross ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide. But no Indian movie reached the mark at the Indian ticket-window for years.

In further updates, From the 1950s to the 80s, Indian films almost always had staggered releases. Prints existed as large spools of reels. Transporting them across the country took time and effort. That is why most Indian films were rolled out in some markets on one date and in others weeks or even months later. For instance, Amitabh Bachchan’s debut movie Saat Hindustani rolled out in Delhi in 1969 and in Bombay only two years later. This meant that the concept of an ‘opening day or weekend’ was absent. Films grew by word of mouth only.

On top of that, That changed in the 90s as the distribution network grew, allowing filmmakers to rollout films almost simultaneously nationwide. The first movie to utilise this was Mukul Anand’s Trimurti. The action entertainer starred Anil Kapoor, Jackie Shroff, and Shah Rukh Khan. It came out two months after DDLJ, which had made Shah Rukh a big star. Anil and Jackie were already established names. The hype made Trimurti the biggest opener in Bollywood history. The movie minted ₹ 1.06 crore rupees on its first day. This feat made ₹ 1 crore rupees an aspirational opening figure for Bollywood, a trend that persisted till multiplexes arrived a few years later.

It was the multiplex era that guaranteed wide national releases as theatre chains allowed distributors to lock screens nationwide. This also led to an increase in ticket prices. According to Ticket-window India, the average ticket price in India increased from ₹ 25 in 2001 to ₹ 70 in 2008. This led to a boom in box-office earnings, too. And in 2008, a Hindi movie finally collected ₹ 100 crore rupees net domestically. It was Aamir Khan ’s Ghajini that created the 100-crore rupees club. Since then, over 150 films have joined the ranks from across languages and industries. This also created a new benchmark for measuring an Indian movie’s success. It had to be a ‘100-crore rupees hit ’.

title: Ranbir Kapoor's on-screen mother in Ramayana, Indira Krishnan, reveals he turned vegetarian to play Lord Rama
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Ranbir Kapoor faced criticism over his casting as Lord Rama in Ramayana ever since the movie's first promotional material was rolled out. However, following its rollout, his portrayal has impressed some of those who had earlier questioned the casting. In an interview with Filmygyan, Ranbir's on-screen mother, Indira Krishnan , opened up that the star turned vegetarian to play Lord Rama.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor essayed the role of Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ranbir Kapoor turned vegetarian for Ramayana Indira, who plays Kaushalya, Lord Rama's mother, in Ramayana, spoke about sharing a close bond with Ranbir off screen as well. The two had previously worked together in Animal. She opened up that while shooting for Ramayana, she always saw Shri Ram in front of her rather than Ranbir. Indira also called Ranbir her biggest supporter and recalled how he would often seek her opinion on his scenes.

Meanwhile, The star also came out in support of Ranbir amid the criticism surrounding his casting as Lord Rama. She shared, "We have this mentality that if someone is growing and is trying to perform a new character, we have a lot of audience who pull them down and troll them. I have also met people who couldn't believe Ranbir played Lord Rama."

Notably, Indira further recalled her memories of working with Ranbir on the sets of Ramayana and opened up that he would often express his wish to eat South Indian food. She shared, "He was completely a vegetarian in this entire process. Because I have seen he would eat fruits, work out a lot-3 hours in the morning and 2-3 hours in the evening. So he had a regime. I had almost been living with him on the set. Even his vanity had fruits. He was completely on the path to create Shri Rama inside and out. Even the way he used to talk and behave with people. He used to talk about Raha's education, always used to grab knowledge about which course he should get for Raha. He is an all-rounder, fabulous star and fabulous father."

As per the latest buzz, Ranbir faced criticism after being cast as Lord Rama in Ramayana because of his past remarks about being a "big beef fan" during a 2011 interview. The comments resurfaced after the casting announcement and upset sections of the audience. His portrayal of the aggressive, violent and misogynistic Ranvijay Singh in Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Animal also became a point of contention, with critics questioning whether an star associated with such a character could convincingly portray Lord Rama.

In further updates, Helmed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is among the most expensive films in Indian cinema. The two-part mythological epic has as per reports been mounted on a budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. Titled Ramayana: Rise of the Legend, the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, Ravi Dubey, Rakul Preet Singh, Lara Dutta, Kajal Aggarwal and Vivek Oberoi in key roles. The movie was rolled out on November 5 and has as per reports collected over ₹ 500 crore rupees at the domestic ticket-window.

title: 'Why watch Bollywood without the songs': Western audiences favour Ramayana's uncut Hindi version over shorter English dub
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Owing to its status as the biggest Indian movie ever, Ramayana was rolled out internationally on more screens than any other Indian movie. Sony Pictures acquired the global distribution rights for the Nitesh Tiwari movie, giving it 50,000 screens outside India, a good 10-15 times what an Indian movie normally gets. The makers also cut a shorter version of the movie for international rollout, christening it Ramayana: Rise of a Legend. The version, dubbed in English, is about 30 minutes shorter, cut that way to appeal to Western audiences. However, initial reactions from the West show that audiences there are lapping up the longer Hindi version.

Adding to this, Star Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama in the movie Ramayana The two versions of Ramayana Ramayana is 3 hours and 18 minutes long. The international version, Rise of a Legend, is 2 hours and 48 minutes long. It cuts out a few musical sequences, interludes, and much of the exposition, including a scene in which Lord Indra reaches out to Lord Vishnu after losing to Ravana. Additionally, the international version is dubbed into English, with Brahma AI technology used to sync lip movements with the lines. As per the latest buzz, the movie’s makers wanted to present a tighter, more action-oriented version to the West. However, early critics’ reviews shared that the longer Hindi version was better, as it did not rush through the story. The viewers seem to agree.

Meanwhile, On Reddit, after a viewer pointed out that the English version cut a lot of the songs, many were disappointed. One wrote, “Why anyone would go to a Bollywood movie about a foundational Indian text and not want to see the musical scenes is beyond me. That’s the best part!” Another echoed the sentiment and added, “Cut out the musical numbers? That's literally the best part of Bollywood/Tollywood films!!!!”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

As per the latest buzz, Many who watched the longer version defended the musical numbers, saying they were essential to the narrative. “The only notable dance scene outside of scattered community celebrations, was a Ravana solo sequence shortly after he comes to power, and it's quite good,” wrote one viewer from the US. Another viewer shared that removing the songs distorts the experiences as the musical numbers are different from the usual ‘Bollywood song-and-dance routine’. The comment read, “Just finished it. Go with the longer runtime. The musical is not really the usual dance-and-sing musicals of Bollywood. And when you kinda remove them from the movie, a part of the storyline would be cut weirdly.”

In further updates, Many swore by the Hindi version, saying they preferred to watch it with subtitles instead of the dubbed version. “Watch the Hindi with subtitles. 3h 15 min version; it's worth it and doesn't miss any beat of the storyline, which the English version does,” read one comment. Others shared that the longer version was even more entertaining than Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. “Saw the 3:15 one last night. I am going to be downvoted for this, but I found it far more entertaining than the Odyssey. It was a 3D extravaganza and a quick three hours,” they wrote.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part is running in theatres, while the second part is set for a Diwali 2028 rollout.
Part One has started off strong at the ticket-window, minting ₹ 935 crore rupees (about $100 million) in its first seven days at the global ticket-window.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection: Unstoppable Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film crosses ₹900 crore; beats Animal, Bajrangi Bhaijaan lifetime in a week
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

It was a post-festive break that allowed Ramayana to regain momentum at the ticket-window on Monday and Tuesday. But on Wednesday, the movie showed that the surge was no fluke. On its seventh day in theatres, the Nitesh Tiwari movie registered the best Wednesday in Indian cinema history, soaring past ₹ 900 crore rupees worldwide. It has now surpassed several all-time blockbusters and is aiming to touch ₹ 1000 crore rupees sometime today (November 12).

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in Ramayana. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash -starrer opened to great reviews on Thursday, with initial audience reactions largely positive. But the box-office opening remained below par. An opening weekend of ₹ 507 crore rupees worldwide would be admirable for most Indian films, but Ramayana has a reported budget of over ₹ 1600 crore rupees and hence, a much higher break-even point than even the biggest Indian films. Monday and Tuesday helped the movie accelerate, with over ₹ 150 crore rupees collected on both days. Wednesday was its first major test as the post-Diwali holidays ended.

Meanwhile, But even on a weekday, Ramayana did exceptional business, earning ₹ 70 crore rupees net in India on the day, the highest ever by an Indian movie on a non-holiday weekday and also the highest on a Wednesday. It beat Baahubali 2’s ₹ 52 crore rupees record by quite a margin. This takes Ramayana’s domestic haul to ₹ 511 crore rupees net ( ₹ 611 crore rupees gross) after seven days. Ramayana finishes its extended opening week today (Thursday).
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rotten Tomatoes (@rottentomatoes)

As per the latest buzz, The issue with Ramayana was its overseas earnings. Sony Pictures distributed the movie internationally, giving it a rollout in 59,000 screens worldwide, almost six times the size of any big Indian rollout. But the opening weekend saw returns of less than $25 million. However, here, too, the tide turned on Monday. On Wednesday, despite there being no holiday, Ramayana continued to mint money overseas. As of now, Ramayana has collected $34.5 million in the overseas markets. This takes the movie’s worldwide gross to ₹ 935 crore rupees after seven days. The movie has now collected over ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide on each of its seven days in the theatres, a new record for an Indian movie.

In further updates, On its seventh day, Ramayana crossed the ₹ 900-crore rupees mark, reaching ₹ 935 crore rupees in worldwide gross. In the process, it became the highest-grossing movie of Ranbir Kapoor’s career, beating the lifetime haul of Animal ( ₹ 915 crore rupees). On Wednesday, the movie also surpassed some other Indian blockbusters, including Aamir Khan’s Secret Superstar ( ₹ 916 crore rupees) and Salman Khan’s Bajrangi Bhaijaan ( ₹ 921 crore rupees). Both films were propped up by significant earnings from China, where Ramayana has not yet been rolled out.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part is running in theatres, while the second part is set for a Diwali 2028 rollout.

title: Shah Rukh Khan recalls not having a house of his own before marrying Gauri Khan, says even Mannat was beyond his means
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Karan Johar hosted an event in Dubai for Shahrukhz Residences by Danube, where Shah Rukh Khan brought his trademark wit and even danced to a track from his soon-to-release movie, King. The star got emotional as he spoke about the importance of having a home of his own, revealing that even Mannat was once beyond his means.

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan striking his signature pose at Mannat. Shah Rukh Khan says Mannat was ‘beyond his means’ The event was also attended by Shah Rukh's wife and interior designer, Gauri Khan. The star recalled how he lost his parents at a young age and did not have a home of his own, revealing that this made owning a house his biggest dream. He added, “Of course I love my family and my work but the only thing I love more than anything else in the world is to have a house. So my children make fun of me. Whenever we are driving through a new city and I like it, I tell them we need to buy a house here. They make fun of me saying one cannot have a house in every city. But I am fortunate. I didn't have my own home until I got married to Gauri.”

Meanwhile, He further emphasised the importance of having a home of his own and shared some advice for people who dream of buying one. He shared, “There are good days, bad days, some wonderful days and some very depressing days. When you finally come knocking, you need to come back to your own home because you regenerate there, you figure things out and go back to face the harsh realities of the world. The first house that Gauri and I bought was beyond our means; the last house, Mannat, that we bought was also beyond our means. But I want to tell everyone that when you want to buy your dream house, Allah helps you; God helps you. If you pray to God for a house, you'll get the most beautiful house in your life because the Almighty will always give you the house of your dreams. Just trust in yourself and the God.”

Notably, During the event, Shah Rukh also recreated some of his iconic dialogues from films such as Raees and Om Shanti Om. He then took to the stage and danced to the track Tu Mil Jaaye from his soon-to-release movie, King.

As per the latest buzz, Shah Rukh purchased Mannat, a seafront property situated in Mumbai's Bandra, in 2001. His house is currently undergoing renovation, which is expected to be completed by December 2026, as per the latest buzz. The family is expected to move back into Mannat once the work is completed, Hindustan Times reported in August 2026.

In further updates, The renovation has also involved a major expansion of the Mannat annexe. The annexe previously comprised around six floors, with two additional floors, covering a combined area of around 7,000 sq ft, being added.

On top of that, Shah Rukh is currently awaiting the rollout of his soon-to-release movie, King. Helmed by Siddharth Anand, the movie also stars Suhana Khan, Deepika Padukone and Abhishek Bachchan in lead roles. The movie marks SRK's return to the big screen after three years and is scheduled to rollout in theatres on December 24, 2026.

title: Film workers' body demands inquiry into reduction of Pyre shows after Ramayana release, asks I&B Minister to ensure FIRs against theatre owners
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Vinod Kapri ’s new movie, Pyre, has been earning acclaim from critics and audiences alike. And yet, the movie is struggling to find theatres nationally. Earlier this week, the filmmaker claimed that his movie's screen count had decreased by 75% after the rollout of Ramayana . He even urged cinema owners to allow his movie back as it had as per reports been running to packed auditoriums. Now, the All India Cine Workers Association has backed Kapri by writing a letter to Ashwini Vaishnaw , Minister of Information and Broadcasting, demanding an inquiry into the reduction in screen count and urging him to change the distribution system.

Adding to this, A still from Vinod Kapri's Pyre, an independent movie made on a small budget. AICWA writes to I&B Minister The letter has been written by AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta and addressed to the I&B Minister. In the letter, the body states that Vinod Kapri's Pyre, made on just ₹ 2.5 crore rupees, grew from 80 to about 400 screens, due to word of mouth. It then reiterates the filmmaker’s allegations that the screen count was reduced to less than 100 despite good response after Ramayana rolled out. “I do not oppose Ramayana: Rise of Legend. It is a large-budget movie that has given work to hundreds of workers, technicians, junior artists and artists across every department. It should succeed, so that producers profit and workers are paid on time. But a big movie's success should not come at the cost of a small movie that audiences are already embracing,” the AICWA president writes.

Meanwhile, Giving an example of small-budget hits like HanuMan, Gupta then advocates for fairness for small-budget films. “Small-budget films are the backbone of Indian cinema. They are the largest number of films made each year, and they give new and genuine talent its first opportunity. Their producers raise money with great difficulty and wait years to reach theatres, where they get very few screens. Most small films do not succeed, and when even a movie that is working is removed, small producers will stop making films, new artists will lose their chance, and lakhs of workers will lose employment,” he adds.

Notably, The letter then lists a set of demands, including a ‘Fair Screen Allocation Policy for Indian Cinema from the Central Government’ and ‘grievance redressal mechanism to protect independent and small-budget films’. Talking specifically about Pyre, the letter asks the I&B Minister to initiate an ‘ impartial inquiry into why Pyre was reduced from about 400 screens to under 100 despite a positive audience response��� and demands that FIRs be filed against the theatre owners and distributors found guilty after the inquiry. The demands also include a restoration of ‘maximum possible screens and shows for Pyre while the inquiry is on, so that audiences who want to see it can do so’.

As per the latest buzz, Pyre , directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri, rolled out in theatres last week to rave reviews. The movie tells the story of an elderly couple who continue to wait for their children, even as life in their Himalayan village grows quieter with each passing day. It features newcomers and is made on a shoestring budget of just ₹ 2.50 crore rupees. On Saturday, Kapri posted a video message on X alleging unfairness from exhibitors.

In further updates, “We are in touch with theatre owners and distributors. They have been told that no other movie will be running in theatres except one movie. I do not understand why you have to run your movie by stopping other films? Is this a win of good over evil? Is there any honor in doing this? The honor with which we tell a story. This is a small movie, with non actors, and people are crying after seeing it. What honor, truth and goodness do you boast when this is the way theatres are ordered? I urge theatre owners and distributors to not do this with Pyre. If you have spent a lot of money, then we have spent our soul in making a movie. We deserve a fair chance,” he shared.

On top of that, While the filmmaker did not name the ‘big movie’, his video came right after the rollout of Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana, the most expensive Indian movie made. “This is not fair, not to Pyre. Not to your audience,” read the caption of Kapri’s post.

title: Kiara Advani reveals bonding over motherhood with Alia Bhatt, Katrina Kaif during postpartum phase after Saraayah's birth
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Kiara Advani embraced motherhood in 2025 when she welcomed her first child, a daughter named Saraayah, with her husband, Sidharth Malhotra . The star is now expecting her second child. In a recent appearance on Koffee With Karan alongside Sidharth, Kiara spoke about the emotional and physical changes that come with motherhood. She also revealed how she reached out to Alia Bhatt, Katrina Kaif and Patralekhaa during her postpartum phase.

Adding to this, Kiara Advani recalls calling Katrina Kaif and Alia Bhatt during postpartum phase. Kiara Advani recalls calling Alia Bhatt and Katrina Kaif during postpartum phase In the last season of Koffee With Karan, Kiara appeared on the couch with her husband, star Sidharth Malhotra. She recalled breaking down during a podcast after becoming a mother and shared the experience helped her channel her emotions. She shared, "Sometimes all you want is an outlet. It is such a whole shift for any new mom that women really understand women. When we found out that we were pregnant for the first time, the first three months were really hard. You go through nausea and hormone changes. At that time, we thought we wouldn’t tell anyone. I shared I needed to talk to my mother and mother-in-law. I need women who understand me."

Meanwhile, Karan then opened up that Kiara would call Alia Bhatt, Katrina Kaif and Patralekhaa during her postpartum phase. Kiara added, "We were checking up on each other. All of us are in the same field. I remember calling her (Alia) up and asking about getting back to shoot, and understanding how do we make this work. Your priority is your family as well, and at work you are professional. How do you blend these two worlds in a way that doesn’t make you feel guilty at times? Mom guilt is just there."
Notably, While Alia welcomed her first child in 2022, Katrina became a mother in 2025 when she gave birth to her son, Vihaan. Patralekhaa and Rajkummar Rao also welcomed a baby girl in November 2025.

As per the latest buzz, Kiara Advani is married to star Sidharth Malhotra. The couple tied the knot on February 7, 2023, in an intimate wedding ceremony in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, after dating for several years. They welcomed their first child, a baby girl, on July 15, 2025. They revealed the news on social media, writing, “Our hearts are full and our world forever changed. We are blessed with a Baby Girl.�� In November 2025, they revealed her name as Saraayah Malhotra, meaning God's princess.

In further updates, On October 7 this year, Kiara put up a post announcing her second pregnancy with Sidharth on Instagram. The couple wrote, “Blessed once again with the greatest gift of all. Our hearts are so full of love and gratitude.”

title: Sidharth Malhotra was aware The Vvaan was being written off before its box office success, says Bollywood needs to support its own films
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Sidharth Malhotra believes audiences are increasingly warming up to films that draw from Indian culture, folklore and traditions, even when there is little confidence in them before rollout. The star spoke about the industry's tendency to dismiss films too early and why people need to be more supportive of each other's work during his appearance with wife Kiara Advani on the final season of Koffee With Karan. It was their first joint appearance on the show, making the episode a special one for the couple as they are set to welcome their second child next year.

Adding to this, Sidharth Malhotra says he heard The Vvaan wouldn't work at the ticket-window, urges movie industry to be more supportive. (SHAZID CHAUHAN) While the two shared some fun moments on Karan Johar's couch, the conversation also turned to Sidharth's movie The Vvaan : Force of the Forrest. The star opened up about how the movie managed to find an audience despite the initial doubts about its ticket-window prospects, and why he believes stories rooted in Indian culture are connecting with moviegoers.

Meanwhile, Karan brought up The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest and pointed out that there had been considerable chatter about the movie not doing well at the ticket-window. Both Sidharth and Kiara acknowledged the skepticism around the fantasy adventure, which rolled out in September 2026. The star, however, believes its reception reflects a growing interest in stories that audiences can connect with culturally.

Notably, "I think they are doing their job and we are doing our job," Sidharth shared. “There is an India and there is a Bharat. I think Bharat is what is coming out to watch our films. They want to watch something rooted, something to them and rooted in culture. The Vvaan came perfectly fitting that bracket whether it is the writing, performance, whether it was sequences.”

As per the latest buzz, Kiara agreed with her husband as Sidharth about how people within the industry are often quick to find fault rather than appreciate each other's work. He shared, “Of course. Our industry has more of that and nobody has anything good thing to say. What we need as a sense of an industry where people help each other.”

In further updates, The subject of criticism came up again during the rapid-fire round when Karan asked Sidharth how he looks at movie critics. The star shared, “Give your opinion, but it is not always about dissing or discouraging people to go to the theatres.”

On top of that, The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest draws from the folklore surrounding the Van Devi Temple near Bihta in Bihar. Sidharth plays Rishi, a Mumbai-based man who travels to the village of Devanchal with his wife Mamta (Tamannaah Bhatia) for a land-related matter. This begins as a routine visit as it turns into something far more unsettling when he learns about the village's age-old beliefs, particularly the warning against entering the forest after dark. The movie collected ₹ 91.49 crore rupees worldwide in its run and is currently streaming on Prime Video.

This is Kiara and Sidharth's first joint appearance on Koffee with Karan. The ninth season of the show is its final, host Karan Johar revealed earlier this year in a promo. Koffee With Karan began in 2003 and has since been a staple, first on TV, and now on streaming. The latest season is streaming on JioHotstar.

title: Emraan Hashmi blames Aditya Datt for his ‘serial kisser’ image at Gunmaaster G9 trailer launch, says he has faced the consequences for 20 years
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The trailer of Gunmaaster G9 starring Emraan Hashmi in the lead role was unveiled on Wednesday. This marks his reunion with filmmaker Aditya Datt and well, the star has a bone to pick with him. At the trailer launch in Pune, Emraan talked about his on-screen image from the early days of his career, especially the ‘serial kisser’ image. Sharing the stage with Genelia Deshmukh, Aparshakti Khurana, Abhishek Singh, director Aditya Datt and producer Deepak Mukut, he also spoke about his reunion with the team of Aashiq Banaya Aapne and why their latest collaboration is designed for the big screen.

Adding to this, Emraan Hashmi recalls how parents sent kids to bed when his films aired on TV at Gunmaaster G9 trailer launch in Pune. Emraan Hashmi jokes about his image Whilst addressing the media and the followers, Emraan was quick to bring up his reputation from the early 2000s, when his romantic films often made headlines for their bold content. Taking a dig at himself, he shared, “These were the films that, whenever they aired on TV, parents would decide it was time to send their children to bed.” He added, “This is all thanks to him (Aditya Datt). I've been dealing with the consequences for 20 years.”

Meanwhile, The star also spoke about working with director Aditya and composer Himesh Reshammiya again, almost 21 years after Aashiq Banaya Aapne (2005). While the trio had discussed several stories over the years, Emraan shared they wanted to wait for the right movie to bring them together. “I think when we wanted to collaborate again; there were several stories we discussed,” he shared. “But we were clear that whenever we came together for a movie, it should be a celebration of cinema, something we would enjoy watching as followers when we go to the theatre.”

Notably, Emraan hopes audiences will be able to immerse themselves in the movie's world and enjoy it as a complete theatrical experience. “When people come together to collaborate, I feel Gunmaaster G9 has come together really well. It is the kind of commercial movie where, once you enter the theatre, you get completely absorbed in its world. You will be entertained throughout. This is a big movie, and it is meant to be enjoyed on the big screen,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, The movie was shot across Haridwar, Dehradun and Rishikesh over a period of nearly 60 days. The star shared one of the things he particularly enjoyed was getting away from studio floors and shooting in actual locations. “Today, when you look at the way films are being made, you see actors shooting in studios. A lot of films are shot against green screens,” he shared. “We stepped out and shot at real locations, despite the technical and logistical challenges involved. Getting that in real locations is but thankfully these occasions, the people there, they were very supportive”.

In further updates, Gunmaaster G9 is a Himesh Reshammiya musical, produced by Deepak Mukut, Hunar Mukut and Sangeeta Ahir. The movie is presented by Soham Rockstar Entertainment Pvt. Ltd. and produced under the banner of SRE Studios LLP. PEN Marudhar is handling its all-India distribution, while Phars Films will rollout it overseas. The movie will rollout worldwide in theatres on November 27, 2026.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Rs. 300 crore blockbuster Hanuman Ansh to have a UNIQUE success bash in Mumbai; guests to be served ONLY pure veg, satvik food
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

A source told Bollywood Hungama , “The success party of Hanuman Ansh will take place over the weekend in Mumbai. The entire team of the movie, including the producers, director Vishal Chaturvedi and the star cast, will be present in full force. Representatives of Cinepolis India, which distributed the movie, will also be in attendance. After all, they played an important role in the movie's success by ensuring that it received a proper theatrical rollout.”

Adding to this, The source continued, “However, this won't be your typical movie success bash. Interestingly, no alcohol or non-vegetarian food will be served at the party. Instead, guests will be treated to pure vegetarian, satvik food, in keeping with the beliefs of the team and the spiritual theme of Hanuman Ansh . The makers want the celebration to reflect the values and sentiments associated with the movie.”

Meanwhile, Hanuman Ansh chronicles the life of Neeb Karori Baba, aka Neem Karoli Baba. Shobhinaw Satyaa plays the titular role in the movie, which also stars Chandan K Anand, Anil Rastogi, Bhagvandas Patel, Nikhil Dubey, Purnima Tiwari and others. The movie is expected to be the first instalment of a three-part series.

Notably, In a recent interview, one of its producers, Namrata Singh, revealed for the first time the movie's actual budget and a detailed break-up of its expenses. She told The Economic Times, “The movie was made at a total cost of Rs 1.7 crore rupees. Haldiram’s provided Rs 1.25 crore rupees towards prints and advertising (P&A) as part of the co-production arrangement. Of the P&A budget, we spent approximately Rs. 65-70 lakhs on marketing, with the remaining amount going towards the rollout. We wanted to ensure that the movie remained in theatres for three weeks, which involved an additional expenditure of over Rs. 40 lakhs. The overall expenditure, including production and P&A, was approximately Rs. 2.95 crores or close to Rs. 3 crores.”

title: Kiara Advani says Sidharth Malhotra was unbothered by her intimate scenes with Yash in Toxic, admits film's negative response left her ‘very low’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Kiara Advani has spoken about the criticism she faced for her intimate scenes with Yash in Toxic : A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, admitting that the movie's initial reception left her disappointed. The star discussed the row on Koffee With Karan Season 9, where she appeared alongside husband Sidharth Malhotra . The episode also gave the couple a chance to celebrate a personal milestone. Kiara and Sidharth revealed in early October 2026 that they were expecting their second child.

Adding to this, Kiara Advani reveals Sidharth Malhotra never brought up her intimate scenes in Toxic, says negative response left her ‘very low’. Kiara Advani admits Toxic's response was heartbreaking In conversation with Karan Johar about the movie's performance, Kiara shared she had a difficult time dealing with the response during its opening weekend. Despite the strong opening, the movie did not receive the reaction the team had hoped for. “On day one, it is heartbreaking. Especially for this movie, because as a team in totality any of us saw this coming. When it misfired despite it opening to what it did. It was heartbreaking for me that first weekend. I was very low about it,” she shared.

Meanwhile, However, the star also found some encouragement in the appreciation she received for taking on a role that was different from what audiences had seen her do before. She shared, “But, then, there was a lot of appreciation. The fact that I had gone outside of my comfort zone playing that role. I think in my journey this will be defining.”

Notably, The conversation soon moved to the trolling that followed the rollout of the song Tabaahi. Kiara faced personal attacks for her intimate scenes with Yash, with several social media users questioning her choices because she is married and a mother. Sidharth was also brought into the discussion, with people speculating about his reaction to the scenes.

As per the latest buzz, Karan highlighted the obvious gender bias in the criticism, pointing out that married male actors are rarely questioned in the same way for performing intimate scenes. Kiara shared Sidharth had never made an issue of it and that the subject had not even come up between them. “He had not cared about it. He has never brought it up. We have never spoken about it. It did not affect him, he was not bothered,” she shared.

In further updates, She also pointed out that this was hardly a new experience for women in the movie industry. “It has been happening now for donkey years, for decades. From Aishwarya to so many wonderful actors,” she added.

On top of that, Interestingly, Kiara shared she did not feel the need to defend herself when the row was unfolding. "What I must touch upon is when I was seeing what was going on the internet, there was a massive reaction of people who had already started calling it out, the hypocrisy, and I really did not feel the need to even justify," she shared.

Directed by Geetu Mohandas, Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups was Yash's first movie after KGF: Chapter 2. Set in post-independence Goa, the gangster drama follows a world shaped by crime, violence, power struggles and shifting loyalties. Yash plays two characters, Raya and his son Rumi, while Kiara plays Nadia, Rumi's mother.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood couple Kiara Advani and Sidharth Malhotra are the latest guests on the last season of Karan Johar’s chat show, Koffee With Karan . The new episode of the show's final season sees Kiara and Sidharth talk about everything from their marriage to their careers, and how their romance began on the sets of Shershaah. However, the couple also opened up that they briefly broke up during the movie’s shoot, only to rekindle their romance later.

Adding to this, Kiara Advani and Sidharth Malhotra began dating in 2020 and tied the knot in 2023. When Kiara Advani and Sidharth Malhotra broke up Kiara and Sidharth met briefly at a party after she had wrapped Lust Stories, following which, in 2019, they started working together on Shershaah, the biopic of war hero Captain Vikram Batra. Romance blossomed on the set. But on Koffee With Karan, Kiara opened up that before Sidharth left for the movie's Kargil schedule, the two had broken up. The night before the star left, Kiara told him, “You’re very hot and cold with me. For me, you’re either in or you’re out. Like this in between, I don’t understand; I can’t do it.”

Meanwhile, Sidharth agreed with Kiara then and felt they both needed to focus on their careers at the point. “I know that you’re the kind of person that if I commit to, then this will be something solid. title: Karan Johar defends celebrity couple episodes amid Koffee With Karan trolling: “Don't tell a couple what they should do”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The filmmaker addresses the online backlash surrounding the episodes that featured real life couples like Ranveer – Deepika and Vijay – Rashmika.

Adding to this, Recalling the backlash that followed the premiere episode of Koffee With Karan 8, which featured Ranveer Singh and Deepika Padukone together for the first time on the star chat show, Karan maintained that the couple was simply being honest about their relationship. Defending their appearance, he shared, “They are beautifully in love. Such good actors in love with each other.”

Meanwhile, He further questioned why their candid conversation became a subject of judgement. “They were just being honest about their lives. Since when should honesty be judged? You should be appreciative of someone's honesty,” he shared.

Notably, Karan also spoke about the criticism surrounding the Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna episode, which featured in the second episode of Koffee With Karan 9. Addressing the way viewers scrutinised the couple's interactions and relationship, the filmmaker shared that while everyone was entitled to an opinion, there was a distinction between expressing an observation and attempting to dictate how two people should conduct their relationship.

As per the latest buzz, “Everyone's entitled to an opinion. But when you start telling them what to do in that relationship, I have a very big problem,” he remarked. Questioning the sense of entitlement behind such commentary, he added, “Who are you? Are you a counsellor? Are you a lawyer? Are you a member of their family?”

In further updates, The filmmaker also raised concerns about the involvement of star families in online discussions. He pointed out that while public figures naturally attract opinions and scrutiny, their family members should not be dragged into conversations about their relationships. “You are commenting on their families. You can have an opinion on any star. Don't demean their families. Their families weren't on that couch,” he shared.

On top of that, Reflecting on the culture of online commentary, Karan observed that every statement made on the show is now subjected to intense scrutiny, with individual lines often being taken apart and analysed. He acknowledged that digital platforms have created opportunities for content creators and publications to generate viewership through provocative headlines and opinions. However, he also maintained that everyone has a role to play in this ecosystem.

“At every given point of time, every line shared is micro-analysed. If you want to, and if you think that your clickbait headline or your content piece about the show is going to get you a certain amount of viewership, that's also great,” he shared.

title: Nitish Bharadwaj withdraws praise for Ramayana Part 1; says he is “deeply upset and disappointed” with Ranbir Kapoor starrer
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The star, who had earlier predicted an Oscar win for the movie, has now criticised and questioned its representation of Indian cultural heritage.

Adding to this, In his post, Nitish emphasised that the Ramayana is deeply embedded in India's civilizational and spiritual consciousness and that its characters cannot be redefined casually. Expressing his reservations about the movie's interpretation, he wrote, “By presenting Ravan as an exceptionally liberal, socially just and fair figure, the movie, in my view, alters the moral framework of the Ramayan and undermines the very purpose of avataar.”

Meanwhile, The star further explained that the purpose of Lord Ram's incarnation was to uphold Dharma, tradition and Maryada. He maintained that the movie's representation of the epic should remain mindful of the values and philosophical significance associated with its characters.

Notably, One of the most significant aspects of his latest post was his decision to withdraw his earlier appreciation of the project. Expressing his disappointment in no uncertain terms, Nitish wrote, “I am deeply upset and disappointed with this movie. I withdraw my earlier post about it. I cannot find a single good word to say about it.” He also criticised the movie's reliance on visual effects, adding, “A spectacle of VFX can never substitute for the core values, philosophical depth and spiritual essence of this Mahakavya.”

As per the latest buzz, Nitish also questioned whether the movie deserved to represent Indian cinema on the international stage, stating that, in his opinion, its narrative misrepresents India's history, heritage and core spiritual values. He concluded by emphasising the need for responsible representation of the country's cultural legacy.
In further updates, A post shared by Nitish Bharadwaj (@nitishbharadwaj.krishna)

On top of that, Interestingly, the star's latest comments mark a significant departure from his earlier reaction to Ramayana . Following the rollout of the movie's trailer a few months ago, Nitish had taken to social media to praise the scale of the project and its technical ambition. He had even predicted, “100% Oscar for Best Foreign Movie,” while congratulating producer Namit Malhotra and director Nitesh Tiwari.

In the same post, he had lauded the production design and cinematography, acknowledged Hans Zimmer's collaboration with Indian cinema and welcomed Yash to global cinema. He had also expressed confidence in Ranbir Kapoor's acting abilities while urging the star to take responsibility for representing India's heritage and cultural values through his choice of roles. At the time, Nitish had expressed his desire to watch the movie multiple times.

title: Gunmaaster G9 trailer: Emraan Hashmi turns deadly for love, warns enemies as he vows to protect his family at any cost
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

After Awarapan 2 , Emraan Hashmi is back in action, and this time, love comes with a heavy dose of violence. The trailer of his soon-to-release movie, Gunmaaster G9, gives a glimpse into a world of broken relationships, betrayal and revenge, with the star playing a man who is willing to go to any lengths to protect his loved ones. Directed by Aditya Datt, the movie also features Genelia Deshmukh, Aparshakti Khurana and Abhishek Singh.

Adding to this, Gunmaaster G9 also brings Emraan, director Aditya Datt and composer Himesh Reshammiya together again, nearly two decades after their 2005 movie Aashiq Banaya Aapne. Gunmaaster G9 trailer The trailer arrives after the movie's teaser and music releases, offering a closer look at its characters and the conflict driving the story. In the opening scene, Emraan's character says, “A priest has his tilak, a Muslim brother has his faith, and we have our love......we hold these on our heads with pride. But one day, someone threw them to the ground and trampled them.” His softer side comes through in his interactions with Genelia's character. Assuring her that he will always protect her, he says, “I may not be able to make you laugh. But I will never let anyone make you cry.”

Meanwhile, But leaving his past behind may not be as easy as he hopes. A police officer introduces him by saying, “He was a thug, and now he's acting all decent.” Aparshakti Khurana, who appears to play an antagonist, adds to the tension. He is first heard reciting the rhyme, ‘Nani teri morni ko mor le gaye…’ before delivering a chilling warning: “Whoever commits treachery, the country devours him and his family.”

Notably, Emraan's character makes his intentions clear in another intense exchange, warning anyone who threatens his loved ones. He says, “If anyone even looks at my love and my family, I will gouge their eyes out. If anyone raises a hand towards them, I will cut that hand off. I won't kill them one by one and lay them on the funeral pyre. First, I'll lay them on the pyre, and then I'll kill them. In love, it's customary to shed tears, but I will shed blood.”

As per the latest buzz, The visuals offer plenty of glimpses of the movie's action-packed world. In one sequence, Emraan walks towards a group of armed men gathered around black SUVs in a vast, rocky landscape. He shows little sign of backing down, even as he finds himself outnumbered. Another scene shows him grabbing a bloodied man by the hair inside a dimly lit room, hinting at the brutality that awaits.

In further updates, Gunmaaster G9 also brings Emraan, director Aditya Datt and composer Himesh Reshammiya together again, nearly two decades after their 2005 movie Aashiq Banaya Aapne. The trailer also makes room for romance with Afsaana Banaaya Aapne, sung and composed by Himesh along with Asees Kaur. The song plays as Genelia's character tries to convince Emraan's character not to let their past affect their relationship.

On top of that, “I'm known for playing characters who have often found themselves in dangerous situations, but Gunmaaster G9 takes that to another level. This time, I am not just reacting to the danger; I am right in the middle of the action. The hand-to-hand combat, gun sequences and stunts demanded a different kind of preparation. I wanted to make sure that the action felt convincing and that audiences saw a side of me they hadn't seen before. That's what made this movie exciting for me,” Emraan says.

Genelia says the movie's commercial appeal lies in its ability to bring together very different emotions. She adds, “What I enjoyed about Gunmaaster G9 is that it doesn't restrict itself to one mood. There's action, but there's also romance, humour, music and emotion. A movie like this gives you the opportunity to entertain audiences in several ways. Working with Emraan for the first time was also something I was looking forward to. The trailer is only a glimpse of the world we've created.”

title: Ramayana box office collection day 7: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film remains unstoppable even after festive break, mints ₹70 crore to race past ₹500 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana created mayhem in the first two days after its opening weekend, raking in over ₹ 200 crore rupees net at the Indian ticket-window. The Nitesh Tiwari movie made full use of the post-Diwali holidays to maximise its box-office collections. Now, on Wednesday, the movie faced its first major test after working days began post the holiday. And the epic passed with flying colours, refusing to lose any momentum and still maintaining its grip at the ticket window.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama in Ramayana. Ramayana ticket-window update Ramayana began with a ₹ 64.85 crore rupees opening day, a low figure given the movie’s scale. It then fell slightly before recovering, ending its opening weekend at ₹ 239 crore rupees net in India. Then came Monday and Tuesday, when the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer shattered all-time collection records. The movie collected ₹ 107 crore rupees net on Monday and ₹ 94 crore rupees net on Tuesday, both the highest in Indian cinema history.

Meanwhile, But while Ramayana had the advantage of Govardhan Pooja and Bhai Dooj on Monday and Tuesday, respectively, Wednesday offered no such respite. Yet, the movie has maintained an impressive pace at the ticket-window. On Wednesday, Ramayana collected ₹ 70.65 crore rupees net in India, taking its domestic haul to ₹ 511 crore rupees .

Notably, Initially, the surge was driven largely by the Hindi version of the movie, but now the dubbed versions have begun to pay off. Ramayana has crossed ₹ 100 crore rupees in net earnings across its four dubbed versions in India, becoming the first Hindi movie to do so.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana entered the elite 500-crore rupees club on Wednesday. No Hindi movie had breached the mark until Pathaan did so three years ago. And now, Ramayana is set to reach the milestone in its opening week. This is a remarkable pace, one that the movie would need to sustain if it wants to break even with its reported ₹ 1600 crore rupees budget.
In further updates, On Thursday, Ramayana will look to surpass the lifetime domestic collections of big-budget blockbusters such as Gadar 2, Pathaan, and Animal.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first part of a duology. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for rollout on Diwali 2028.

He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. title: Ramayana actor Chetan Hansraj reveals his Sumali look took 4 hours to create
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Star Chetan Hansraj , who plays Raja Mali, the maternal grandfather of Ravana , in Ramayana , of late shared his experience of working on the movie on social media. The star posted behind-the-scenes pictures from the sets and credited makeup artist Virginia Holmes for his look in the movie. He also opened up that it took the makeup team four gruelling hours every day to create his character's look.

Adding to this, Chetan Hansraj shared his experience of working on Ramayana. 'The visual madness doesn't happen in isolation' Chetan also shared a picture with director Nitesh Tiwari and credited him and the rest of the team for bringing the world of Ramayana to life. He wrote, "The architects of the epic. 🎬🔥 ​The visual madness you are all seeing on the big screen doesn't happen in isolation. It takes a village of absolute masterminds to build a cinematic universe of this scale. ​Massive respect to our visionary director @niteshtiwari22 for steering this colossal ₹ 1,500 crore rupees ship and trusting me to anchor the opening sequence."

Meanwhile, Crediting makeup artist Virginia Holmes and her team, Chetan wrote, "Before I even stepped onto the Volume, the brilliant Virginia Holmes @virgholmes and her team spent 4 grueling hours every day meticulously sculpting the ancient, brutal visage of Raja Mali onto my face."

Notably, The star also spoke about working with movement director Terry Notary, who is known for his work on Hollywood films, including the Planet of the Apes franchise, X2 (2003), Superman Returns (2006) and Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007).

As per the latest buzz, Speaking about working with him, Chetan wrote, "Then came the physical execution. An incredible honor working alongside the legend Terry Notary @terrynotary (Action Director , Motion Capture & Movement Director). We spent hours breaking down the exact physics and psychology of a demon king so that every single movement felt lethal. ​Huge props to Ian Van Temperley @stuntalliancegroup and his stunt team for curating those absolutely insane action sequences, ensuring every swing of the axe was merciless. ​And a massive shoutout to Andrew Doucette (Animation Supervisor) for taking all that raw performance capture data and translating it into the most groundbreaking VFX Indian cinema has ever seen. ​The blood, sweat, and scale of this movie is historic. Thank you for the massive love on the recent posts!"

title: Vinod Kapri submits Pyre independently for 99th Oscars, says film deserves to compete on its own merit
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri has submitted his independent movie Pyre for consideration in the General Entry categories of the 99th Academy Awards through the independent route. In a recent interaction, the director verified the development and also revealed why he decided to submit his movie independently.

Adding to this, Vinod Kapri's Pyre aims for an Oscar. 'Never imagined the movie would touch so many hearts' In conversation with India Today, Vinod admitted that he had never expected the movie to touch so many hearts around the world. He shared, "We made Pyre independently, with complete faith in the story and the people who brought it to life. We never imagined that two ordinary people from a small Himalayan village would touch so many hearts across the world. The movie has travelled to international festivals, won awards and, most importantly, found its audience."

Meanwhile, Sharing the reason behind submitting his movie through the independent route, he shared, "We believe independent cinema deserves the opportunity to compete on its own merits. Our decision to pursue the Academy Awards through the applicable independent submission route is an extension of that belief. This is not just a journey for our movie; it is also a journey for the many independent filmmakers who continue to tell stories against all odds."

Notably, Filmmaker Santosh Davakhar's Marathi thriller Gondhal has been selected as India's official entry in the Best International Feature Movie category for the 99th Academy Awards. Meanwhile, the Nagaland movie Angh, which won the coveted Platform Prize at the 2026 Toronto International Movie Festival, also qualified for the Best International Feature Movie category at the Academy Awards. This was made possible by a new Academy rule that gives certain top honours at international movie festivals a direct pathway to Oscar qualification.

As per the latest buzz, Pyre stars 80-year-old Padam Singh Kapri, a retired Indian Army serviceman, and 70-year-old Heera Devi, both of whom are making their acting debuts. Padam plays a character named after himself, while Heera portrays Tulsi. The movie revolves around an elderly couple living in the hills who wait for their children to return after they leave the village in search of better opportunities.

In further updates, In an interview with Hindustan Times, Vinod spoke about the challenges of bringing his movie to theatres. He also recalled announcing his retirement after receiving an award at the Toronto International Movie Festival. However, he admitted that the positive response from audiences restored his faith in filmmaking.

On top of that, He shared, “I was so so depressed and so mentally, physically, financially exhausted that I revealed my retirement from that stage after receiving the award from Deepa Meta. I shared I'm done with filmmaking. I'm not going to make any movie after this because I'm completely drained out after making this movie.”

title: Divya Dutta: This has been a knockout year for me with Chiraiya, Gajab Raat and Last Man In Tower

title: Rohit Shetty clarifies his social media presence after fake post about Gaurav Gupta’s Bigg Boss 20 roast goes viral: “My only official social media presence is on Instagram”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Taking to Instagram, Rohit clarified that it is the only platform where he maintains an official social media presence. He also specifically shared that he does not have accounts on Facebook or X (formerly Twitter), cautioning people against mistaking profiles impersonating him for his official accounts.
Adding to this, Rohit wrote, “I would like to clarify that my only official social media presence is on Instagram. I am not present on Facebook or X.”

Meanwhile, The filmmaker also addressed the circulation of unauthorised profiles using his name and identity. Warning users against engaging with such accounts, he shared, "Any account or profile claiming to be me on these platforms is fake and unauthorised."

Notably, Reiterating his request, Rohit urged people not to associate any content shared through these profiles with him. “I request everyone to not engage with such accounts or consider any content posted through them as coming from me. Thank you for your understanding and continued support,” he wrote.

As per the latest buzz, Rohit's clarification comes amid discussions surrounding a post attributed to him that began circulating online following Gaurav Gupta's roast of Bigg Boss 20 contestants Scout OP and Love Gill. The widely shared post appeared to take a stand against humour that crosses the line into personal insults. It as per reports carried the message, "Friendly roasting theek hai par roasting ke naam par kisi ka mazaak udaana band hona chahiye."

In further updates, The alleged post was being linked to Gaurav's jokes about Scout OP's relationship with his girlfriend, Kaashvi Hiranandani, as well as his equation with fellow contestant Love Gill. As the message gained traction, several social media users speculated that Rohit had indirectly commented on the comedian's performance.

On top of that, However, with his latest clarification, the filmmaker has distanced himself from the Facebook and X profiles circulating such content, reiterating that Instagram remains his only official social media platform.

title: Nora Fatehi’s appearance in Sukesh Chandrashekhar Case comes under scrutiny as defence prepares for cross-examination
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

During her deposition, Fatehi as per reports reiterated her account that she had been engaged as an artiste for a charity event in Chennai in December 2020 and had not received any payment for it. However, the defence has questioned this version, pointing to her earlier statements to investigating agencies, as reported in the media, concerning a luxury handbag, a phone and a BMW car allegedly linked to the same event.
Adding to this, The defence maintains that these aspects have not yet been examined through cross-examination and will be raised during the proceedings.

Meanwhile, Fatehi's team has maintained that she is appearing in the matter only as a witness. Responding to this, the defence has referred to Section 319 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), which allows a trial court to proceed against another person, including someone appearing as a witness, if evidence presented during the trial indicates their involvement in an offence.

Notably, In a statement, Advocate Anant Malik, counsel for Sukesh Chandrashekhar, shared, “Nobody disputes that Ms. Fatehi has been summoned as a witness. But a summons is not a certificate of innocence, and it is certainly not a licence to treat the Court’s time as optional. The Hon’ble Court itself had to remind her not to take it for granted. What the public has heard today is a handful of rehearsed lines. Cross-examination is where that story will be tested. The defence will place documents and material before the Hon’ble Court, and if that material shows her role was larger than she admits, we will seek appropriate orders, strictly in accordance with law, including under Section 319 CrPC. Star or not, every witness stands equal before the law.”

As per the latest buzz, The defence further shared that it has full faith in the court and the trial process, adding that its arguments will be presented through evidence and cross-examination. The statement was issued by the office of Advocate Anant Malik, who represents Sukesh Chandrashekhar in the case.
