title: Mumbai Police advises Bollywood stars to avoid public places after attack on Tiger Shroff: Report
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Indian police have advised prominent Bollywood actors to avoid attending large gatherings, visiting public places andmingling with followers in crowded areas after an star was shot at in Mumbai last month, local media reported on Tuesday.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan greets followers outside his house in Mumbai's Juhu suburb. (PTI) Mumbai Police issuedthe advisory as a precautionary measure due to renewed security concerns surrounding Bollywood stars in the city, the reports shared, citing an unnamed senior police officer. The Mumbai Police Commissioner's office did not respond to an email from Reuters seeking comment.
Meanwhile, Star Tiger Shroff was shot and injured when three men opened fire on his car as he was leaving a football ground in Mumbai, India's financial and entertainment capital.
Notably, The three suspected shooters were arrested within days, and eight others allegedly linked to the conspiracy were detained subsequently, local media reported, citing police.

As per the latest buzz, Police are investigating whether the attack was linked to a criminal gang which has been associated with other attacks targeting Bollywood personalities in the past, the reports shared.
In further updates, The incident prompted a wider security reassessment for Bollywood personalities by police and the private security teams that protect the actors, local media shared.

On top of that, Heightened security has also become visible during public appearances by movie stars since, with veteran star Amitabh Bachchan greeting followers outside his Mumbai residence from behind protective glass, as shown in images on social and local media.
Bollywood has a long history of being targeted by organised crime groups, with attacks, extortion demands and threats spanning more than three decades.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 6: Back-to-back ₹150-crore days lift Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film past ₹800 crore; beats PK, Chhaava lifetime
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

After the best Monday in Indian cinema history, Ramayana followed it up with the best Tuesday ever: another red-letter day where the movie collected close to ₹ 100 crore rupees net in India and over ₹ 160 crore rupees gross worldwide. This has propelled the Nitesh Tiwari movie close to the ₹ 1000-crore rupees mark worldwide, and it has not even completed a full week at the ticket-window yet.

Adding to this, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash -starrer opened to great reviews on Thursday, with initial audience reactions largely positive. However, the ticket-window receipts were underwhelming for a movie of this scale and ambitions. For a movie as per reports budgeted at ₹ 1600-2000 crore rupees, an opening weekend of ₹ 507 crore rupees was slightly below par.

Meanwhile, But Ramayana turned it around in the post-Diwali break. Making use of the Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj breaks, the movie returned extraordinary figures on Monday and Tuesday, easily moving past the ₹ 800 crore rupees mark worldwide and gaining much-needed momentum both in the domestic market and overseas.

Notably, On Tuesday, Ramayana collected a staggering ₹ 94 crore rupees net in India, obliterating Baahubali 2’s ₹ 59 crore rupees record by a wide margin. The movie saw several houseful shows across India and recorded occupancy figures exceeding 80% for all night shows nationwide. This comes after the movie collected ₹ 107 crore rupees net on Monday, giving it a combined ₹ 200 crore rupees domestic haul after its four-day opening weekend. After six days in theatres, Ramayana has now collected ₹ 440 crore rupees net ( ₹ 526 crore rupees gross) at the Indian ticket-window.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

In further updates, The issue with Ramayana was its overseas earnings. Sony Pictures distributed the movie internationally, giving it a rollout in 59,000 screens worldwide, almost six times the size of any big Indian rollout. Yet the movie opened to $12.2 million in North America and barely crossed $11 million in other markets. But here, too, the tide turned on Monday and continued to turn on Tuesday. In the US, Ramayana bridged the gap with Godzilla Minus Zero, despite playing in less than half the screens. It is estimated to have made close to $3 million in the US across both days, not far behind Minus Zero’s $4 million haul in the same period. As of now, Ramayana has collected $31.7 million in the overseas markets. This takes the movie’s worldwide gross to ₹ 823 crore rupees after six days.

On top of that, It seems absurd now that just a few days ago, Ramayana was lagging behind Adipurush in daily earnings. Now, it is surpassing the lifetime earnings of all-time blockbusters with each passing day. On Monday, the movie beat SS Rajamouli’s Baahubali The Beginning ( ₹ 650 crore rupees). On Tuesday, as another record-breaking day saw it surpass the ₹ 700-crore rupees and ₹ 800-crore rupees marks, Ramayana also moved past the final collections of huge hits like Rajinikanth’s 2.0 ( ₹ 691 crore rupees), Aamir Khan’s PK ( ₹ 769 crore rupees), and Vicky Kaushal’s Chhaava ( ₹ 807 crore rupees).

Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part is running in theatres, while the second part is set for a Diwali 2028 rollout.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star-comedian Vir Das has flagged the bursting of firecrackers in public spaces in Mumbai despite the High Court's prohibition. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), he questioned how long people will continue to flout the rules. The Mumbai Police responded to his post and escalated the issue to the Bandra Police Station.

Adding to this, Mumbai Police responded to an X post made by Vir Das regarding firecracker use. Vir Das questions public bursting of firecrackers in Mumbai On Tuesday evening, Vir took to his X account and wrote, “Crackers still happening right outside Joggers park. At what point do we as citizens take the orders of the @mybmc and @MumbaiPolice seriously?” The official account of Mumbai Police responded, writing, “We have informed the Senior Officials of @BandraPS.” He reacted to them with folded-hands emojis.

Meanwhile, In another post, Vir even joked, “The year 2037. We are all ruled by AI. At 10.55pm when you are still bursting crackers it disables your phones and the electricity in your house. You call AI anti national and ask it why it only lectures you once a year. It doesn’t listen, says a law is a law and you are 55 minutes over. You spend the night in darkness. Could happen.”

Notably, Vir also reacted to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) banning the use of rockets and aerial firecrackers in Mumbai till November 25. It came after major fire incidents caused by bursting firecrackers at various locations, according to the Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB). Reacting to a Hindustan Times post about the same, he wrote on X with sarcasm, “Well. This should work. It’s been so effective thus far.”

As per the latest buzz, Late in October, the BMC reminded citizens of the HC's prohibition on bursting crackers in public spaces. Calling for an ‘eco-friendly’ Diwali, they urged people to avoid bursting firecrackers as they cause air and noise pollution that leads to health hazards. The BMC also urged people to opt for green crackers. Actors Gurfateh Pirzada and Divyanka Tripathi opened up that they of late experienced house fires caused by firecrackers. Divyanka's apartment guard died due to smoke suffocation.

In further updates, This year, Vir made his directorial debut with Happy Patel : Khatarnak Jasoos. The star also wrote and produced the movie, which was also backed by Aamir Khan. The movie received lukewarm reviews and collected ₹ 7 crore rupees worldwide, according to the trade website Sacnilk. The movie tells the story of the adopted son of two gay British agents who aspires to follow in his fathers’ footsteps. When he’s finally sent on a mission, he finds himself in trouble.
On top of that, Vir currently has stand-up comedy shows scheduled for India, the UK and the US.

Despite having a Master's degree in Journalism and over a decade of experience in print and digital media as a field reporter and sub-editor at organisations such as The Times of India and Reader's Digest, Neeshita Nyayapati remains a movie buff first and a Chief Content Producer second. She fell in love with movies in childhood and believes nothing matches the magic of watching a good movie that moves you with a warm tub of popcorn in hand. title: Salman Khan's next film director Vamshi Paidipally says he knows the stress and sacrifice actor went through for Maatrubhumi
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

On Tuesday evening, the trailer for Apoorva Lakhia’s Salman Khan -starrer Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace was finally rolled out, a few days after it was launched in Mumbai. The movie, which underwent an overhaul, will see Salman play an Indian Army soldier. The director of his next movie, Vamshi Paidipally, remarked on how he knew the sacrifices the star made and the stress he went through for the movie.

Adding to this, Salman Khan and Vamshi Paidipally are working together in a yet-to-be-titiled movie. Vamshi Paidipally on Salman Khan and Maatrubhumi On Tuesday evening, Salman rolled out the trailer of Maatrubhumi and wrote on X (formerly Twitter), “Aaj rollout karoon ya kal? Jo kal kare so aaj kar, Jo aaj kare so ab. (Should I rollout it today or tomorrow? Do tomorrow's work today, and today's work right now.) Enjoy the trailer.” Vamshi re-shared his post, writing, “#Maatrubhumi.. The Wait is over…”

Meanwhile, “@BeingSalmanKhan Sir... I know the sacrifices you made and the stress that you have gone through for this movie...Your Strength and Commitment shine through... Wishing You all the Love, Peace & Success You truly deserve Sir…” the director further wrote, adding, “Wishing @LakhiaApoorva @IChitrangda and the whole Team the Best of Everything..”

Notably, Vamshi and Salman are working together for the yet-to-be-titled SVC63, which also stars Nayanthara in the lead role. The movie, produced by Dil Raju, will see Anil Kapoor and Jackie Shroff in key roles.

As per the latest buzz, Maatrubhumi was initially conceptualised as Battle of Galwan and was supposed to be based on the aftermath of the 2020–2021 China–India skirmishes. Salman was cast as Colonel B Santosh Babu, and shooting took place last year. Anoop Bikram Shahi, Chitrangada Singh , and others were also roped in for key roles. However, the movie’s story was eventually changed, along with the title, and the team underwent reshoots.

In further updates, “This narrative that we are going against China or that our government has pressured us to change the script or rewrite it…this is all nonsense. It’s not true at all,” Salman shared at the trailer launch of late, further explaining, “We have made a movie about soldiers and what they and their families go through. We have shown that side and this side too. So, there are no negative forces here. Only their circumstances are such. And for these soldiers, the nation comes first. They like each other, but when a situation arises, both sides try to resolve it.”
On top of that, Maatrubhumi is scheduled to be rolled out in theatres on December 4.

title: Rohit Shetty warns fans against fake Facebook, X accounts after post on Gaurav Gupta's Bigg Boss 20 roast circulates online
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Rohit Shetty has issued a clarification after a Facebook post attributed to him began circulating online, leading many to believe that he had commented on comedian Gaurav Gupta's roast of Bigg Boss 20 contestants Scout OP and Love Gill. The filmmaker has clarified that he is not on Facebook or X and that Instagram is his only official social media platform.

Adding to this, Rohit Shetty shared Instagram is his only official social media platform. (Sunil Khandare) Rohit Shetty warns followers against fake account Rohit posted on Instagram to warn followers against fake accounts impersonating him on other platforms. He urged people not to engage with such profiles or consider the content shared through them as his own.

Meanwhile, In his statement, he wrote, "I would like to clarify that my only official social media presence is on Instagram. I am not present on Facebook or X. Any account or profile claiming to be me on these platforms is fake and unauthorised. I request everyone to not engage with such accounts or consider any content posted through them as coming from me. Thank you for your understanding and continued support."

Notably, The clarification came after a Facebook post, seemingly discussing Gaurav Gupta's roast of Bigg Boss 20 contestants Scout OP and Love Gill, began circulating online. The post read, "Friendly roasting theek hai par roasting ke naam par kisi ka mazaak udaana band hona chahiye. Hansana achhi baat hai, lekin kisi ko rulakar ya insult karke hansna nahi. Respect everyone (Friendly roasting is fine, but making fun of someone under the guise of 'roasting' needs to stop. It’s good to make people laugh, but not at the expense of making someone cry or by insulting them)."
As per the latest buzz, Many social media users believed the post was written by Rohit, prompting the filmmaker to set the record straight.

In further updates, Of late, comedian Gaurav Gupta appeared on the Diwali-special episode of Bigg Boss 20, hosted by Salman Khan. During the episode, he took playful digs at several contestants, including Scout OP(real name Tanmay Singh) and Love Gill. However, some of his jokes, particularly those concerning their personal lives and relationships, did not go down well with the contestants.

On top of that, Rohit Shetty is gearing up for Golmaal 5, the fifth instalment of his popular comedy franchise. The movie stars Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Tusshar Kapoor, Shreyas Talpade, Kunal Kemmu and Sharman Joshi, with Akshay Kumar joining the franchise. The filmmaker has revealed January 8, 2027, as its theatrical rollout date. The movie marks the return of the Golmaal gang nearly a decade after Golmaal Again (2017).

title: Arun Govil says he was pressured to play Lakshman to Jeetendra's Ram in Lav Kush against his wishes, recalls film 'didn't even run for one day'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

To a generation, Arun Govil is the personification of Lord Rama . The star played Rama in Ramanand Sagar’s seminal TV show Ramayan, which aired from 1987-88. The show made Arun a household name, forever linking him to the image of Lord Rama. Even as the star tried to diversify, typecasting brought him back to the mythological fold. The best example of this is the 1997 movie Lav Kush, in which he played Lakshman.

Adding to this, Arun Govil (L) and Jeetendra (R) played Lakshmana and Rama respectively in Lav Kush. Arun Govil recalls playing Lakshman in Lav Kush In a recent interview, the veteran star opened up that he never wanted to do the movie, as he didn’t feel right about playing Lakshman, having previously done a memorable job as Lord Rama. In fact, Arun believes that ineffective casting was one of the reasons the movie flopped.

Meanwhile, “In the movie Lav Kush, where Jeetendra played Rama, they wanted me as Lakshman. I had told the producer it's not right; don't make me play the character of Lakshman, but they did not listen. They wanted me. I shared, ‘Okay, let's do it.’ But then, look what happened. The movie didn't even run for one day. Nobody knows about that movie,” Arun Govil told Variety India in an interview.

Notably, Produced by Dilip Kanikaria under the Devyank Arts banner and directed by V. Madhusudhana Rao, Lav Kush starred Jeetendra as Lord Rama, Jaya Prada as Sita, Arun Govil as Lakshman, Dara Singh as Hanuman and Pran as Valmiki. Mounted on a massive budget, the movie rolled out on 25 July 1997 and proved to be a box-office disaster, earning only ₹ 43 lakh.

As per the latest buzz, Arun Govil believes that most followers see Lord Rama in him due to Ramayan’s enduring success. “Even today, people see me as Lord Rama. They even call me Ramji. They don't call me Arun Govil. Even today, in my constituency (he is a Member of Parliament in the Lok Sabha, representing the Meerut constituency), all the people address me as Ramji. And they also come with the thought: ‘You are Ramji, you tell us what to do.’ Even in the political field, whoever I meet, they believe, ‘We have come to you, now our work will get done’,” the star added.

In further updates, The veteran star returned to the world of Valmiki’s Ramayan for a third time this year as he appeared as King Dashrath, Lord Rama’s father, in Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana . The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Ramayana Part One is running in theatres and has minted over ₹ 600 crore rupees worldwide in just five days.

On top of that, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Maatrubhumi trailer out: Salman Khan heads to the battlefield, takes on Chinese troops with a message of peace
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Following much wait the entire day of November 10, Salman Khan unveiled the trailer of his soon-to-release movie Maatrubhumi : May War Rest in Peace around 10:30 pm. The star is ready to head to the battlefield as the trailer offered a look at a soldier caught in the middle of a tense conflict with Chinese troops.

Adding to this, Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi trailer ends with an unexpected 'bro' moment after intense India-China battle. Salman Khan launches the trailer of his movie Maatrubhumi After entire day's wait, Salman Khan dropped the trailer which shows him leading the charge as tensions between Indian and Chinese troops escalate. Amid the action, one exchange towards the end has already caught attention. The trailer also captures the emotional cost of leaving home. A senior officer reminds his team, “When soldiers leave, they don't say goodbye. They salute. Right? Yes, sir." A soldier preparing to leave for the frontlines says, “I'm heading out to the front. We’re on duty and have to leave in 10 minutes. Our son has his mother with him, and our mother has her son.”

Meanwhile, “Soldiers, remember this: bravery isn't always about fighting. It’s also about stopping a fight,” Salman's character tells the troops. However, in another scene, his orders are clear to the troops: “No matter what happens, not a single bullet will be fired from our side.”

Notably, The promo also questions the people who make decisions about war without facing its consequences. Towards the end, a soldier is described as "the best husband, the best father, and the best soul", while another reflects, "Why fear death? It has to come eventually." The trailer closes with its central message: "Humanity and patriotism aren't about wiping out the enemy. They are about wiping out the enmity." Facing a soldier from China, Salman signs off with, “Let's sort this s**t, bro. Peace out.”

As per the latest buzz, The movie, earlier titled Battle of Galwan , has been surrounded by speculation about its storyline and reported changes amid the improving relationship between India and China. It was initially scheduled to rollout in April, but questions about its narrative have continued to follow the project.

In further updates, At the trailer launch on November 6, Salman addressed speculation that the government had asked the makers to change or rewrite the movie's script. Dismissing the reports, he shared, "This whole narrative that we are going against China and that the government pressured us to change or rewrite the script is all nonsense."

On top of that, Clarifying the movie's subject, he added, "We've made a movie about soldiers and what they and their families go through." Salman also pointed out that the story does not paint either side as the villain. "It’s not true at all. We’ve made a movie about soldiers—about what they and their families go through, on both sides. There are no negative forces..." he shared.

The official logline reads: “Some battles are fought for victory. Some are fought for the future. And some remind us that the greatest victory is when war comes to an end. Presenting the official trailer of #Maatrubhumi : May War Rest in Peace, starring Salman Khan and Chitrangda Singh. A story of courage, sacrifice, humanity and the hope for a world where peace prevails.”

title: Ranveer Singh’s maternal grandfather Dr Ram Hingorani dies at 96 on Diwali; his cousin remembers him as a ‘rockstar’ who lived a glorious life
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Ranveer Singh ’s maternal grandfather, Dr Ram Hingorani, passed away at the age of 96 on Diwali. Sharing the news on social media, the star’s family member remembered him with love, choosing to celebrate the long and happy life he had lived. He breathed his last during Lakshmi Puja, on November 8.

Adding to this, Bollywood star Ranveer Singh’s maternal grandfather, Dr Ram Hingorani, passed away at the age of 96 on Diwali. Ranveer Singh's cousin confirms the death Saumya Hingorani , Ranveer’s cousin from his maternal side, shared several pictures and videos of her grandfather, whom the family lovingly called Dadu. Along with the memories, she penned an emotional note about his life, the time they spent together and how much he meant to everyone.

Meanwhile, Saumya wrote on Instagram on Tuesday night, “96 years young. A glorious life to be celebrated, not mourned ✨ My Dadu, Dr. Ram, peacefully left us on Diwali to go home to my Dadi. He couldn’t have picked a more auspicious time - the golden hour of the day, during Lakshmi Puja 🙏🏽 I bet the two of them are in their chairs sipping on a crisp whiskey, enjoying watching us together 🥰 Thank you for being the best Dadu in the world. Thank you for giving us everything ♥️ Save a scoop of icecream for me 🤗 Until we dance again 🤍Hari Om 🕊️.”

Notably, View this post on Instagram Ranveer Singh's memories of his 'rockstar' Nana Ranveer has often spoken about his love for his maternal grandfather, occasionally sharing pictures and videos that gave followers a glimpse of their bond. During the promotions of Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani in 2023, the star had posted a video of his grandfather dancing along to the movie's popular song What Jhumka. The star also shared pictures of the two together, with his nana wearing a Team Rocky T-shirt. At 93, he was clearly enjoying himself and even had a rather entertaining demand. “Leave tikki bring Tequila for me”, he shared in the video. Ranveer shared the pictures with the caption, “Nana is peak Rocky-ism! (bomb and fire emoticon) 93 and Rock(y)ing!!!”

As per the latest buzz, The star gave followers another glimpse of his grandfather's spirit during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Despite the heat, his 93-year-old nana made sure to step out and cast his vote. Ranveer shared a picture of him wearing a shirt, trousers and sunglasses, with a policeman helping him. He wrote, “93 yrs old. 93°F outside. But he voted. He’s a voter! My Rockstar Nana #EveryVoteCounts”.

In further updates, Of late, Ranveer and his star-wife, Deepika Padukone, shared the first glimpse of their second daughter, Devi, during Dussehra. The couple welcomed their first daughter, Dua, in September 2024.

On top of that, On the work front, Ranveer has been enjoying the success of the Dhurandhar franchise and is now preparing for his next movie, Pralay. Directed by Jai Mehta, the project is a survival thriller set in a post-apocalyptic Mumbai, where people are forced to fight for survival following a zombie outbreak.

The movie is particularly special for Ranveer as it marks his debut as a producer under his banner, Maa Kasam Films. He is backing the project alongside Birla Studios, led by Ananya Birla, and True Story Films, founded by Hansal Mehta and Sahil Saigal. Pralay went on floors in Mumbai in August 2026. The movie also stars Kalyani Priyadarshan and marks her debut in Hindi cinema.

title: ‘Today or tomorrow, Siang Dam will be built,’ says BJP MP amid protests in Arunachal Pradesh
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Arunachal East MP from BJP, Tapir Gao on Monday while addressing students of Indira Gandhi Government College (IGGC) at Tezu in Lohit district shared Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) will be constructed regardless of the ongoing opposition, saying the dam would become a reality “today or tomorrow”, even if it takes another generation.

Adding to this, Congress on Tuesday also questioned Union minister Kiren Rijiju over his alleged silence on several key issues concerning the state, including the issue of the proposed dam. (HT Photo) He shared that the protests were being driven by individuals harbouring political ambitions rather than genuine opposition from local communities.
Meanwhile, “The dam will be built anyhow, whether today or tomorrow. Even if it is not constructed in our generation, the Government of India will build it in the future,” Gao shared.

Notably, “People must understand that this project does not belong to the Arunachal Pradesh government or Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It was declared a national project in 2008 by the government led by Dr Manmohan Singh,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, Referring to the violence that erupted in Pasighat on October 23 protests, the MP criticised the alleged involvement of students under the banner of ‘Gen Z’ in vandalism and attacks on private properties. Gao shared that 92 people were arrested and that more than 100 others would face arrest. He shared minors detained were rolled out.

In further updates, Reacting sharply to Gao’s remarks, Adi Ba Kebang United (ABKU), in a letter to Commissioner (East) Amjad Tak on Tuesday, questioned the government’s contradictory positions on the proposed Siang dam.

On top of that, The organisation pointed out that chief minister Pema Khandu repeatedly assured that the dam would not be constructed without the consent of affected communities, while Gao and other elected representatives continued to insist that the project would be implemented.

“Whom should the people of Siang dam affected area and the people of Arunachal trust — the Chief Minister or the MP, Minister or his MLAs? There cannot be two contradictory statements from the same Govt!” it shared.

title: Anupam Kher says he felt proud as an Indian when audience got teary-eyed at Ramayana Sweden premiere, thanked him for voicing Jatayu
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash-starrer Ramayana: Part 1 was rolled out in theatres on November 5, right on time for Diwali. The movie, which had world premieres, received mixed reviews from critics but has performed well at the ticket-window. Anupam Kher , who dubbed for Jatayu, posted a video from the movie’s premiere in Stockholm, Sweden, stating that the audience left him overwhelmed with their reaction to watching the movie. The video he posted showed the audience shaking hands with him and interacting after the premiere.

Adding to this, Anupam Kher narrates Ramayana Part 1 as Jayatu. Anupam Kher on Ramayana’s Sweden premiere Anupam posted a long note on X (formerly Twitter) and Instagram, penning down his thoughts about the Stockholm premiere. “Extremely happy to share these visuals from the Swedish premiere of Ramayana: The Rise of Legend in Stockholm. I began my speech with a sentence in Swedish: “Jag är mycket glad att vara här i Stockholm i kväll.” — “I am very happy to be here in Stockholm this evening.” And I truly was. After 41 years and 556 films in India, it was also special to share that I have become a small part of Swedish cinema for the first time with Out of Fashion,” he wrote.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Anupam Kher (@anupampkher)

title: Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra not worried about recovering Rs-4000-crore budget through box office; plans to make money through merch, theme parks
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana , or as it is internationally titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, rolled out in theatres on November 5 ahead of Diwali 2026. Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, the movie opened on a decent note but picked up momentum as the first weekend concluded. With the two-part epic, mounted on a whopping ₹ 4000 crore rupees budget, one would think that producer Namit Malhotra would be stressed about how the movie will fare at the ticket-window. However, that does not seem to be the case. The producer is looking beyond ticket sales for his ambitious two-part adaptation and believes there are several ways to make the massive investment work.

Adding to this, Ramayana ticket-window pressure? Namit Malhotra reveals why he isn't worried about the movie's ₹4,000 crore rupees budget. (AFP) What Namit Malhotra had to say about the ticket-window earnings While the scale of the movie is massive, Namit is confident that the Ramayana has enough potential to find an audience across different formats. In an interview with CNN, the producer shared, “I'm not motivated by the bean-counter logic of, ‘How much money did we make or not make'. If we don’t make money with the movies, we’ll make it in the merchandise. If we don’t make it in the merchandise, we’ll make it in the theme park. If we don’t make it in the theme park, we’ll make it some other way.”

Meanwhile, During an earlier conversation with the same publication, he spoke about the movie with the conviction of someone who believes the story itself gives the project a strong foundation. "I don’t want to sound spiritual as a businessman," he shared. “But honestly … you can’t do this right and not succeed. To me, there’s one fundamental truth: that if we do ‘Ramayana’ well, and if people like it, financially we’ll be fine. That's my fundamental belief. There’s no way to argue it. There’s no way to debate it. And I don’t think anybody in the world is smart enough to counter it with scientific or commercial logic.”

Notably, It is not the first time he has spoken about the adaptation and that he has several plans for the epic. At the movie's Telugu pre-rollout event in Hyderabad, he explained that the larger ambition was always to create something that could continue engaging audiences long after the two films have been rolled out.

As per the latest buzz, He had shared, “The word Ramayana, as we all know, is really a philosophy. It is a word that we have grown up with. All of us have, from our fathers, our grandfathers, our multi-generations have known the story of an epic called the Ramayana. When we were conceiving this, this was not meant to be just a movie. This was meant to be much more than that.”

In further updates, He added that the intention is not to bring the story to a close after two films but to use them as a starting point for exploring the larger world of the epic: “The idea is not to make one or two movies and stop the journey of Rama. In fact, it is to start this journey. On the back of this movie, we can actually start to open up the different areas of engagement.”

On top of that, At the same event, the producer had also presented a behind-the-scenes video that offered a glimpse into the proposed expansion of the Ramayana universe. The plans include video games based on the epic, along with merchandise spanning apparel, toys, gadgets and home furnishings.

The team is also looking at developing spin-off stories through origin films, television shows and animated projects. The plans include theme park experiences and a Broadway musical adaptation. Virtual reality, augmented reality and metaverse experiences are also part of the larger vision.

title: Arun Govil didn't want to play Dashrath in Ramayana, says Nitesh Tiwari wanted a connection with Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

When Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana was revealed four years ago, everyone knew it would be compared with Ramanand Sagar’s TV adaptation of the epic from the 80s. The show remains the most-watched Indian TV show of all time and set the benchmark for how the epic is to be adapted. Perhaps that is why director Nitesh Tiwari pulled off a casting coup when he cast Ramayan’s OG Lord Rama, Arun Govil , as King Dashrath in his movie. In a recent interview, Arun Govil opened up that he did not initially want to play King Dashrath and was only won over by the director’s insistence.

Adding to this, Arun Govil as King Dashrath in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Arun Govil didn’t want to play Dashrath Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, with Arun Govil essaying the role of his father, Ayodhya’s King Dashratha. Talking about taking on the role, the star told Variety India, “Had I felt it wasn't right, I would not have done it. To be honest, initially, I didn't want to do this role. But Nitesh Tiwari, the director, was insistent. They wanted some connect between our Ramayan and this Ramayana.”

Meanwhile, Ramayana has received great reviews and has already minted over ₹ 660 crore rupees worldwide in five days, one of the best starts for an Indian movie ever. While Ranbir Kapoor’s performance has been lauded, many viewers have still compared it unfavourably with Arun Govil’s portrayal. The star addressed the comparisons and the criticism coming Ranbir’s way, “That perhaps is also because my performance as Lord Rama became the touchstone. It is still alive in the hearts and minds of people. Nobody wants to see another Rama. You know, my Ramayan keeps playing somewhere or the other at any given time. Even today in North and Central India, whenever there are melas and tamashas and photos of Rama are sold, they have my face on them. So, for me, to talk about an star's performance as Lord Rama doesn’t feel right,” he added.

Notably, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first part of a duology. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Part 1 is running in theatres, while part 2 is scheduled for rollout in 2028.

title: Mahabharat star Nitish Bharadwaj goes from predicting Oscar for Ramayana to criticising it, says film misrepresents India's history
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nitish Bharadwaj , who played Lord Krishna in BR Chopra's iconic 1988 television series Mahabharat , was among the first celebrities to praise Ramayana after its trailer was rolled out. The star even predicted that the movie would win an Oscar. However, Nitish changed his stance after watching the movie and went on to criticise the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer, saying it misrepresents India's history and heritage.

Adding to this, Mahabharat star Nitish Bharadwaj criticised Ramayana. ‘The movie alters the moral framework of Ramayana’ The star expressed his disappointment with the makers' portrayal of Ravana, played by Yash, as a fair and socially just character. According to him, this changes the moral framework of the epic.

Meanwhile, He wrote on Instagram, "The Ramayan is not just a story. It is deeply rooted in the civilizational and spiritual consciousness of Sanatan Bharat. Its heroes, heroine and antagonist are integral to the values and message of this Mahakavya. Their character and significance cannot be casually redefined. Mahavishnu took the Ram Avatar to uphold Dharma, parampara and establish Maryada. By presenting Ravan as an exceptionally liberal, socially just and fair figure, the movie, in my view, alters the moral framework of the Ramayan and undermines the very purpose of avataar."

Notably, Nitish also pointed out that impressive visual effects cannot substitute for the core values of the epic. He further opened up that he was withdrawing his earlier social media post in which he had lauded the movie after watching its trailer.

As per the latest buzz, He wrote, "I am deeply upset and disappointed with this movie. I withdraw my earlier post about it. I cannot find a single good word to say about it. A spectacle of VFX can never substitute for the core values, philosophical depth and spiritual essence of this Mahakavya. This movie, in my opinion, does not deserve to represent Indian cinema internationally when its narrative misrepresents Bharat's history, heritage and core spiritual values."
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nitish Bharadwaj (@nitishbharadwaj.krishna)

On top of that, Earlier, after watching the movie's trailer, Nitish had taken to social media to praise the makers and predict a major international recognition for the movie. He had written, "100% Oscar for Best Foreign Movie. Nitesh Tiwari is Bharat's next gift to world cinema after Satyajit Rai and Shekhar Kapoor. Tens of awards for Production Design and DOP. Wonderful period creation using VFX and AI. Thanks to the great music maestro Hans Zimmer for collaborating with Indian cinema. Ranbir now at par with Ranveer as the next two unbeatable Dhurandhars. Yash — welcome to global cinema."

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Produced by Namit Malhotra, the two-part epic features music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. The first instalment was rolled out in theatres on November 5, 2026, with the second part scheduled to arrive in 2028.

title: ₹156 crore on a Monday, beating Dhurandhar 2, outpacing Pushpa 2: Ramayana's incredible box office comeback in numbers
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Mondays are traditionally not a movie’s best friend at the ticket-window. Most films around the world rollout on Fridays and do their best business over the weekend. Mondays are when the collections drop. Over the last few years, with shorter theatrical runs, the Monday tests have become sharper and the drops bigger. That is why whenever a movie earns big on Monday, it is a sign of a healthy lifetime run. Of course, it is easier for word of mouth to propel smaller films like The Kashmir Files or Hanuman Ansh , but every once in a while, a movie like Ramayana comes along. The Nitesh Tiwari movie made the most of post-Diwali holidays to mount the biggest Monday ever seen in Indian cinema history, with a collection so gargantuan that it dwarfed even the Baahubalis and Dhurandhars of the world.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana’s manic Monday On Monday, its fifth day in theatres, Ramayana finally breathed free as the Diwali festivities ended, but the holidays did not. The movie saw a spectacular 91% jump in domestic collections. It collected ₹ 107.50 crore rupees net in India on the day, a new record for Mondays. Prior to this, the record belonged to Baahubali 2, which collected ₹ 80 crore rupees net in all languages on its first Monday.

Meanwhile, In Bollywood, the record belonged to Dhurandhar 2, which collected ₹ 60 crore rupees net on its first Monday earlier this year. Ramayana took that record, too. However, both Baahubali 2 and Dhurandhar 2 had their first Monday hauls on a non-holiday. Ramayana benefitted from the Govardhan Puja holiday on its first Monday. The previous festive Monday record for an Indian movie was held by Salman Khan’s Tiger 3. The 2023 movie collected ₹ 58 crore rupees net on Diwali, a Monday.

Notably, Pushpa 2: The Rule emerged as the biggest opening movie in Indian cinema history in 2024. On its rollout day, the Allu Arjun smash hit raked in ₹ 164 crore rupees net in India. During the day, the movie sold 1.07 lakh tickets per hour on BookMyShow. It remained the only movie to have a lakh tickets per hour on the platform till Dhurandhar 2 joined in this year. Ramayana beat both these films on Monday. Around noon, the movie was selling 1.4 lakh tickets per hour, a new record for BookMyShow.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by BookMyShow (@bookmyshowin)

In further updates, Ramayana collected ₹ 107.50 crore rupees net ( ₹ 131 crore rupees gross) in India on Monday, its single-largest collection since rollout. Overseas, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer did not have the benefit of a post-Diwali holiday, but it still brought in $2.7 million from international markets. This gave the movie a single-day haul of ₹ 156 crore rupees on Monday, one of the highest for any Indian movie on a non-rollout weekday.

title: Yash wore Ravana costumes weighing up to 33 kg in Ramayana; crown alone weighed 1.8 kg, reveals designer
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The making of an epic mythological movie is always challenging, especially when it is based on a Hindu epic like the Ramayana . Costumes play an important role in bringing such characters to life and convincing audiences of their portrayal. In a recent interaction, costume stylist and designer Saniya Sardhariya spoke about Yash’s elaborate look as Ravana , revealing that the star had to wear costumes weighing between 16 and 20 kg. On some days, the costumes weighed as much as 30–33 kg.

Adding to this, Yash played the role of Ravana in Ramayana. 'Most of the costumes used to weigh around 16 to 20 kg' In conversation with India Today, Saniya shared, "Most of the costumes used to weigh around 16 to 20 kg, including the jewellery. But we had a few heavy pieces, like the Ravana look associated with Lanka, his wedding costume, and the costume he wore for Surpanakha's wedding. Those were close to 30–33 kg, if I remember correctly."

Meanwhile, Saniya admitted that the most difficult part of designing Ravana's costume was his crown. She opened up that despite several attempts to reduce its weight, the crown eventually weighed 1.8 kg.

Notably, She shared, “I think the most difficult part was wearing the crown because any amount of weight on your head feels very restrictive and heavy. So, we experimented a lot with the idea. We had so many mock 3D crowns made, and we ensured that we got the design right first. Then we started reverse-engineering it to see how we could make it lighter and lighter. But I don't think we could go any lighter than 1.8 kg. That was the best we could do, and even that felt like a lot. You don't see that in his expressions or anything like that, but it was quite a task.”

As per the latest buzz, She also spoke about how the elaborate costumes restricted the star's movements. Despite the physical discomfort and long hours, however, Yash took it in his stride and often amused those around him. Saniya recalled that the star soon realised how draining the experience would be. To entertain himself and playfully tease the team, he would turn the sharp elements of his costume into everyone's problem.

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Produced by Namit Malhotra, the movie features music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. The first part is scheduled for a Diwali 2026 rollout, while the second part is expected to arrive in 2028.

title: Ramayana actor Indira Krishnan defends Sai Pallavi’s Sita wielding a sword, admits she ‘didn’t connect’ it with what she saw in Ramanand Sagar show
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sai Pallavi’s portrayal of Sita in Ramayana has sparked a debate, with some viewers questioning the decision to show the character participating in combat and wielding a sword. Of late, Indira Krishnan , who plays Kaushalya in the movie, reacted to the discussion and admitted that she, too, found it difficult to connect with this aspect of Sita’s character. However, she also explained why the makers chose to portray Sita as a warrior.

Adding to this, Sai Pallavi plays Sita in Ramayana. ‘I couldn’t connect this bit of Sita’s character’ In the movie, Pallavi is seen wielding a sword during a forest encounter with the demon army led by Khara and Dushana. In conversation with News18, Indira shared, “I would also go with the audience. As a child, when I watched Ramayan, I never saw Sita as a warrior. I couldn’t connect this bit with what I had watched in the old television show."

Meanwhile, Explaining why the makers decided to portray Sita as a warrior, she added, “The makers wanted to portray that Sita isn’t weak. She belonged to a family of warriors who made sure that the girl child learned the art of wielding a sword. Through the sequence, they’ve depicted the valour of Sita, who was otherwise soft-minded."

Notably, Indira explained that Sita wasn’t the only female character whose strength was highlighted in the movie. The makers wanted to show that every woman has her own strength. Talking about her character, Kaushalya, Indira shared she did not portray a mother who was always sad. Instead, she played Kaushalya as someone who is emotionally strong and confident.

As per the latest buzz, She also pointed out that the movie explores the lesser-known side of Kaikasi, Ravana’s mother, who was herself a warrior. The star admitted that this aspect of Kaikasi surprised everyone.
In further updates, Speaking at the movie’s Pratham Sankalp event in New Delhi in July, Pallavi opened up about playing Sita and shared she felt blessed to have been offered the role.

On top of that, “It's not easy for actors to get roles like this. Because it's not easy to play a Goddess. There must be a team putting their heart and soul into making it the best version. I don't think I chose to play Sita maa. I was blessed to play this role. It's not something that you can go after and not something you can write down and say, this is how I want to play. I would sit and meditate and say, Sita maa, you act through me. Whatever comes through me is what you want for the movie,” she shared.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is being made as a two-part cinematic adaptation of the epic, with the first instalment releasing in theatres worldwide on November 5, 2026. The second part is slated to rollout in 2028.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 5: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film crosses ₹660 crore after manic Monday; beats Baahubali, Jailer lifetime hauls
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana has finally had that red-letter day that a movie of that scale should have. On Monday, its fifth day in theatres, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer became the second Hindi movie to net over ₹ 100 crore rupees at the domestic ticket-window in a single day. Add to that an impressive showing overseas, and Ramayana had a manic Monday, enabling it to get back on track in recovering its costs.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama in the movie Ramayana Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer opened to great reviews on Thursday, with initial audience reactions largely positive. Yet that did not drive footfall momentum very strongly. The movie collected ₹ 128 crore rupees worldwide on its rollout day. By the end of its extended four-day opening weekend, the movie had reached ₹ 500 crore rupees worldwide. However, for a movie as per reports budgeted at ₹ 1600-2000 crore rupees, this was a slightly underwhelming figure. That changed on Monday. The post-Diwali break in India meant that Ramayana saw a breakneck pace of ticket sales. It raked in ₹ 107.50 crore rupees net in India on the day. The highest ever by a movie not named Dhurandhar: The Revenge. As word of mouth lifted Ramayana on Monday, it registered its biggest day and Bollywood’s biggest Monday ever. This enabled it to reach ₹ 346 crore rupees net ( ₹ 413 crore rupees gross) domestically.

Meanwhile, The issue with Ramayana has been its overseas earnings. Sony Pictures distributed the movie internationally, giving it a rollout in 59,000 screens worldwide, almost six times the size of any big Indian rollout. Yet the movie opened to $12.2 million in North America and barely crossed $11 million in other markets. On Monday, with no Diwali off outside India, the movie faced a minor drop in earnings. It has now collected $26.7 million in overseas territories, a steadily rising figure.
Notably, This takes Ramayana’s worldwide gross to ₹ 663 crore rupees after five days. With the Bhai Dooj holiday on Tuesday, the movie could see another bumper day in India.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana had been lagging behind Adipurush for its first three days before easily overtaking it on Diwali. On Monday, as it added a staggering ₹ 156 crore rupees worldwide, Ramayana entered the list of the 25 highest-grossing Indian films ever. It climbed 13 spots in a single day, overtaking some all-time blockbusters such as Rajinikanth’s Jailer ( ₹ 605 crore rupees), Salman Khan’s Sultan ( ₹ 621 crore rupees), and SS Rajamouli’s Baahubali The Beginning ( ₹ 650 crore rupees).

title: Ramayana's Urmila, Sonia Balani, says she wasn't worried about less screen time, is 'okay to be part of something big'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Sonia Balani had a small part in the of late rolled out epic Ramayana . The star plays Urmila, Sita’s sister and Lakshman’s wife. But while the epic gives Urmila a significant role, the movie cut almost all of her sequences from the final product, giving Sonia just a minor cameo with no lines. The star, however, isn’t too sad about it.

Adding to this, Sonia Balani (R) with Sai Pallavi in a still from Ramayana. Sonia Balani on playing Urmila In Valmiki’s Ramayan, Urmila is the younger daughter of Mithila’s King Janaka, sister to Sita. After Lord Rama wins Sita’s hand in the swayamvar, he expresses his wish that his brothers be also married at the same time. That is how Lakshman marries Urmila. However, when Rama is exiled by Kaikeyi, Lakshman accompanies him, leaving Urmila behind in Ayodhya for 14 years. In an interview with India Today, Sonia talked about her character’s strength. “It's one of the biggest sacrifices that we have known about. Being a woman of today's generation, it's beyond my imagination. I am yet to fathom how she found that strength. I just can't imagine anyone making such a big sacrifice, that too, right after getting married,” the star shared.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sonia Balani (@soniabalani9)

Notably, Valmiki’s Ramayan gives Urmila some scope and character growth. She confronts Lakshman for leaving her in Ayodhya, but also agrees with her husband when he says he is duty-bound to serve his brother. According to the epic, Urmila sleeps for 14 years, day and night, allowing Lakshman to stay awake all those years and protect Rama and Sita during the vanvaas.

As per the latest buzz, These episodes are not part of Ramayana Part 1. But Sonia shared she learnt from her character’s tendency to never try and be the ‘main character’. The star added, “I feel she made every sacrifice with a smile on her face, and she never wanted to be the main character in her own story. That's really my takeaway. Sometimes, it's okay to be part of something big and be happy with what you have done. You have done it with your best intentions and the best energy. Sometimes, it's about greater things that we can't see right in the moment.”

title: Assamese craftsmen who created Ranbir Kapoor, Ravie Dubey's armour never knew it was for Ramayana, worked 3 years on cane-rubber armour
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Traditional cane craftsmanship from a remote village in Assam’s Barpeta district has found a prominent place on the silver screen in Nitesh Tiwari’s newly rolled out mythological epic Ramayana , starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor wearing Assam's handmade cane-rubber armour in Ramayana. 15 artisans worked for over three years Master artisan Jaynal Abdin, a resident of Jania Banglipara village in Barpeta district, led a 15-member local team over a span of three-and-a-half years to handcraft 30 to 35 pieces of the specialised cane-and-rubber armour featured in the movie.

Meanwhile, In conversation with ANI, Abdin recalled that the project first reached him around three-and-a-half years ago through Abdul Malek of the local organisation Gram Unnayan in Jania, rather than directly from the movie’s production house. "It did not come to me directly. It first came to Abdul Malek ji of Gram Unnayan here in Jania. He called me over, shared a project had come in, and asked me to take a look. They had sent a file initially containing the drawings and designs. After examining it, I shared it could be done and discussed it with my team head. Soon after, five to six members from their team arrived here, and a member named Sagar stayed back with us to help oversee the measurements and corrections," Abdin told ANI.

Notably, Crafting wearable armour out of stiff cane for high-intensity movie sequences posed significant technical hurdles. Abdin shared that the initial prototype had minor fitting issues around the neck and shoulders and was returned with markings for alteration. Once refitted and tried on the lead star, the pure cane structure proved too rigid and tight for comfortable movement.

As per the latest buzz, "After we fixed the initial cuts, they made the main star of the movie wear it, and he shared it was very hard and tight—which cane naturally is. They asked what alternative material could be used. I told them we could craft it out of whatever material they provided. They sent us black and green rubber, but weaving with rubber alone was not working. When I spoke to costume designer Ajay, I suggested using half cane and half rubber. He agreed and asked us to make one sample," Abdin explained.
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by The World Of Ramayana (@worldoframayana)

On top of that, Once the hybrid cane-and-rubber design was approved, the artisans worked intermittently over three to three-and-a-half years under tight deadlines whenever the production schedule demanded fresh pieces. To meet urgent shooting requirements in Mumbai, finished armour jackets were rushed directly from Barpeta to Guwahati Airport.

"They gave me the contact number of a person at Guwahati Airport and told me to simply hand the jackets over to him. I would go to the airport, hand it over, and within two to three hours they would call to confirm they had received it. The work was not continuous; sometimes there would be no news for three to six months, and then suddenly a call would come asking for eight or ten pieces on very short notice before shooting resumed. In total, over three to three-and-a-half years, we sent around 30 to 35 pieces," he shared.

title: Amyra Dastur says Farah Khan almost made her cry by saying the actor will ‘ruin her career’ with how she danced on Kung Fu Yoga set
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Farah Khan visited star Amyra Dastur 's Mumbai residence for the latest episode of her YouTube channel. The star welcomed her and the two of them recalled memories of working together on the set of the movie Kung Fu Yoga. Farah had choreographed a song called Goosebump, which had Amyra in it. The star shared how she was intimidated by Farah and then there was one moment when she almost made her cry on set.

Adding to this, Farah Khan had a priceless reaction as Amyra Dastur shared the memory with her. Why did Farah make Amyra cry? Amyra recalled what happened on set and shared, “Farah has a very good sense of humour but I did not know that. I had only heard that Farah ma'am will yell at you so don't mess up… Then she comes at me and she says, ‘Congratulations!’ So I thought I was doing such a good job. She shared, ‘You are going to be my Titanic and ruin my career!’”

Meanwhile, Farah looked surprised and laughed at this recollection, and shared that whoever has got some yelling has done well in their career! Amyra agreed to that statement and shared that Farah has also yelled at Boman Irani on the set of Happy New Year. Farah recalled how Boman was trying to get in character, but it was making her think he had gone into a coma. She asked him, "Will you do something or will you stay in coma?" Farah added that Boman got up and told her he was trying to stay in character.

Notably, Kung Fu Yoga was rolled out in 2017. It was an action-adventure comedy movie written and directed by Stanley Tong. It also starred Sonu Sood and Disha Patani. It was the first movie made under the India-China co-production treaty.

Adding to this, Now, with the holiday season kicking in, audiences are heading to cinemas in huge numbers. This has created capacity issues at several properties. title: Kumar Vishwas calls writing lyrics for Ramayana a divine experience, shares BTS video with AR Rahman and Shreya Ghoshal
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramayana has been receiving praise from viewers ever since it rolled out in theatres ahead of Diwali. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash in the lead roles. The movie's lyricist, Kumar Vishwas, has now penned a heartfelt note on the journey of being part of the process from the very beginning. He shared that Ramayana felt as if God chose him for this journey.

Adding to this, Ramayana rolled out in theatres on November 5. The lyricist has written for all the songs that were composed by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. He shared a BTS video where the team was present inside the studio to collaborate on the songs and find the correct tune for each and every part. It showed the hours of dedication and hard work that went into creating the songs. Namit Malhotra, Nitesh Tiwari, Shreya Ghoshal and Vishal Dadlani were also seen in the BTS footage.

Meanwhile, In the caption, Kumar wrote, “Sometimes, I believe God chooses you for certain journeys Himself. Ramayana has never been just a movie for me. I believe it is the blessing of all these years of devotion, faith, and surrender to Shri Ram. Thank you, Bhagwan Ram for choosing me to be a small part of something so extraordinary. What an experience it has been to work alongside some of the greatest creative minds of our time, to witness this vision come alive, and above all, to see the love with which you all have embraced my words.”

Notably, He thanked the makers and concluded, “To see you all not just listen to my lyrics, but feel them and understand even their deepest meanings, is a blessing beyond words.Some journeys are not planned. They are written for you by the divine. Jai Siya Ram.”

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. Ramayana is one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu (played by Ranbir Kapoor), and his battle against the asura king Ravana (played by Yash) after the latter abducts his wife, Sita (played by Sai Pallavi). The cast also includes Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The movie is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, with music by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer.

In further updates, As per reports mounted on a budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees, the movie is backed by Yash and Namit Malhotra and is planned as a two-part franchise. The first instalment is scheduled to rollout in theatres on November 5, 2026, with the second part expected to arrive around Diwali 2028.

title: Kunal Kohli slams residents for bursting loud firecrackers outside Mumbai hospital
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Director Kunal Kohli did not have a pleasant Diwali this year. The filmmaker of late took to social media to share how he had to take his mother to Mumbai's Khar Hinduja Hospital for emergency treatment on Diwali night. However, he was shocked to find people bursting loud firecrackers outside the hospital gate, seemingly with little regard for the patients inside.

Adding to this, Kunal Kohli slams residents for bursting loud firecrackers outside Mumbai hospital. Kunal Kohli calls out residents for bursting loud firecrackers outside Mumbai hospital In his post, Kunal mentioned that he even requested the residents not to burst loud crackers outside the hospital, but they paid no heed to him and continued with the celebrations. Tagging the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), Kunal wrote, "Took my mom for an emergency to Khar Hinduja hospital tonight, Diwali night. Sadly some residents were burning loud bombs just outside the hospital gate. I politely requested them to burn all crackers except loud bombs outside the hospital gates. A man told me ‘hospital galat jagah pe hai-hum yahan 40 saal se hain (Hospital is built at the wrong place, we have been here for the last 40 years)’ and he continued to burst loud bombs. @mybmc."

Meanwhile, Meanwhile, star Bhumi Pednekar also raised concerns over deteriorating air quality and the impact of firecracker celebrations. Taking to Instagram Stories, she shared, “Houses have caught fire, the AQI is hazardous, roads are full of waste, its 3 am and all I can hear are loud crackers. Our roads were full of people bursting crackers on them, out in the open, even when it’s not allowed. This is heartbreaking. @my bmc ®mumbaipolice."

Notably, She also shared another post on Monday morning, which read, “Diwali is a festival of light, love, family and new beginnings. But every year, along with the celebrations, comes a familiar aftermath: polluted air, firecracker waste, noise and frightened animals. Firecrackers rollout fine particulate matter and other pollutants that add to an already challenging air-quality situation. And the impact isn’t experienced equally. Children, older people, those with respiratory conditions and animals are particularly vulnerable. This year, let’s make a choice that allows everyone including the ones who cannot speak for themselves to enjoy the festival.”

As per the latest buzz, Firecracker celebrations on Diwali night led to a rise in pollution levels in several cities across the country. In Mumbai, nine of the city's 25 air quality monitoring stations recorded poor air quality on Monday morning. The city's overall Air Quality Index ( AQI ) stood at 171, placing it in the moderate category.

title: Gurfateh Pirzada furious at the ‘stupidity of masses’ on Diwali, says firecrackers burnt his entire balcony and a room
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Diwali celebrations in Mumbai led to numerous small fires caused by firecrackers. Star Gurfateh Pirzada , who was of late seen in Lust Stories 3, shared that the entire balcony of his Mumbai residence was burnt on Diwali eve after catching fire from bursting crackers. The star shared pictures of his room in Mumbai and tagged Mumbai police to raise concern about the situation.

Adding to this, Gurfateh Pirzada shared that parts of his Mumbai residence was affected by firecrackers. Gurfateh shares pictures of his room Taking to Instagram Stories, Gurfateh shared a picture of how his room looked after it was burnt due to crackers entering from the balcony situated just outside. Not even going to talk about what the domesticated animals and strays must have been through.”

title: Pankaj Tripathi recalls peeling onions and potatoes at hotel for 2 years before becoming an actor
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Pankaj Tripathi of late appeared on Kapil Sharma 's Netflix show, The Great Indian Kapil Show , along with Vikas Divyakirti and Zakir Khan. During the show, Pankaj spoke about his journey and the choices that shaped his career. He also made an interesting revelation about what he wanted to pursue before becoming an star.

Adding to this, Pankaj Tripathi recalls his humble beginnings at The Great Indian Kapil Show. Pankaj Tripathi recalls working at hotel before becoming an star When an audience member opened up that he was confused about his career, Kapil asked Pankaj if he had ever experienced similar uncertainty before getting into acting. The star then revealed, "Even I wanted to be a student leader, but the police beat me so badly, that day I changed my mind because I realised getting beaten up is involved in it. I even worked at a hotel for 2 years, while peeling onions and potatoes, I realised my desitny is something else and not this."

Meanwhile, When Navjot Singh Sidhu asked if he credited the OTT space for helping him grow, Pankaj shared, "I agree that OTT helped outsiders make a name for themselves. We all belong to ordinary families, but in this democratic space we got opportunities and worked hard to earn our places. This possibility exists for every kid in India, and of course new mediums emerge, so new opportunities open up."

Notably, After graduating from the National School of Drama in 2004, Pankaj Tripathi moved to Mumbai to pursue acting. He made his movie debut with a small role in Run in 2004, followed by appearances in films such as Omkara, Apaharan and Agneepath.

As per the latest buzz, His breakthrough came in 2012 with Anurag Kashyap's Gangs of Wasseypur, in which he played Sultan Qureshi. The performance brought him wider recognition and opened doors to projects such as Fukrey, Masaan, Bareilly Ki Barfi and Newton. He received a National Movie Award Special Mention for his performance as Atma Singh in Newton.

In further updates, The star's popularity grew further with the arrival of OTT platforms. His portrayal of Kaleen Bhaiya in Mirzapur (2018) became a turning point, earning him immense popularity and making the character a household name. He then went on to win audiences over as lawyer Madhav Mishra in Criminal Justice.

On top of that, The star is now awaiting the rollout of his soon-to-release movie, Parvarik ManuRanjan. Directed by Varun V Sharma, the movie also stars Aditi Rao Hydari in the lead role, alongside Mukesh Tiwari, Vijayant Kohli, Karan Chanana and Bijendra Kala in supporting roles. Our roads were full of people bursting crackers on them, out in the open, even when it’s not allowed. This is heartbreaking. @my bmc ®mumbaipolice."

Meanwhile, She also put up a post on Monday morning, which read: “Diwali is a festival of light, love, family and new beginnings. But every year, along with the celebrations, comes a familiar aftermath: polluted air, firecracker waste, noise and frightened animals. Firecrackers rollout fine particulate matter and other pollutants that add to an already challenging air-quality situation. And the impact isn’t experienced equally. Children, older people, those with respiratory conditions and animals are particularly vulnerable. This year, let’s make a choice that allows everyone including the ones who cannot speak for themselves to enjoy the festival.”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bhumi Satish Pednekkar (@bhumisatishpednekkar)

As per the latest buzz, According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI of 0-50 is considered good, 51-100 satisfactory, 101-200 moderate, 201-300 poor, 301-400 very poor and 401-500 severe.

In further updates, On Monday morning, nine monitoring stations recorded poor air quality, 12 were in the moderate category, three recorded satisfactory air quality and only Borivali East recorded good air quality.

On top of that, Chembur recorded similarly high readings, with the AQI rising to 334 before climbing further to 401 overnight. By 7 am, the reading had fallen to 216. Navy Nagar was among the worst-affected locations. Its AQI, already high at 359 around 10pm, remained close to the 400 mark through the night, peaking at 497 at 2 am. At 7 am, it stood at 274. At Shivaji Nagar, the AQI spiked to 444 at 11 pm. Readings were comparatively lower in the hours before and after the spike, with the AQI standing at 223 at 7 am.

title: Adnan Sami slams Mumbai Airport's Pranaam service over staff's ‘rude’ behaviour, says they didn't inform him of 5-hour flight delay
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Adnan Sami has taken to social media to complain about the service he received at Mumbai Airport's Terminal 2, alleging negligence and unprofessional behaviour by the staff of its Pranaam service. The singer also called out the staff of the service of being rude.

Adding to this, Adnan Sami compalined about rude staff of airport service. 'Wasn't informed about 5 hour flight delay' Adnan shared that he had been using the service since its early days, but his latest experience left him disappointed. He alleged that no one was actively waiting to receive him and his team upon their arrival. He also blamed the service for failing to inform him about a five-hour flight delay in advance.

Meanwhile, He wrote, "Our flight was delayed by @airindia five hours (which in itself was appalling!), a fact that Pranaam knew, but they only informed us after we had gone through the entrance security. Had they informed us beforehand, we would have easily avoided coming earlier to the airport & been sitting comfortably at home. Instead, because of their negligence and carelessness, we had to endure this long tiring wait at the airport."

Notably, Adnan also called the female staff member assigned to them rude and incompetent. He wrote, "Then, the female staff member assigned to us was completely rude! First, she was consistently on her mobile phone. When it was time to escort us from the lounge to the departure gate, she failed to show up. Instead she sent the porter. When asked where she was, the porter had no clue! We were take by buggy and when we arrived at the gate, the porter had to search for her, and he found her sitting in a corner, AGAIN, engrossed in her mobile phone chatting away, Only when she was reprimanded, did she hang up."

As per the latest buzz, The singer further alleged that the staff member was unaware of where to take them to access the fast-track facility for First and Business Class passengers, leaving him and his team to navigate the process themselves.

In further updates, He wrote, "When she was reprimanded again, instead of being apologetic, she tried to snap back, for which she was immediately shut down. Extremely bad conduct and disappointingly unprofessional! This is the 2nd time Pranaam has misbehaved. You charge for these services and have a monopolistic attitude which is extremely arrogant, infinitely annoying & egregiously disrespectful. I’m once again extremely disappointed in the staff for this incident."

On top of that, Adnan Sami is known for songs such as Lift Kara De, Tera Chehra, Kabhi To Nazar Milao and Bheegi Bheegi Raaton Mein. He has also lent his voice to several Bollywood songs, including Bhar Do Jholi Meri from Salman Khan's Bajrangi Bhaijaan and Aye Udi Udi Udi from Saathiya. Born in London, he became an Indian citizen in January 2016 and was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2020 for his contribution to music.

title: Ahaan Panday’s Beparwah co-star, Aaishvary Thackeray, loses Rs. 19,000 to cyber fraud; files police complaint
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

According to a report in The Times of India, Aaishvary Thackeray opened up that he lives with his mother, Smita, and grandmother, Kunda. He was at his residence in Andheri on October 30 when, at around 1:30 am, he received a text message informing him that Rs. 307.82 had been deducted from his bank account. Eight minutes later, he received another message notifying him of a further deduction of Rs. 15,511.98. Four more fraudulent transactions followed, taking the total amount lost to cyber fraud to Rs. 19,638.15.

Adding to this, Hence, Aaishvary Thackeray visited Oshiwara police station and filed a complaint. The Times of India report verified that the cops have begun investigating and have found that the transactions had been made overseas. The article also shared that an FIR was registered against an unknown cyber fraudster under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Information Technology Act.

Meanwhile, Aaishvary Thackeray, 30, worked as an assistant director on Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s Bajirao Mastani (2015), starring Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone and Priyanka Chopra. Last year, he made his debut as an star in Anurag Kashyap’s two-part crime comedy saga, Nishaanchi (2025). Aaishvary played a double role in his debut venture and was quite appreciated.

Notably, Besides acting, Aaishvary Thackeray also has an interest in music. In Nishaanchi 's first part, he composed and wrote the song 'Pigeon Kabootar' and sang 'Neend Bhi Teri' . In the second part, he composed the 'End Theme' .

As per the latest buzz, In the 2026 YRF (Yash Raj Films) Spy movie, Alpha , starring Alia Bhatt and Sharvari, Aaishvary was one of the music programmers on the song 'Massacre', 'Champagne', 'Haaniya' and 'Agni' . He was also one of the lyricists of 'Massacre - Midnight Version' .

In further updates, Aaishvary Thackeray will next be seen as an star in Beparwah , which marks Ahaan Panday’s second movie after the sleeper smash hit Saiyaara (2025). Besides Aaishvary and Ahaan, it also stars Sharvari, Bobby Deol and Jimmy Sheirgill. Directed by Ali Abbas Zafar, it releases in cinemas on March 26, 2027.

title: Neetu Kapoor reveals buying her first Mercedes and five properties at 15, says she had done 100 films by 21
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran Bollywood star Neetu Kapoor began her acting journey as a child artist and later stepped away from the movie industry after getting married and having children, Ranbir Kapoor and Riddhima Kapoor Sahni . In a recent conversation with Curly Tales, Neetu recalled how she had appeared in around 100 films by the age of 21. She also opened up that she bought her first Mercedes when she was just 15.

Adding to this, Neetu Kapoor talks about working as a child artist. Neetu Kapoor on buying her own mercedes at the age of 15 Neetu opened up that she had her first child, Riddhima Kapoor Sahni, at the age of 21 and had already featured in around 100 films by then. She added, "10-12 films I had done when I was a kid. I started when I was 5 in Suraj, a movie with Vijayanthimala. Then Do Kaaliyan was a very famous movie of mine where I essayed a double role. So then there was a gap from 11 to 13, and at 14 I started again. Then, from 14 to 21, I did around 70 movies."

Meanwhile, When asked if she had become a superstar by the age of 15, Neetu shared, "I had bought 4-5 properties by the age of 15, and I had my own Mercedes. Can you believe that? I was in 8th standard, and after that, offers started coming, and I never went back to school. I had learnt dancing from Vyjayanthimala, so I knew how to dance. I never went to acting school, but after doing films as a kid, there was no camera shyness, so that helped."

Notably, Neetu further opened up that leaving the movie industry at the age of 21, after her marriage, was an easy decision because she had already worked a lot. She shared that, in those days, she would often work three shifts in a single day. Recalling her hectic schedule, she shared she would wake up at 7 am and then head to her second and third shoots. The demanding routine left her exhausted, and she had little time to make friends. Soon after getting married, she welcomed Riddhima, followed by Ranbir two years later. She shared she was content with staying at home and raising her children.

As per the latest buzz, Neetu made her acting debut as a child artist in the 1966 movie Suraj. She went on to establish herself as one of the leading female actors in Hindi cinema in the 1970s. She played her first lead role opposite Randhir Kapoor in Rickshawala, a remake of the Tamil movie Rickshawkaran (1971). The same year, Neetu garnered attention for her appearance in the popular song Lekar Hum Deewana Dil from Nasir Hussain's smash hit Yaadon Ki Baaraat. She also featured in films such as Deewaar, Khel Khel Mein, Kabhi Kabhie and Amar Akbar Anthony. She frequently shared screen space with her husband, Rishi Kapoor.

In further updates, After her marriage in 1980, Neetu retired from acting. Her last movie to be rolled out was Ganga Meri Maa in 1983. After a 25-year hiatus, she made her comeback with a cameo appearance in Imtiaz Ali's romantic comedy-drama Love Aaj Kal in 2009, playing the older version of her husband's love interest in the movie. She followed it with films such as Do Dooni Chaar, Jab Tak Hai Jaan, Besharam and Jugjugg Jeeyo. Her most recent movie is Dadi Ki Shaadi.
