title: Ramayana box office collection day 5 (updated live): No Monday blues; Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film set for Bollywood's biggest Monday, races to ₹300 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

With the Diwali festivities behind it, Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana finally seems to be recovering at the ticket-window. The epic had a good but not great start at the ticket-window on its opening weekend. However, its first Monday now gives the movie its best chance for a healthier long run. Given the post-Diwali holidays, Ramayana is sure to buck the trend of a drop on the first Monday and is actually on course to register its best day at the domestic ticket-window, and arguably the biggest Monday in Indian cinema history.

Adding to this, Ramayana is seeing a boost in collections after Diwali. Ramayana ticket-window update Ramayana began with houseful shows on day 1, netting ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net in India on its opening day. The figure was low given the movie’s scale, but it was still the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. The movie then fell slightly before recovering, ending its opening weekend at ₹ 239 crore rupees net in India. This included a Saturday haul of ₹ 69.80 crore rupees net, the movie’s best single day so far.

Meanwhile, But with Diwali now over, the movie is expected to see two bumper days on the Govardhan Puja (Monday) and Bhai Dooj (Tuesday) holidays. Advance booking is indicative of that. Ramayana sold over 14 lakh tickets in pre-sales for Monday, grossing over ₹ 50 crore rupees. This is the movie’s highest single-day advance booking gross so far. This means the movie is poised for its biggest single-day at the domestic ticket-window.

Notably, By 4 PM on Monday, Ramayana had grossed ₹ 68 crore rupees net in India, storming past the ₹ 250-crore rupees mark and taking its domestic haul to ₹ 307 crore rupees . The only worrisome factor for the movie is that its earnings have come largely on the back of some good performance by the Hindi version. Despite Yash’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version hasn’t quite broken the bank yet.

As per the latest buzz, However, on Monday, Ramayana was selling 1.37 lakh tickets per hour on BookMyShow around noon, the highest since the platform started keeping records post-pandemic. Only two other Indian films have ever breached the 1 lakh-ticket-per-hour mark prior to this: Dhurandhar 2 (1.08 lakh) and Pushpa 2 (1.07 lakh).

In further updates, Dhurandhar 2 holds the record for the best Monday collection by an Indian movie. The Ranveer Singh-starrer minted ₹ 60 crore rupees net on its first Monday earlier this year. Ramayana easily left this mark in the dust. But it’s important to note that Dhurandhar 2’s earnings came from a non-holiday Monday. Before Ramayan, the record for the biggest Monday on a holiday belonged to Salman Khan’s Tiger 3, which collected ₹ 58 crore rupees on its first Monday, the day of Diwali 2023.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first part of a duology. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for rollout on Diwali 2028.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Adding to this, Neetu Kapoor reveals how Ranbir Kapoor makes daughter Raha express better. She was standing below, so she got hit by it."
Notably, She also opened up that Raha always greets Ranbir with ‘Jai Shri Ram’ when he returns home from work.

As per the latest buzz, Earlier, Neetu had also lauded Ranbir and Alia's parenting style. Speaking on a podcast, she shared, "Raha listens to Alia, and she is a great mother, but Ranbir is like a friend to her. What a father. Hats off. Both are amazing. He does all the fun and masti with her, but she is very scared of her mother because Alia is a disciplinarian.”

Alia shared glimpses of the celebrations on social media, including pictures of the family cutting a cake at a Bluey-themed birthday party. Alia's father, Mahesh Bhatt, had earlier opened up that she often takes her daughter to movie sets. title: Ramayana vs Dhurandhar 2: How Ranveer Singh film, with its gore and A-rating, beat Ranbir Kapoor-starrer's family-friendly appeal
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

It is the most expensive Indian movie ever made. Ramayana 's exact budget, though, remains a mystery. Years ago, producer Namit Malhotra claimed the two parts were being made for $500 million ( ₹ 4000 crore rupees). More recent reports have claimed that Part 1 has a landing cost of ₹ 1600 crore rupees (approximately $175 million). Either way, Ramayana needs to make a ton of money to break even. In fact, it needs to out-earn the likes of Dhurandhar 2 and Pushpa 2 just to be profitable. But if the opening day and weekend have indicated anything, it’s that the crown of Ranveer Singh ’s Dhurandhar 2 is secure. And that is a curious thing. How did Ramayana, the story with the most universal appeal and devotional following, fail to unseat an A-rated violent spy thriller?

Adding to this, Dhurandhar 2 remains the highest-grossing Hindi movie in India. Dhurandhar 2’s edge over Ramayana Dhurandhar: The Revenge arrived with unprecedented hype when it rolled out this March. The smash hit success of part 1 meant that advance bookings for the sequel reached never-before-seen numbers. The Aditya Dhar movie gave pan-India behemoths a run for their money, becoming the first Bollywood movie to earn ₹ 100 crore rupees in a day domestically and ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. Ramayana should have emulated these numbers, given its massive scale and wide overseas rollout. Yet, it had to settle for ₹ 65 crore rupees in India and ₹ 128 crore rupees worldwide. These are staggering numbers for any movie without a ₹ 1600+ crore rupees budget. But sadly, Ramayana does not fall in that category.

Meanwhile, The edge Dhurandhar 2 had was its appeal as a sequel to a revered movie. The timing of the rollout also mattered. Part 2 arrived just three months after Part 1. In fact, the first Dhurandhar was still playing in theatres when The Revenge rolled out. The movie's nationalistic themes and slick production values also added to its appeal.

Notably, But the biggest surprise is that Dhurandhar 2 offset an A-rating and abundant gore with its hype. On paper, Ramayana should draw crowds by the dozen, with families also raring to go to the theatres en masse. But that universal appeal wasn’t enough to outdo Dhurandhar 2’s hype, at least in the opening weekend.

As per the latest buzz, Over the last decade, Ranveer Singh and Ranbir Kapoor have been hyped up as the best - and most bankable - stars of their generation. Vicky Kaushal has attempted to enter the fray with Uri and Chhaava, but the larger conversation centres on Ranbir and Ranveer. With Animal, Ranbir seemed to pull ahead before Ranveer reigned supreme with the two Dhurandhars. Ramayana was being seen as Ranbir’s turn to stake the throne again, but it hasn’t quite panned out that way. The Nitesh Tiwari-directed movie collected 36% less than Dhurandhar 2 on its opening day and 32% less over its first four days (including the extended weekend).

In further updates, The post-Diwali break is bound to diminish the gap, but unless word of mouth really kicks in, Ramayana may not be able to overtake Dhurandhar 2 any time soon. That means the movie’s hope of breaching the ₹ 2000-crore rupees mark may remain just a dream. Dhurandhar 2 missed that mark by about ₹ 150 crore rupees. Ramayana would have to see a great surge overseas to beat Dhurandhar 2 there.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first part of a duology. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part rolled out worldwide on November 5, while the second part is set for rollout on Diwali 2028.

title: Aneet Padda celebrates Diwali with Saiyaara co-star Ahaan Panday's mom Deanne Panday and family
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood actors Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda became overnight sensations with their movie Saiyaara , which was rolled out in 2025. While their on-screen chemistry won hearts, their off-screen bond has led followers to speculate about a possible romantic relationship between them. Amid the dating rumours, Aneet was seen celebrating Diwali with Ahaan's family, with his mother, Deanne Panday, sharing pictures with the star on social media.

Adding to this, Deanne Panday's Diwali celebration with Aneet Padda. Aneet Padda celebrates Diwali with Ahaan Panday's family On Sunday, Deanne posted on Instagram stories and shared a selfie with Aneet. In the picture, Aneet, dressed in traditional attire, was seen covering her head with a dupatta, suggesting that the photo was taken shortly after the Diwali puja. Deanne, meanwhile, was seen pouting for the selfie. Another picture showed Aneet posing with Deanne and other family members in front of a rangoli. The remaining pictures shared by Deanne showed her celebrating with family members, including Chunky Panday, Bhavana Panday and Ananya Panday.

Meanwhile, This is not the first time Aneet has been part of a celebration with Ahaan's family. The star was also seen at Ahaan's sister Alanna Panday's baby shower, where she participated in fun games alongside Ananya Panday and Ahaan. Aneet also celebrated her 24th birthday with Ahaan and Deanne. The star had a fairytale-themed birthday celebration, and pictures from the party surfaced online. Alia Bhatt was also among those who attended the celebration. Aneet later shared a loved-up picture with Ahaan, in which he was seen hugging her at the party, sending social media into a frenzy.

Notably, Ever since their movie Saiyaara broke records and became the highest-grossing romantic movie in Indian cinema, followers have been shipping Aneet and Ahaan. Their frequent appearances together at events and family celebrations have further fuelled dating rumours. However, both actors have maintained that they are just best friends. Following Saiyaara, the two will share the screen again in Mohit Suri's next movie, backed by Yash Raj Films.

As per the latest buzz, Aneet will next be seen in Shakti Shalini, part of Maddock Films' horror-comedy universe. Directed by Aditya Sarpotdar, the movie is centred on Shakti, an ordinary woman who becomes a protector, while Shalini, a vengeful spirit, returns to punish men after being brutally betrayed and killed. title: CAIT calls meeting on Nov 13, says will discuss demand to shift protests to city outskirts
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT), a traders’ body led by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) lawmaker Praveen Khandelwal, on Monday shared it will hold a meeting on November 13 to discuss a proposal to demand designated protest sites on the outskirts of major cities, arguing that prolonged political agitations in commercial hubs disrupt local businesses and hurt the national economy.

Adding to this, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) supporters scuffle with security personnel during a protest demanding India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged voter roll irregularities linked to the "special intensive revision" (AFP FILE) Once they make a decision, the statement shared, the traders’ body planned to approach the government and could even approach court to push for designated protest venues on the outskirts of the city.

Meanwhile, In October, thousands of people hit the streets, braving Metro closures, internet shutdown, prohibitory orders and 40,000 security personnel who turned the Capital into a virtual fortress and sparked row by dragging, manhandling and detaining many agitators. The Centre subsequently ended Jantar Mantar’s three-decade-old status as Delhi’s designated protest site, with the Delhi Police issuing an order on October 11, 2026, to denotify the venue and shift demonstrations to three alternative locations. Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi, Burari Ground in north-west Delhi and CBD Ground in east Delhi have been designated as the alternative protest venues.

Notably, The demand comes against the backdrop of a massive protest in the heart of New Delhi on November 1, the largest show of strength by the INDIA bloc, that attacked the ruling BJP and demanded Kumar’s removal over allegations of irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission of India and the special intensive revision, which has already removed 130 million names from India’s electoral rolls, many of them under absent, shifted or dead categories.

As per the latest buzz, CAIT claimed that the agitations led to “widespread disruption to business activities” in the national capital. “Suitable locations should be designated on the outskirts of every city, or at other appropriate places, for protests and demonstrations,” Khandelwal, the Chandni Chowk MP, shared in a note.

In further updates, “The arrangement should be implemented across the country and not remain limited to Delhi. The proposed sites would enable peaceful demonstrations while protecting markets, commercial centres, transport routes and essential business activities.”

On top of that, Khandelwal claimed disruptions caused by protests affected not just shopkeepers and sales but also supply chains, the movement of goods, employees’ livelihoods and the cash flow of small businesses. The meeting would also discuss other issues including GST reforms, protection against cyber fraud and simplification of regulations.

CAIT national president BC Bhartia shared discussions would focus on simplifying GST returns and compliance requirements, resolving technical difficulties and reducing unnecessary notices and litigation, particularly for small traders.

title: Makers of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer 'Ramayana' issue warning against unauthorised recording of the film
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

New Delhi, The makers of "Ramayana", featuring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, issued a warning against the recording and sharing of unauthorised video clips from the cinema halls and shared legal action will be taken against the offenders.

Adding to this, Makers of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer 'Ramayana' issue warning against unauthorised recording of the movie The movie rolled out in theatres on November 5 in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam languages. It features Kapoor as Lord Ram, Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, among others. It is the first installment of the two-part cinematic adaptation of the ancient epic "Ramayana".
Meanwhile, The makers shared a statement on Instagram on the movie's official handle on Saturday and asked to deleted the uploaded content from the platforms.

Notably, "Legal Notice. It has come to our attention that unauthorised footage of Namit Malhotra's 'Ramayana' is being recorded inside cinema halls and circulated across social media and messaging platforms.

As per the latest buzz, "The Hon'ble Bombay High Court, by orders dated 2 November 2026 and 6 November 2026 in commercial IP suit no. 37230 of 2026, has restrained all persons, known and unknown, from recording, uploading, sharing or otherwise communicating the movie or any part of it without authorisation," read the caption.
In further updates, "Offenders will be reported to the authorities and platforms and will face criminal, civil and contempt proceedings, without further notice," it added.

On top of that, The movie is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations. It follows Lord Ram's journey, his exile, the abduction of Sita by Ravana and the ensuing battle between the forces of good and evil.
The movie's music has been composed by Oscar-winning composers Hans Zimmer and A R Rahman, while Terry Notary and Guy Norris are part of the action team.

title: Sunita Ahuja is confident about reunion with Govinda amid his dating rumours with Komal Rani Swarnkar, says ‘nobody can ever separate us’
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Govinda and Sunita Ahuja 's relationship has been under the spotlight amid reports of trouble in their marriage and rumours of the star's alleged affair with Komal Rani Swarnkar . Sunita of late claimed that Govinda and Komal were planning to get married and called the star her alleged partner's ‘sugar daddy’. However, months after making the remarks, Sunita has now expressed confidence that she and Govinda will reunite.

Adding to this, Govinda and Sunita Ahuja have been married for 39 years now. Sunita Ahuja is confident about reunion with husband Govinda In a conversation with Pinkvilla, Sunita recalled celebrating Diwali with Govinda and spoke about the gifts he would bring home for her. She shared, "Earlier Govinda used to buy me gold, give gifts. We would go shopping for all the shagun we got from him. Sometimes he would even take me and Tina to buy jewellery. Those days would come again soon, and we would go jewellery shopping together."

Meanwhile, Sunita also recalled how Govinda used to call her ‘ghar ki laxmi (the one who brings prosperity and good fortune to the family)’ and shared she would always stand by him because he was her childhood love. She further addressed Govinda's objection to her use of abusive language, defending herself by saying that she did not feel the need to be sophisticated in front of him.

Notably, She then expressed hope of seeing her happy family back again and shared, "Of course, we will see; why won’t we? Right now, the time isn’t in our favour, and you can't fight time. It’s a 40-year-old marriage; why won’t it sustain? It’s fine; he’s doing what he likes. I am working, and my entire focus is on work, but nobody can ever separate us in this lifetime. Rest, I’ve left it all to the Almighty. Apart from God, I don’t ask anything from anyone. Whatever is right for him, and me, God will bless us with that."

As per the latest buzz, The rift between Govinda and his wife, Sunita, began following the star's rumoured relationship with his Roopa co-star Komal Rani Swarnkar. The couple, who got married in 1987 and have two children, have been making headlines over marital troubles for nearly two years. Sunita had as per reports filed for divorce in December 2024, citing adultery, and cruelty, but later withdrew her petition in August 2026. She subsequently claimed that Govinda and Komal were planning to get married, an allegation that the star's manager denied.

In further updates, The row intensified after Govinda and Komal were spotted together at Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja pandal in September, while Sunita had visited the same pandal separately. Sunita then called Govinda 'sugar daddy' of Komal Rani. Reacting to Sunita's remarks, Komal shared a lengthy note on Instagram Stories without directly naming her or Govinda. She wrote, "Nobody ever can be a homebreaker in already broken house." She also questioned Sunita's decision to discuss her marital problems publicly, suggesting that it was a carefully planned conspiracy to gain sympathy.

On top of that, Komal further alleged that Sunita was mentally harassing her husband, stopping him from working and isolating him. She concluded by asking people not to use her name to serve an agenda. Following Komal's post, Sunita shared she had nothing to say about Govinda or his co-star. In an interaction with Sarish Media, she shared, "I see that he is happy; God bless him. Let him live his life the way he wants to." She added that her main focus was now her work and that she did not want to get involved in controversies repeatedly.

Sunita is set to make her Bollywood debut playing the role of her son, Yashvardhan Ahuja's mother in Sajid Khan's soon-to-release movie. Backed by Ektaa Kapoor, the movie also stars Nitanshi Goel in a lead role and is expected to rollout in theatres next year.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 4: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film storms past ₹500 crore on opening weekend; beats Adipurush's lifetime haul
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

It took some time, but Ramayana Part 1 seems to have finally found its footing. The Nitesh Tiwari movie recovered after a relatively lukewarm opening for a movie of that scale, particularly overseas. By Sunday, it was finally galloping, taking big strides in India and making inroads internationally. This took its global business past ₹ 500 crore rupees in its first weekend.

Adding to this, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer opened to great reviews on Thursday, with initial audience reactions largely positive. Yet that did not drive footfall momentum very strongly. The movie collected ₹ 128 crore rupees worldwide on its rollout day. The two disappointing aspects of this number were that the Kannada version netted only ₹ 7.50 crore rupees despite Yash’s presence, and the overseas collections did not cross $6 million despite a 50,000-screen rollout by Sony Pictures.

Meanwhile, But word of mouth lifted Ramayana over the weekend. It had its biggest single-day on Saturday, followed by a strong Sunday despite limited footfall in India for Diwali. This helped the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer to earn ₹ 239 crore rupees net ( ₹ 285 crore rupees gross) domestically in its extended four-day rollout weekend.

Notably, The issue with Ramayana has been its overseas earnings. Sony Pictures distributed the movie internationally, giving it a rollout in 59,000 screens worldwide, almost six times the size of any big Indian rollout. Yet the movie opened to $12.2 million in North America and barely crossed $11 million in other markets. This still gives the movie an international haul of $23.7 million in its first four days. Ramayana has now grossed ₹ 507 crore rupees globally.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

In further updates, Quite interestingly, Ramayana had lagged behind Adipurush , the other recent big-budget adaptation of Valmiki’s epic, for its first three days at the global ticket-window. But the fact that Ramayana maintained its momentum on Sunday, while Adipurush crashed on its fourth day due to negative word-of-mouth, turned the tables. On day 4, Ramayana surpassed the ₹ 400-crore rupees and ₹ 500-crore rupees marks. In contrast, Adipurush had collected fewer than ₹ 20 crore rupees on its fourth day. In fact, after a bumper start, the Prabhas-starrer had shut its shop with a global final haul of ₹ 393 crore rupees, way below its budget. Ramayana has surpassed its lifetime collection in just four days. Given the post-Diwali holidays, the movie’s collection is now expected to truly soar.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Kareena Kapoor says she is ‘very against botox’ and vouches for self preservation rather than going going under the knife
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Going under the knife to look younger might have become a norm for many in showbiz, but Kareena Kapoor doesn't prefer that. Instead, the star has her own ways of making sure that she preserves her talent. Kareena was in conversation with Barkha Dutt for Mojo Story where she was asked for her opinion on botox and cosmetic procedures, to which the star immediately responded by saying that she is very against botox.

Adding to this, Kareena Kapoor was last seen in Daayra. What Kareena shared The star shared, “I am very against botox, that I have been very, very honest about. I am for self-preservation in a good sense. Which is being healthy, feeling great, natural therapies. Self preservation is also preserving my talent, because that is my weapon. Taking holidays with family and friends, engaging in different things apart from just being on set is also a form of self-preservation. Rather than the needles and going under the knife. That is something that I am all for because people are forgetting that it is so important to preserve your body and mind rather than your injectibles.”
Meanwhile, She also added, “It is terrible where young girls not wanting to look beyond 18 or 20. I am having the best time in my 40s. I have never felt better or even acted better…”

Notably, Kareena was most of late seen in Daayra, directed by Meghna Gulzar. The movie marks her first on-screen collaboration with Malayalam star Prithviraj Sukumaran. title: HT Exclusive: Vinod Kapri on almost quitting filmmaking after Pyre's OTT rejection, ₹7,000 bank balance and losing 70% shows after Ramayana release
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri says that getting Pyre to theatres was a struggle that nearly made him quit filmmaking. Despite winning awards at international movie festivals, the movie failed to find takers among streaming platforms and faced hurdles in securing a theatrical rollout. Now, with audiences responding warmly to the movie, he hopes strong word of mouth will help it reach more screens. Set in Uttarakhand's Kumaon region, Pyre follows an elderly couple whose children have moved away in search of better opportunities, leaving them to face old age and loneliness together. The movie stars 80-year-old Padam Singh Kapri, a retired Indian Army serviceman, and 70-year-old Heera Devi, both making their acting debuts. Padam plays a character named after himself, while Heera portrays Tulsi.

Adding to this, National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri says that getting Pyre to theatres was a struggle that nearly made him quit filmmaking. In an interview with Hindustan Times, Vinod spoke about the challenges of bringing the movie to theatres, the loss of shows following the arrival of a major rollout and the audience response that has renewed his faith in filmmaking. He also recalled announcing his retirement after receiving an award in Toronto.

Meanwhile, Despite the movie's recognition at international festivals, finding a rollout platform proved to be a major challenge. Vinod shared he approached several OTT platforms, but none showed interest in acquiring the movie. “There are many better films than Pyre which are not rolled out yet, which are still yet to see light of the day. There are many better films than Pyre and I know these films,” he shared, pointing to the number of independent films that struggle to reach audiences despite their quality.

Notably, The experience left him physically, mentally and financially drained. Recalling how he had reached a breaking point, Vinod shared, “I was so so depressed and so mentally, physically, financially exhausted that I revealed my retirement from that stage after receiving the award from Deepa Meta. I shared I'm done with filmmaking. I'm not going to make any movie after this because I'm completely drained out after making this movie.”

As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram He credited his executive producer Arindra Rai Chaudhuri, who also came on board as a producer, for encouraging him not to lose hope. Arindra eventually connected him with London-based businessman Suresh Joshi, who watched the movie and believed it deserved a theatrical rollout. But by then, Vinod had very little left to spend on the movie. “My company bank account is only 7,000 rupees and I don't have a single penny to spend on this movie anymore I don't have any energy I don't even have a money,” he recalled.

In further updates, Suresh offered to put money into the rollout, allowing the movie to reach cinemas. Vinod shared he remains grateful to both for stepping in when he had almost given up on the project. Looking back, he feels the rejection from streaming platforms may have worked in the movie's favour. “It is a blessing in disguise that OTT rejected this movie otherwise this movie could not have get this kind of love and recognition the movie is getting right now,” he shared.

On top of that, While the movie has started finding its audience, its theatrical run has not been without hurdles. Vinod shared Pyre began with a limited rollout of around 80 screens, with the number of shows increasing as more people started watching it. “So we started with 80 screens on day one, 80 plus something, and by day five, it went up to 400 shows all over India,” he shared.

He also shared how the movie's opening collections grew over its first three days. “Day one we just opened with 8 lakh. Our opening was just 8 lakh rupees and on day two it went up to 27 lakhs and on day three it went up to 70,” he shared.

title: Daler Mehndi thanks fans for their support during Uttarakhand event controversy, says brother Mika Singh showed up like a force to reckon with
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Punjabi singer Daler Mehndi made headlines after Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister Subodh Uniyal reprimanded him on stage during a cultural evening and questioned his conduct, alleging that he was intoxicated. Mika Singh had called on Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal to apologise. After weeks since the incident, Daler has finally broken his silence on this row and rolled out a statement on his Instagram account.

Adding to this, Daler Mehndi has spoken out on the entire row that erupted last month over his live performance. Daler's note He wrote, "Over the years, I have received so much love through my music and on every stage I have stood. But what I have experienced of late has touched me in a way that is difficult to put into words. The way you stood by me, the way you spoke for me, the faith you showed in me and the love you gave me I don’t think I can ever fully express what it has meant to me."

Meanwhile, Daler did not miss a special mention for his brother and singer Mika Singh , and wrote, “My family has been my greatest strength through this time. My brother Mika stood up for me like a force to reckon with.” He thanked his family and all other members of the entertainment industry for showing support.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Daler Mehndi (@thedalermehndiofficial)

As per the latest buzz, Daler shared that he felt fortunate to have felt so much love for him in this lifetime and that he will never forget the kindness. He concluded his note by extending his wishes for Diwali.

In further updates, Singer Daler Mehndi performed at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in New Tehri, Uttarakhand, on Sunday night. He was interrupted mid-performance and reprimanded on stage by Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister Subodh Uniyal. The minister criticised the singer's conduct and shared, “You cannot even speak, so how are you going to sing?”, hinting that the singer was intoxicated. The clip subsequently circulated widely on social media.

On top of that, Later, while in conversation with ANI, Subodh explained why he had reprimanded Daler publicly. He shared, “He is a big artist. If a big artist doesn't do justice to their art... He seemed disoriented on stage and didn't seem to be able to even keep standing. Besides this, he was only lip-syncing to his songs. I told him that he is a big artist and he should do justice to his art; he had been offered ₹ 35 lakh to come and perform, but he was not even singing. So, I expressed my resentment."

Following the incident, Daler's brother and fellow singer Mika Singh, along with several other celebrities, criticised the minister for disrespecting the singer. Mika also shared that Daler was unwell during the performance.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 4 (updated live): Diwali boost propels Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi film past ₹200 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana seems to be recovering after a good, but not great, start at the domestic ticket-window. The most expensive Indian movie ever made set a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. But there were concerns about its earnings on the day of the festival. However, on Sunday, the movie allayed all those fears to register an all-time record for Diwali

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash play Rama and Ravana, respectively, in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana ticket-window update Ramayana began with houseful shows on day 1, netting ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net in India on its opening day. The figure was low given the movie’s scale, but it was still the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. On Friday, Ramayana fell slightly, bringing in ₹ 48 crore rupees, but jumped up on Saturday to mint almost ₹ 70 crore rupees net. This took its three-day domestic haul to an impressive ₹ 183 crore rupees net. On Sunday, despite Diwali keeping footfalls low in part of the country, Ramayana had a great day. The movie collected ₹ 32 crore rupees net in India by 5 PM, taking its earnings past ₹ 200 crore rupees in just four days. Its domestic haul now stands at a formidable ₹ 215 crore rupees .

Meanwhile, What is worrisome for the movie is that its earnings have come largely on the back of some good performance by the Hindi version. Despite Yash’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version has started extremely slowly. It collected just ₹ 7.50 crore rupees on day 1 and has lacked pace since. Of the other versions, Telugu has fared well, while Malayalam and Tamil are just filling the ranks.

Notably, While the Diwali weekend has seen many big films rolled out in theatres over the years, very few rollout on the day of the festival itself, choosing to maximise the days after Diwali. But Ramayana came out three days before it, which meant its biggest day - the first Sunday - falls on Diwali. It is currently tracking to beat Tiger 3’s all-time Diwali earnings record. The Salman Khan-starrer collected �� 44.50 crore rupees in net ticket-window on Diwali 2023. Ramayana is aiming for a ₹ 60+ crore rupees day as things stand currently.

As per the latest buzz, On its opening day, Ramayana beat the opening-day hauls of blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 57 crore rupees), Animal ( ₹ 63 crore rupees), and Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 62 crore rupees). But it fell short of Adipurush, the previous adaptation of the epic that opened at ₹ 86.75 crore rupees. The trend continued on the second and third days. But thanks to its extended weekend, Ramayana managed to surpass the Prabhas-starrer on day 4. Adipurush collected ₹ 237 crore rupees net in India in its first four days. Ramayana is almost certain to cross the mark by the end of Sunday.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Proud father Sonu Nigam gets emotional as son Nevaan begins musical journey at 19, reveals he practices vocals for 16 hours a day
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Sonu Nigam and his wife, Madhurima Nigam, marked Diwali with a special announcement about their son, Nevaan. The couple introduced the 19-year-old as he begins his musical journey with a short movie titled Slide. In their social media post, they looked back at his growing years, recalling how the once-shy child who would hesitate to sing in front of his father has slowly grown into a young artist willing to put in the hours to pursue his passion.

Adding to this, nu Nigam's son Nevaan steps into music world with short movie Slide. Sonu Nigam shares son's journey into music In their note, Sonu and Madhurima looked back at Nevaan's journey from childhood to the young musician he is today. They recalled how he once hesitated to sing in front of his father and spoke about the dedication he has shown towards music over the years.

Meanwhile, Sonu shared a photo and wrote, “On this auspicious and pious occasion of Diwali, Nevaan embarks upon his journey into the world of Music venturing into a path far flung from his Grandfather and Father to explore his own horizons. From a chubby little boy to a fit and lean young man, from someone who was extremely shy to sing in front of his own father, to someone who's practicing the vocal exercises taught to him by his brilliant vocal coach 16 hours a day and cracking one take recordings in the studio with the legend Poo Bear, from someone who had a tough time jogging even for merely 3 minutes, to someone who's doing hours of dance practise to hone his skills; Nevaan has truly made our family very very thankful and happy, (Proud, is a word I avoid using in life)!”

Notably, View this post on Instagram The parents also looked back at Nevaan's earliest memories of music, including his time in the studio as a four-year-old and his performance of his father's song Abhi Mujhme Kahin on stage when he was just four and a half. He thanked followers for the love they have shown him and sought their blessings as he begins this new journey. The note continued, “From Kolaveri di in studio at age 4 to Abhi mujhme kahin live on stage at age 4 and a half, he's been fortunate to receive your enormous and unfathomable love. Do bless him that he continues his journey ahead with dignity, hardwork, passion and humility. Give him your love.. Presenting 'SLIDE' BY NEVAAN NIGAM.”

As per the latest buzz, Slide is Nevaan's first big step as an artist. He has come up with the concept for the short movie and co-directed it with Alexander Cobian. The music is by The Audibles, while Nevaan has also been training his voice with music producer Poo Bear.

I think that's a great philosophy to actually follow in life. Don't be bothered by what people are saying. What matters is the people who matter, the people who care for your work, your intention, and your kindness. That's what matters the most,” shared the star.

However, on the occasion of Diwali, for the very first time, the pair shared the face of their son to the public. The picture comes a day after Vihaan turned one on November 7, making the occasion even more special for their followers.

Adding to this, Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal finally give followers a closer look at baby Vihaan, see the picture. Katrina Kaif shares her son's photo Katrina shared the photograph on Instagram on Sunday, captioning it, “Our brightest Diwali yet… ❤️✨Wishing everyone love, light and happiness.” The picture captures the couple enjoying a festive family moment with their son, all three dressed in traditional outfits. Katrina is seen sitting on the floor in a bright yellow embroidered ensemble, paired with statement earrings and her hair left open. She looks at Vihaan with a fond smile as she holds him close.

Meanwhile, Vihaan, dressed in a cream kurta-pyjama and a yellow printed Nehru jacket, stands between his parents, smiling at the camera with one hand raised. Vicky, meanwhile, is seen in a cream embroidered kurta, sitting beside his son with a smile and gently resting one hand on his hip.

Notably, View this post on Instagram Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal welcomed their son in 2025 Katrina and Vicky became parents to a baby boy on November 7, 2025. The couple shared the news through a joint social media post, expressing their happiness at welcoming their first child. “Our bundle of joy has arrived. With immense love and gratitude, we welcome our baby boy.”

As per the latest buzz, A few months before becoming parents, the actors had revealed their pregnancy in September 2025. They shared a sweet Polaroid-style picture of Vicky holding Katrina's baby bump, with both looking visibly happy. Along with the photograph, they wrote, “On our way to start the best chapter of our lives with hearts full of joy and gratitude.”

In further updates, In January 2026, Katrina and Vicky shared their son's name for the first time. The couple posted a photograph of his tiny hand held between theirs and introduced him as Vihaan Kaushal. Their caption read, "Our Ray of Light ❤️ Vihaan Kaushal विहान कौशल. Prayers are answered. Life is beautiful. Our world is changed in a instant. Gratitude beyond words 🙏🏽🧿🕉️."

On top of that, Followers were quick to notice a familiar connection in the name. Vicky played Major Vihaan Singh Shergill in Aditya Dhar's 2019 movie Uri: The Surgical Strike, and many pointed out the connection in the comments. Katrina and Vicky got married on December 9, 2021, at Six Senses Fort Barwara in Rajasthan.

On the work front, Katrina was last seen in Sriram Raghavan's Merry Christmas with Vijay Sethupathi. Meanwhile, Vicky will next star in Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love & War , alongside Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt. The movie is slated January 21, 2027 rollout. He is also shooting for Mahavatar.

title: Amitabh Bachchan says he is facing discomfort in writing letters to thank fans for their gifts, extends them wishes on Diwali
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Amitabh Bachchan told followers last month that he will take a break from his usual social media updates after being advised to rest and recover. The 84-year-old star has been busy shooting for Kaun Banega Crorepati as a host as well as the sequel to Kalki 2898 AD. On the occasion of Diwali, the veteran star put a new post on his Tumblr account to speak about his current health situation and also extended wishes to everyone on the occasion of Diwali.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan has spoken about his current health situation. What Amitabh wrote Starting his post with good wishes to his followers and well-wishers for a happy Diwali, Amitabh wrote, "I have been receiving greetings and gifts from so many well-wishers, and in such abundance that I am now running out of space to keep them. Not storing these gifts properly would amount to disrespecting them. Therefore, to all of you who have been sending gifts as expressions of your affection, I wish to convey my appreciation and acknowledgement. I am also making an effort to respond to each of you personally through letters.”

Meanwhile, "I really wanted to write these replies myself. However, I have been experiencing some discomfort in the hand, for writing, which has caused delay. I sincerely apologise (folded hands emoji),” added the star.

Notably, He also shared, “But what can one do? Circumstances have become such that apologising seems to come easily. One should seek forgiveness. After all, there is nothing wrong with asking for it. The other person may refuse, reject the apology, or understand and accept it. If they understand and accept the apology, my heart will be filled with happiness. If they do not, their mind will remain troubled.”

As per the latest buzz, The message followed a similar update on his personal blog while extending his Dussehra wishes last month. The star had shared in a previous blog post that he had been given strict instructions to focus on his recovery and avoid communication for the time being. "First Dussehra greetings to all .. love happiness, fulfilment, prayers. Under very strict rest and recuperation .. so am not allowed to communicate .. do excuse .. my apologies," he wrote. He also added, “But do take this as my respected response .. more hopefully later.”

In further updates, A bomb threat email targeting Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow, the Bombay High Court and Mumbai's Mahalaxmi Racecourse prompted security agencies to launch an investigation on Friday. Authorities later verified the threat to be a hoax.

On top of that, Amitabh's message also comes as the police investigate the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff's car. Reports about the case suggest that the suspects had allegedly surveyed other prominent personalities before deciding on their target. According to several reports, the accused had considered the residences of Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar and Aamir Khan. However, they as per reports dropped the idea after assessing the security arrangements around the actors' homes.

On the work front, he is set to return in the sequel to Nag Ashwin's science-fiction movie Kalki 2898 AD, which stars Prabhas and Kamal Haasan . On television, the star continues to host the 18th season of Kaun Banega Crorepati, the long-running quiz show closely associated with him.

title: ‘We will withdraw from agitation only after Gyanesh Kumar is removed’: K C Venugopal
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

AICC general secretary K C Venugopal on Sunday shared the Congress-led agitation against CEC Gyanesh Kumar would continue until he was removed from the post and the country's electoral system was made impartial and transparent.

Adding to this, Venugopal alleged that the deletion of names from electoral rolls would deprive poor people of their voting rights and access to various government benefits. (File Photo/ANI) In conversation with reporters here, Venugopal shared protests were continuing across states and districts, with only a brief pause expected during the Diwali festival.

Meanwhile, He described the November 1 rally organised by the Congress in New Delhi as one of the strongest protests witnessed in the country, saying the party was fighting against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

Notably, "We will withdraw from this agitation only after Gyanesh Kumar is removed from the post and steps are taken to make India's electoral system and processes flawless, impartial and fair. This is not a struggle that we will abandon midway," he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Venugopal alleged that the deletion of names from electoral rolls would deprive poor people of their voting rights and access to various government benefits, which, he claimed, were increasingly being linked to voter identity cards.
In further updates, He shared the Congress would launch a nationwide 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' (Save the Vote, Save the Nation) campaign at the panchayat level over the next one-and-a-half months.

On top of that, As part of the campaign, the party would appoint a 'Vote Rakshak' (guardian) in every polling booth to scrutinise electoral rolls, identify people whose names had been deleted and visit their homes to help them get their names restored, he shared.
Congress units were organising programmes across states and districts, while plans were also being drawn up for joint programmes with other political parties, he shared.

title: 'Mockery of democracy': Ex-BJP MP Gopal Shetty tonsures head in protest over BMC demolition in Borivali
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Former BJP MP Gopal Shetty has tonsured his head in protest against the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) demolition of 27 houses in Borivali East, alleging that the civic body acted in haste without giving residents time to retrieve their belongings.

Adding to this, Former BJP MP Gopal Shetty stagng a protest against the BMC's demolition drive at Borivali in Mumbai, following the demolition of an unauthorised structure on a reserved plot. (Hindustan Times/File) Calling the sudden early-morning drive on November 4 a "mockery of democracy", Shetty on Saturday claimed the structures stood on private land occupied for nearly 50 years, and criticized the local BJP leadership for not supporting the affected families.

Meanwhile, The BMC demolished 27 houses built on a 3,400-sq-metre plot, reserved for a BEST bus station, on Swami Vivekanand Road in Borivali East. The drive was carried out after the Supreme Court pulled up the civic body for failing to remove encroachments despite earlier directions.

Notably, The court had also ordered a freeze on the November salaries of Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide and concerned officials, besides initiating contempt proceedings. It subsequently withdrew the salary-related direction and contempt notice after the BMC informed it that the structures had been removed.

As per the latest buzz, In conversation with reporters, the BJP leader shared he had tonsured his head as a mark of protest as the affected families were not allowed to remove their household belongings before the demolition.

In further updates, "I have never seen such action in my public life. Even a person like (26/11 terror attack) Ajmal Kasab was given eight years to face trial and an opportunity to approach the President after his conviction," he shared.
On top of that, He claimed that residents were given notices around 1.30 am and their houses were demolished by 7 am, without allowing them sufficient time to remove their belongings.

He further questioned the manner in which the civic body presented the matter before the apex court, accusing it of failing to submit copies of notices issued to occupants and their replies, as sought by the court.

title: HT Exclusive: Vinod Kapri on casting an 80-year-old Army veteran and a 70-year-old woman with no acting experience as Pyre's elderly lead couple
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri 's search for the lead actors of Pyre took several years, countless auditions and a few unexpected turns. He had considered actors such as Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak Shah, and even tried making the movie with the real-life couple who inspired the story. But the faces he was looking for eventually came from two rather unexpected places.

Adding to this, Vinod Kapri's Pyre features Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, both first-time actors from Uttarakhand. Set in Uttarakhand's Kumaon region, Pyre tells the story of an elderly couple whose children have left their village in search of better opportunities. With no one else around, the two are left to navigate old age, loneliness and the changing life of their mountain home. The movie looks at migration through the lives of parents who stay behind while the younger generation moves away.

Meanwhile, Pyre features Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, both first-time actors from Uttarakhand. Padam, a retired Indian Army serviceman, plays a character named after himself, while Heera takes on the role of Tulsi. The movie has won 18 international awards and is produced by Vinod Kapri, Suresh Joshi and Arindra Rai Chaudhuri under Bhagirathi Films and Mashakbeen Studios. It rolled out in theatres across India on October 30 in Hindi and Malayalam.

Notably, In conversation with Hindustan Times, Vinod looked back at the unusual journey that brought his two lead actors on board. One was discovered during his father's 80th birthday celebration, while the other came into the picture during a stop on a village road.

As per the latest buzz, The idea for Pyre took shape in 2018, when Vinod met an elderly couple in Munsyari, Uttarakhand. He spent close to two hours talking to them and recorded their conversation on his phone. Their bond left a lasting impression on him, and he initially felt they should play themselves in the movie. He even spent eight to 10 days shooting with them, hoping to bring their story to the screen. However, the experience soon made him realise that their real-life chemistry alone was not enough to carry the movie.

In further updates, "That was my first attempt to make this movie with them and but I failed miserably because we went there unprepared and they don't even understand they don't have even understanding of cinema or camera or acting or anything. I realized that should look for more mature actors," he shared.

On top of that, Vinod then began searching for elderly actors from the Himalayan region who could bring a natural understanding of the setting, its culture and language to the story. He auditioned more than 50 to 60 people over the next two years, but none seemed right for the roles. After struggling to find his lead pair, he eventually approached Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak Shah.

Vinod shared the script with Naseeruddin after star Vishal Bhardwaj helped connect them. Both Naseeruddin and Ratna liked the story and were keen to be part of the movie. However, the Main Vaapas Aaunga star had a question about whether they would be able to do justice to characters so deeply rooted in the region. “He was so candid about movie and a story and he shared you know we really wanted to do this movie and we don't want to leave this movie because this is such a beautiful script but I have one concern do you think that we belong to that place and do you think we both of us can do justice to this movie just think about it,” Vinod recalled.

title: Actors should not blame industry for typecasting, it’s their limitation: Saurabh Sachdeva
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Mumbai, Star and acting coach Saurabh Sachdeva says he does not view negative roles as mere antagonists but as individuals with distinct personalities and motivations.

Adding to this, Actors should not blame industry for typecasting, it’s their limitation: Saurabh Sachdeva Sachdeva, known for playing intense and morally complex characters in films such as "Animal", "Vadh", "Jaane Jaan" and "Dhadak 2", believes audiences may see his characters as negative but he approaches each of them differently, looking for nuances in human behaviour.

Meanwhile, "People can typecast you, but it is the shape that I have to give to the characters. If you see all my negative characters, you might say, 'Oh, it's a negative character', but they are different human beings, different personalities," Sachdeva told PTI in an interview.
Notably, "There's so much to explore in human behaviour. That's what we don't see. If we see that, then there is so much work to do for me," he added.

As per the latest buzz, Sachdeva, who currently stars in a key role in Nitesh Tiwari's "Ramayana", shared actors should not blame the industry for typecasting as he believes it is up to them to decide whether they allow themselves to be confined to a particular image.

In further updates, "If I say I've been typecast, then it's my limitation, then I'm putting myself in a box and people will see from that box. Like, you see a negative character, I see different human beings, which have their own problems, struggles and barriers, which I've to cross.

On top of that, "And those barriers should be so strong that it enhances the protagonist. Like, in 'Vadh', if the antagonist is not so strong, then the protagonist won't be able to do anything. So, I have to take it to that level."
Before foraying into acting, Sachdeva worked behind the camera as an acting coach and he attributed his delayed start as an star to personal self-doubt.

title: Sargun Mehta says she is biggest fan of husband Ravie Dubey after watching him as Lakshman in Ramayana, calls it a personal win
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramayana Part 1, also titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, rolled out in theatres in November 5. It stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Ravie Dubey as his brother, Lakshman. Ravie's performance has been receiving praise from viewers, and the star's wife, Sargun Mehta, could not be more proud. She posted on Instagram to pen a heartfelt note to cheer for Ravie and noted how he never complained about the years and years of hard work, and patiently waited for this day to arrive.

Adding to this, Sargun Mehta cheered for Ravie Dubey after the rollout of Ramayana. What Sargun shared Sargun shared pictures of Ravie as Lakshman from the movie, as well as snippets from the shoot in her post. She wrote a long caption along with it, noting how this Diwali their ‘vanvaas’ also came to an end with the rollout of Ramayana. Sargun added, “You knew this is in your heart all along .21 years of WAIT , of highs and lows , of rejections, of judgements , of barriers lost today to your faith and perseverance.” She opened up that Ravie always kept his heart to his work and never spoke ill of others even during the worst of times.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sarggun mehta (@sargunmehta)

Notably, She shared, "No matter who i meet and what i see on the internet today , your win feels like a personal win for everyone. Your win gives hope , your win makes me believe that Achchai ki jeet hoti hai (Good always wins). My heart is so full today as I know ki jo main kehti thi - ki "mera banda rabb hai" ab sab kahengey. (Now everyone will say that my guy is the real god). I am proud wife have always been but I am also your PROUDEST and BIGGEST FAN for life. You are my light badi . May you shine brighter , brightest . Thank you for making this diwali my brightest ever."

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana marks Ravie's first major movie in a pivotal role after a storied career on television spanning over a decade. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana, along with Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman.

In further updates, Planned as a two-part saga, the movie is inspired by the ancient epic Ramayana and follows the journey of Rama, believed to be an avatar of Lord Vishnu, from his life as the prince of Ayodhya and his exile to his battle against Ravana.

On top of that, The music has been composed by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman. The first installment of Ramayana is scheduled to rollout in theatres during Diwali 2026, while the second part is expected to arrive during Diwali 2028.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 3: Saturday surge takes Ranbir Kapoor's film past ₹375 crore, beats Adipurush, Pathaan and Animal
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

After a slower first Friday, Ramayana : Part One, starring Ranbir Kapoor , Yash and Sai Pallavi, has picked up pace at the ticket-window, with Saturday bringing a big jump in collections. The Nitesh Tiwari directorial collected its biggest single-day worldwide earnings since rollout. With its three-day worldwide gross touching ₹ 375 crore rupees, the movie has already put up some impressive numbers and is now closing in on the Day 3 record of Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan.

Adding to this, ₹375 crore rupees in 3 days! Ranbir Kapoor's movie Ramayana beats Pathaan and Animal, trails Jawan, Ramayana sees a big jump on Day 3 According to trade tracker Sacnilk, the movie had a strong Saturday, collecting ₹ 83.45 crore rupees gross in India. Overseas markets added another ₹ 60 crore rupees on the day, taking the movie's total overseas gross to ₹ 157.25 crore rupees. Its worldwide gross now stands at ₹ 375.50 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, The jump is particularly noticeable when compared to Friday's numbers. Ramayana collected ₹ 57.30 crore rupees gross in India on day 2, which means Saturday saw a 45.3% rise. The movie has also gone past its opening-day India gross of ₹ 77.50 crore rupees, making Day 3 its biggest day at the domestic ticket-window so far.

Notably, Ramayana's third-day worldwide gross has already taken it past the numbers of some major Indian films. Adipurush, which also told the tale of Ramayana starring Prabhas and Kriti Sanon, had collected ₹ 304.04 crore rupees worldwide on day 3. With that collection, Ramayana is ahead by approximately 23.5%.

As per the latest buzz, However, Jawan remains the movie to beat. Shah Rukh Khan's smash hit had collected ₹ 383.18 crore rupees worldwide on day 3 whereas Dhurandhar: The Revenge starring Ranveer Singh had surpassed over ₹ 500 crore rupees mark worldwide by the third day.

In further updates, Sunday will be an important day for Ramayana, although Diwali celebrations could affect theatre footfalls, particularly during evening and night shows. The bigger opportunity may come after the festival, when the holiday period could bring more families to theatres. Monday's collections will be worth watching, especially after the strong Saturday performance.

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Sunny Deol plays Lord Hanuman, while Ravi Dubey portrays Lakshman. The ensemble also features Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Kajal Aggarwal, Indira Krishnan, and Kunal Kapoor. The sequel has been verified for 2028 rollout instead of 2027.

title: Janhvi Kapoor reveals Sridevi was unsure of her acting career, jokes her mother saw ‘potential’ in her after she got a nose job
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Janhvi Kapoor has shared an interesting memory about her late mother, Sridevi , and how she reacted to her decision to become an star. In a recent conversation with her maternal cousin, star Maheswari on Galatta Plus Tamil, Janhvi opened up that Sridevi was not entirely convinced about her entering films at first. However, she recalled a rather unexpected moment when her mother seemed to have a change of heart. According to Janhvi, it happened after she underwent a nose job.

Adding to this, Janhvi Kapoor recalls how a nose job changed Sridevi's opinion about her acting dreams: ‘Yeah, there's potential’. Sridevi had reservations about Janhvi becoming an star Looking back on the day she first told Sridevi she wanted to act, Janhvi shared her mother's unforgettable response. Sridevi gave her blessing, but not without a heavy reality check, warning Janhvi that the profession would demand everything she had. Maheswari remembered that Sridevi was not entirely convinced about Janhvi joining films, given how demanding the profession could be. “Jaanu wants to be in films, but I’m not very keen because it’s a lot of hard work, a lot of dedication, and you have to be really strong to get in there,” Maheswari recalled her saying.

Meanwhile, Janhvi then made a rather surprising revelation about what may have changed her mother's mind. Whilst laughing, she shared, “I think maybe you should cut this out, but I think before I did my nose, she was unsure. She was like, 'I don't think it's…' After I did my nose, she's like, 'Yeah, there's potential'.”

Notably, Sridevi passed away in February 2018 at the age of 54. She was in Dubai to attend the wedding celebrations of her nephew, star Mohit Marwah, when news of her sudden death emerged. The news left the movie industry and her followers in shock. According to the Dubai Police investigation, she died due to accidental drowning in her hotel apartment's bathtub following a loss of consciousness.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The makers of Ramayana : Part 1 or as it is internationally called Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, have issued a strong warning against people recording the movie inside theatres and sharing clips online. With the movie running in cinemas since November 5, the team has raised concerns over unauthorised footage being circulated on social media and messaging platforms. They have now made it clear that anyone involved in recording or distributing such content could face legal consequences. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari , the movie stars Ranbir Kapoor , Sai Pallavi and Yash in the lead roles.

Adding to this, Ramayana makers issue stern warning over leaked footage, say offenders could face criminal action. Ramayana makers cite Bombay High Court orders The movie's official social media handles shared a legal notice addressing the unauthorised recording and sharing of its footage. The makers shared they were aware of people recording portions of the movie during theatrical screenings and circulating them across various online platforms.

Meanwhile, The notice also refers to two recent Bombay High Court orders, dated November 2 and November 6, 2026, which restrict people from recording or sharing the movie without permission. It reads, “The Hon'ble Bombay High Court, by orders dated 2 November 2026 and 6 November 2026 in commercial IP suit (l) no. 37230 of 2026, has restrained all persons, known and unknown, from recording, uploading, sharing or otherwise communicating the movie or any part of it without authorisation.”

Notably, The makers have also pointed out that such actions are not limited to copyright violations and could invite criminal charges. The notice states, “Doing so is copyright infringement, a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment and fine under the Copyright Act, 1957, the Cinematograph Act, 1952, the BNS, 2023 and the IT Act, 2000, and a contempt of court.”

As per the latest buzz, Along with Sunny Deol's post-credit appearance as Lord Hanuman, which ws officially posted on the day of the rollout along with Hanuman Chalisa song, another clip from the movie has caught the attention of social media users. The footage, which is as per reports from an international version of the movie, appears to feature a scene that was left out of the Hindi rollout. It comes after Lakshman cuts off Surpanakha's nose, when a group of asuras arrive to defend her and confront Lord ama, Lakshman and Sita. The clip features an extended fight sequence, with several moments leading up to Rama taking on the asuras.

In further updates, Ramayana: Part 1 features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana. The movie is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. The ensemble cast also includes Ravie Dubey, Indira Krishna, Arun Govil, Vivek Oberoi, Sonal Jha, Lara Dutta, Kunal Kapoor, Rakul Preet Singh and Kajal Aggarwal, among others. The second part is scheduled for Diwali 2028, instead of 2027 rollout.

title: Ranbir Kapoor's stunt double from Ramayana shares unseen set pics, calls him one of the best actors
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A new behind-the-scenes post from the sets of Ramayana has revealed another detail about the movie's making. Stunt performer Luke Ioannou has shared that he doubled for Ranbir Kapoor in Nitesh Tiwari's soon-to-release epic. Luke posted several pictures from the shoot on Instagram, along with a note about his experience of working on a movie that brings the story of Ramayana to the big screen on such a large scale.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor's stunt double shares a glimpse of Ramayana's action-packed sets, reveals working on the epic. Luke Ioannou on doubling for Ranbir Kapoor Luke spoke warmly about being part of the project and working as Ranbir's stunt double. He also lauded the star, describing the opportunity as a memorable experience. Sharing the pictures, he wrote, “Feeling incredibly privileged to have been part of telling such an important story on Ramayana, stunt doubling for Ranbir Kapoor, truly one of the best actors I've had the pleasure of working with.”

Meanwhile, He also thanked Ian Van Temperley and the G Stunt Alliance Group for giving him the opportunity to work on the movie. He extended his gratitude to the cast and crew, acknowledging everyone he worked with during the shoot. He added, “An unforgettable journey, and truly humbled to have been a part of it.”

Notably, The pictures shared by Luke offer a closer look at how the movie's elaborate scenes are being shot. One image shows a performer dressed in a traditional golden-brown outfit, with layers of rudraksha beads and his hair tied in a topknot next to Ranbir. Other pictures show a detailed costume featuring a leather-like chest piece and a maroon dhoti, with artificial rocky structures in the background.

Another picture shows a massive camera rig positioned for a shot, giving a sense of the equipment involved in filming these sequences.

In further updates, Luke has worked on several major international productions, including Wonder Woman, Wonder Woman 1984, No Time to Die and The Batman. His credits also include the fantasy series House of the Dragon, which features elaborate action sequences and large-scale battle scenes.

title: Nanncy Gill talks Udta Teer, working with Ayushmann Khurrana, directing plays and why she chose the UK over cashing in on fame
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nanncy Gill, of late seen as a Counter Terrorist Squad (CTS) agent in Ayushmann Khurrana -starrer Udta Teer , is expanding her wings with her ongoing course in the UK. She is pursuing an MA in screen and stage from the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama in Cardiff , Wales, and is looking to take up international projects besides working in India.

Adding to this, Star Nanncy Gill and with Ayushmann Khurrana and other team members on the set of her last rollout Utda Teer. The Raisinghani vs Raisinghani (2024) star says, “After getting attention in a successful movie, the obvious thing is to cash in on the moment and look for opportunities in India, which I am getting, but I have a bigger picture in mind. I first want to complete my course and improve my craft and come with full force besides exploring opportunities here. I just wanted to expand my artistic choices.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nanncy Gill (@inanncygill)

Notably, She is looking forward to expanding in India and abroad. "I don't just want to be a screen star. I really love theatre also and I want to be a complete artist. In the direction of my career, I want to be an star, writer and theatre director, building my career in the UK as well."

As per the latest buzz, Gill got this confidence by dabbling deeply in theatre. "I'm not only limited to being an star now. I wrote, produced and directed my own theatre plays and that gave me a different viewpoint. So, I want to build an international career and this is the right time for me. Leaving India at a high point of my career was tough but I had to make a hard choice."

In further updates, Back in India, she directed two plays, House Arrest and Mandi House . “After Mumbai, we did Delhi's Shri Ram Center and people really loved it. I have started getting opportunities here. I shot for a BBC short movie two weeks back for experience. Besides, I have written a play, which I have submitted to my college and if they approve it, I'm going to get all the production to do a ticketed play. Once that happens, I can develop my own. In the UK, theatre is big, so opportunities are there where I can bring my Indian roots into play!”

On top of that, Playing CTS agent Sharon, she was part of the team with Ayushmann. "Shooting with him was really great as he is a very humble person and he makes everyone so comfortable. We shot for 45 days in Manali. Of course, some of my scenes and dialogues were cut but the makers are the best judge. But having a presence throughout the movie is a big deal and a great experience. It's humbling to see people posting stories and appreciation coming my way. After the OTT rollout, the visibility will be more."

She recalls being in Dubai when she got the call. “Besides my audition, they wanted to see my fitness and action videos. I put them together with my gym, kalaripayattu, boxing and MMA ones and sent them. I got selected and then came to know what project it was for. We did lots of tough action sequences under Korean action director Oh Se-Yeong and it was great fun. Interestingly, I watched it in London, in a theatre, and people were like, 'Hey, you're in the movie.' It felt nice.”

title: Amitabh Bachchan wins personality rights case; Delhi High Court passes final decree after four defendants settle
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Court held that the right to control the commercial use of an individual's identity falls under the “right to publicity”. It observed that Bachchan's name and photographs had been used without permission in ways that could falsely suggest his endorsement of products or services.

Adding to this, The star had approached the Court over the alleged unauthorised use of his identity across different platforms and merchandise. These included a mobile application titled Amitabh Bachchan Video Call, messages promoting a purported Kaun Banega Crorepati lottery, a general knowledge quiz book featuring his photograph, T-shirts, posters and domain names incorporating his identity.
Meanwhile, The Court noted that the unauthorised use involved Bachchan's “very name and photographs” and found that the requirements for protecting his publicity rights had been met.

Notably, The final decree also covers unidentified individuals, commonly referred to as John Does. The Court took note of the continued use of Bachchan's persona through anonymous websites, applications, posters and messaging platforms, observing that those responsible may not always be identifiable.

As per the latest buzz, Four defendants, Rajat Nagi, Manoj Publications, Tamatina and Mahesh Patel, settled the matter with Bachchan and acknowledged his publicity and privacy rights. As part of the settlement, the defendants agreed to discontinue the use of his identity. The commitments included deleting the video-call application, stopping publication of the quiz book and sale of posters, and deleting the domain name amitabhbachchan.in.

In further updates, The remaining defendants did not appear before the Court or file written statements despite being served. The Court held that the case did not involve disputed facts requiring a trial and granted a summary judgment against them. It also clarified that Bachchan could initiate fresh proceedings if further unauthorised use of his persona occurs.
On top of that, The November 2022 interim injunction now stands merged with the final decree.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramayana Part 1, also titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, rolled out in theatres in November 5. Viewers who have seen the movie were treated with one of its biggest reveals in the post-credit scene. It is Sunny Deol who makes an appearance as Lord Hanuman in the closing moments. The star makes his appearance in a post-credit scene, offering a first glimpse of his character and setting up his role in the second installment.

Adding to this, Sunny Deol poses at the special screening of Ramayana: Part 1 in Mumbai. (ANI Photo) (Sunil Khandare) On Saturday, Sunny posted on Instagram to share his review of the movie and urged every Hindustani to support it. He shared, “I just watched Ramayana. I really, really liked it. I urge each and every Hindustani to watch it. This movie is not less than any Hollywood movie. But I would say it is better than them. The special effects truly transport the viewer to that time. It is my request to all of you and tell you to go and watch it.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sunny Deol (@iamsunnydeol)

Notably, Meanwhile, the post credit scene opens with a powerful musical backdrop, as Hanuman makes his entry. While his face remains hidden, a wider shot towards the end shows him flying through the air with his gada as he hails Jai Shri Ram. The Hanuman Chalisa, sung by Diljit Dosanjh, Sukhwinder Singh, Mohit Chauhan, Kailash Kher and Anirudh Ravichander, plays in the background, adding to the impact of the moment. The makers have revealed just enough to build curiosity around Sunny's portrayal without giving away his complete look. Before Hanuman's appearance, the movie also offers a glimpse of Raghav Juyal as Meghnada, Ravana's eldest son and the crown prince of Lanka.

As per the latest buzz, Hanuman's arrival also marks a significant point in the Ramayana for the sequel which will arrive in 2028. He becomes one of the most important figures in Rama's journey after Ravana abducts Sita. From finding her in Lanka to helping Rama prepare for the war against Ravana, Hanuman plays a crucial role in the events that follow.

In further updates, Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. It is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. Ranbir plays Ram in the movie, Sai plays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana. The movie also stars Ravi Dubey as Lakshmana, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanaka, Arun Govil as Dasharatha, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi, Shobana as Kaikashi, Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari, and more.

On top of that, The first part delves into Ravana’s backstory, setting up the tale till his abduction of Sita after a fight with Jatayu, voiced by Anupam Kher. It also shows Ram’s childhood and upbringing, his marriage to Sita, the circumstances of his 14-year exile, and his vow to bring Sita back from Ravana.

title: Dhanush says no one other than Sai Pallavi could have played Sita in Ramayana, calls her a great performer
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Dhanush has lauded his OM co-star Sai Pallavi for her devotion and her craft as an star. The star was speaking at a pre-rollout event of the movie, where he shared how he does not understand the chatter around the casting of Sai as Sita in Ramayana. Dhanush shared that even if there was a search in whole of India for the role of Sita, no one could have done justice to the part other than Sai Pallavi.

Adding to this, Sai Pallavi at the premiere of Ramayana at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello) (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello) What Dhanush shared Dhanush spoke about Sai on stage and shared how they first worked together in Maari 2, when she was extremely shy off camera and a person with few words. After nine years when the two of them worked again in OM, Dhanush shared that he was surprised at the complete transformation of Sai. “She stood there as if she totally mastered the art of cinema. In her poise, in her expressions, there was so much confidence. It was truly astonishing. Playing this role was not easy at all but she bravely took the chance and did it so well,” he shared.

Meanwhile, In OM, Sai plays a CBI officer Nithya Reddy tasked with investigating the illegal red sandalwood trade. The first glimpse offered a look at her character's past and the personal loss that drives her investigation, bringing her into the orbit of characters played by Dhanush and Mammootty.

Notably, Dhanush then went ahead and congratulated Sai on the rollout of Ramayana, where she plays the character of Sita. He added, “There is so much noise around her portrayal of Sita. I don't understand it. Even during shot breaks, she would be praying constantly. She is someone with such profound devotion to God, someone with such a pure heart. She looks so beautiful and she is a great performer.”
