title: Pyre director Vinod Kapri says 75% shows of film has been cut down within first week, reveals theatre owners were told only one film will be shown
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

National Award-winning fimmaker Vinod Kapri’s Pyre rolled out in theatres last week to rave reviews. The movie tells the story of an elderly couple who continue to wait for their children, even as life in their Himalayan village grows quieter with each passing day. On Saturday, the filmmaker took to X to share that majority of the shows of the movie has been removed for a bigger movie to rollout and theatre owners were told that only one movie will play now.

Adding to this, Vinod Kapri's Hindi movie Pyre rolled out in theatres across India on October 30 ‘This is not fair’ In a video post, the filmmaker shared that he did not want to make this video statement because of the need of the hour. He shared that Pyre had a limited rollout from the beginning, in around 80 screens. But because of the love that the movie got, the number extended to 400. But, since the last two days, 75% of the shows have been cut of Pyre and now the number is less than 100.

Meanwhile, “We are in touch with theatre owners and distributors. They have been told that no other movie will be running in theatres except one movie. I do not understand why you have to run your movie by stopping other films? Is this a win of good over evil? Is there any honor in doing this? The honor with which we tell a story. This is a small movie, with non actors, and people are crying after seeing it. What honor, truth and goodness do you boast when this is the way theatres are ordered? I urge theatre owners and distributors to not do this with Pyre. If you have spent a lot of money, then we have spent our soul in making a movie. We deserve a fair chance,” he shared.

Notably, “This is not fair, not to Pyre. Not to your audience,” read the caption of the post. Although Vinod did not name the big movie in question, the big rollout over the last two days is Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash in lead roles. The movie rolled out in theatres on November 5 and has already crossed ₹ 155 crore rupees so far.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 3: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi film sees growth on Saturday, crosses ₹182 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana rolled out in theatres on November 5. The movie did great business on its opening day, setting a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. However, the collections hit a dip on the second day, given it was a non-holiday and right before the weekend. The movie is expected to pick up pace on Saturday ahead of Diwali and recover during the weekend. It remains to be seen how Ramayana fares in its first weekend, so let us take a detailed look at the ticket-window performance so far.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor is portraying Lord Rama in the movie Ramayana. Ramayana ticket-window update Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 days before rollout. By the time of its rollout, the movie had already sold tickets worth ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. The movie went on to collect ₹ 64.85 crore rupees in India on its first day of rollout, becoming the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. Friday saw a dip, and the movie collected only ₹ 48.05 crore rupees. Despite Yash ’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version has started extremely slowly. On Saturday though, the occupancy rate of the Kannada version improved.

Meanwhile, By 10 PM on day 3, the movie had collected ₹ 69.80 crore rupees net in India, taking its three-day haul to ₹ 182.70 crore rupees , according to the trade website Sacnilk. This shows that the movie has managed to show a significant improvement on Saturday. The movie is now eyeing the ₹ 200 crore rupees mark, which it is expected to cross by Sunday.

Notably, By the end of day 3, Adipurush had collected above ₹ 200 crore rupees net in India. It remains to be seen whether Ramayana can cross that mark. However, it must be noted that Adipurush’s first three days in theatres were a Friday, Saturday and Sunday, while Ramayana’s first three days included a working Thursday and Friday, and then Saturday. However, Ramayana has managed to beat the opening-day hauls of blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 57 crore rupees), Animal ( ₹ 63 crore rupees), and Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 62 crore rupees).

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu and his battle against the asura king Ravana after the latter abducts his wife, Sita.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

title: Farah Khan says the film industry makes people insecure about themselves, admits she felt the same before making her first film Main Hoon Na
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Farah Khan has worn many hats in her decades-long career as a choreographer, filmmaker, show judge, and now, a YouTuber. In a recent chat with Neha Dhupia, Angad Bedi on their podcast, Farah was asked about her recent hit YouTube channel, in which she visits the houses of her star friends with her cook Dilip. Farah shared that she did not plan of continuing her channel for so long but it has been a welcome change in her lifestyle.

Adding to this, Farah Khan shared why she started her YouTube channel. What Farah shared When Neha congratulated Farah on her YouTube channel and asked that now that it has crossed 300 episodes and become such a big hit, did she plan this from the beginning? Farah denied any planning for the YouTube channel and shared that she had some free time after finishing her script for her next movie and started her YouTube journey to not feel angsty in that period. She shared, “Later everyone shared that I pivoted at the right time but that is all destiny. I get angsty and if one is not doing anything then after waking up they think that my movie is not hapenning and someone else is making theirs. I can't go through that. I have been through it when I wanted to make my first movie.”

Meanwhile, “This industry makes you insecure. Because at all times you are comparing yourself to somebody else. That this star is doing this movie and what not. When I hit 50, I told myself that I want to detach, cut off and live a happy life. But ofcourse, we are hustlers and YouTube is something that I didn't realise that there was a lack of family-oriented content perhaps and people liked it and ofcourse they liked Dilip. As we went along, we kept tweaking the format,” she added.

Notably, Farah Khan's YouTube channel currently has over 3 million followers. In her vlogs, Farah visits the homes of celebrities to cook new dishes with them in their kitchens, gives viewers a tour of their homes, and indulges in fun conversations over food. Her quirky banter with her cook Dilip has become the highlight of the videos, helping him rise to social media fame. In one of the vlogs, the filmmaker also admitted to having increased Dilip’s salary since they began their YouTube journey.

As per the latest buzz, Farah made her directorial debut with Main Hoon Na in 2004. It starred Shah Rukh Khan and Sushmita Sen. She then directed Om Shanti Om with Shah Rukh Khan, and Tees Maar Khan with Akshay Kumar. Her last directorial was Happy New Year, which rolled out in 2014.

title: Vivek Oberoi recalls being ostracised from Bollywood for standing up against what he perceived as wrong; says filmmakers got calls from underworld
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Vivek Oberoi was considered one of the rising stars in the early 2000s thanks to films like Company and Saathiya. However, one press conference in 2003 seemed to change it all for him. Now, years later, Vivek claimed on the Relearn podcast that he was ‘in hell’ during the fallout of the row. He also claimed that filmmakers who wanted to work with him would get calls from the underworld, warning them against it.

Adding to this, Vivek Oberoi most of late starred in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. (AFP) Vivek Oberoi recalls being ostracised from Bollywood Vivek was asked to talk about the row he faced in the early 2000s even as his career was taking off. Without taking names or getting into details of what happened, he shared, “It was a very dark phase in my life. I tried to stand up for something. I came from the thought process that there’s a certain line you don’t cross. Women have to be respected and treated a certain way. I stood up to what I perceived was wrong, and I started being bullied a lot. Despite delivering successes, hits, and awards, a very powerful lobby took over. I became persona non grata. I would have people pulling out of films I had signed.”

Meanwhile, He also claimed that everything ‘snowballed and just got worse’ for him, with filmmakers dropping him from projects. And those who stood by him would allegedly receive calls from the underworld. “Those who decided to stick by me for ethical reasons would suddenly call me a few weeks later and say, listen man, I got a call from the underworld. I had gangsters calling me, saying that, you movie with this guy and you’re done; you’re toast. I went through real hell, real misery. I didn’t get the work not because I wasn’t able to deliver. It wasn’t based on talent. It wasn’t based on performance. It wasn’t based on work ethic. It was based on something that I couldn’t control,” shared Vivek.

Notably, Vivek experienced career fluctuations after early success. He even tried to play morally grey and dark characters in films such as Krrish 3, Vivegam, and Lucifer. After starring in Kesari Veer and Masti 4 in 2025, he starred in Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana Part 1 this year. The star played Ravana’s brother-in-law and Surpanaka’s husband, Vidyutjihva, in the movie. He now has Sandeep Reddy Vanga’s Spirit lined up for rollout. The movie stars Prabhas and Triptii Dimri in lead roles. It will be rolled out next year.

title: Ranbir Kapoor reveals plans for directorial debut, says he wants to move behind the camera in 2-3 years: ‘It's my last decade as an actor’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor has started working on a script for his directorial debut. The star, who is currently seen as Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana : Part 1, spoke about his plans to move behind the camera during an interview with co-star Sai Pallavi for BBC Asian News Network. While he hasn't decided on all the details of his first movie, Ranbir knows the kind of story he wants to tell. He is hoping to begin shooting it in the next two or three years, once he has wrapped up his current acting projects.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor says he is 'dying to direct a movie', reveals plans to make his first movie in 2-3 years. (PTI) Ranbir Kapoor on writing his first movie Ranbir opened up that he started working on a script a few months ago, but the experience has been far more challenging than he expected. Writing has given him a new respect for the people who create stories and bring them to life on screen. He also spoke about the satisfaction of being a director and having the opportunity to bring different people together to tell a story.

Meanwhile, Explaining what appeals to him about the craft, he shared, “I just started writing a script a couple of months back, and it’s so hard to create. I have so much respect for writers and creators. ‘How do you create?’ It’s exciting because I truly believe that after a musician, if there’s somebody who feels a creative high, it’s the director. An star’s high is very superficial but the director, when he directs a movie, however good or bad, the opportunity to tell a story and get all these people together to tell your story, it’s just a beautiful experience and I hope I can do it.”

Notably, Ranbir is still figuring out what his first movie as a director will look like, but he has a fair idea of the kind of stories he wants to tell. He mentioned Life is Beautiful, It's a Wonderful Life and Rajkumar Hirani's films among his favourites, and shared he would like to make a family drama that leaves people with a warm, feel-good experience.

As per the latest buzz, He also explained how he hopes to balance direction with his acting career. Ranbir shared he usually works for around 100 to 125 days a year, leaving him time to write and develop ideas. Sharing his plans, he shared, “I work only 100-125 days a year; I have a lot of time to write stories. I’ve never ever been so busy, never ever been so committed. I’ve always had one movie out, and then I would start working on the other movie. But, I guess, it’s my last decade as an star; will I get to play these parts? I do want to kind of pivot towards direction. I don’t want to direct myself for sure. I really want to get these films done (Brahmastra 2, Animal 2 and Ramayana Part 2), and really get on floors with my directorial debut within 2 or 3 years, I hope.”

In further updates, After Ramayana: Part One, Ranbir will be starring in Love & War . The Sanjay Leela Bhansali directorial also features Alia Bhatt and Vicky Kaushal and is set to rollout on January 21, 2027. The star also has Animal Park, helmed by Sandeep Reddy Vanga and then Ramayana: Part Two for 2028.

title: Exclusive| Hansal Mehta on Ranveer Singh starrer Pralay row: Mumbai, the home of Indian cinema has become most unfriendly to shoot in
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Hansal Mehta has responded to the row over the shoot of R anveer Singh -starrer Pralay at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan, saying the team had secured the required permissions. The row began after the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) raised objections to the six-hour shoot, claiming it forced the postponement of inter-school cricket matches. The association has questioned why a ground used by young cricketers was made available for a commercial movie shoot.

Adding to this, Hansal Mehta, Ranveer Singh In conversation with us Mehta says, “Our shoot at Azad Maidan was fully permitted. We have requisite permission letters from police departments, sports departments including an acknowledgement of the same from MCA. The larger problem is this. Mumbai is the home of Indian cinema. It has also become a most unfriendly city to shoot in. A single location needs clearances from multiple departments, each with its own process, its own delays and its own power to stop a shoot. Even when you have every permission, you are treated as if you are trespassing.”

Meanwhile, He adds that so many other states welcome movie crews. He says, “They understand that a shoot brings jobs, business and visibility. Here, we are met with obstruction. I say this with much sadness as a proud Mumbaikar and Maharashtrian - This is why so many of us now prefer to shoot outside Mumbai.”

Notably, However he continues saying he wants to shoot in Mumbai. “I have worked in this city for over three decades. I love it and I want to keep telling its stories here. But filmmakers will go where they are allowed to work. If Mumbai wants to remain the centre of this industry, it has to stop treating its own filmmakers as a nuisance.We followed every rule no matter how complicated or difficult it may be. We will continue to do so. We simply seek the cooperation of the authorities and a much needed lack of mistrust in doing so.”

title: Arunachal govt releases 4 Siang dam protesters, seeks fresh dialogue
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Arunachal Pradesh government on Saturday rolled out four protesters detained during the agitation against the proposed 1,000-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), signalling an attempt to end the prolonged standoff with organisations opposing the project.

Adding to this, A formal response from SIFF is awaited. (HT Sourced Photo) The four protesters — Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron — were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, following protests in the Siang Valley.

Meanwhile, Their rollout came a day after the chief minister’s office (CMO), in a letter dated November 6, informed the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum (SIFF) of the government’s decision to free the detainees as a goodwill gesture aimed at creating an atmosphere conducive to dialogue and reconciliation.
Notably, The government also approved the reinstatement of gaon buras and gaon buris (traditional village authorities) who faced disciplinary action in connection with the agitation.

As per the latest buzz, These decisions address two of the major concerns raised by SIFF, which had earlier refused to engage in talks with Chief Minister Pema Khandu until its demands were fulfilled.

In further updates, However, uncertainty remains over two other key demands — the withdrawal of security forces from the affected areas and the withdrawal of criminal cases registered against protesters.

On top of that, Responding to SIFF’s demand for the immediate withdrawal of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel, the government maintained that decisions regarding security deployment must be guided by law-and-order considerations and public safety.
It nevertheless expressed its willingness to discuss the issue during the proposed meeting, taking into account the prevailing security situation.

title: Nitesh Tiwari says he believes Homer was inspired by Ramayana for The Odyssey; Ranbir Kapoor calls bow-lifting scene coincidence
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana hit screens on November 5. But much before that, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey had followers pumped for it purely because of a scene involving a queen choosing her groom and a bow and arrow. Nitesh and Ranbir Kapoor , who plays Lord Rama, of late discussed the parallels between the Indian epic and Homer’s Odyssey.

Adding to this, Queen Penelope and Sita both ask suitors and lift and string a complicated bow in The Odyssey and Ramayana. Nitesh Tiwari, Ranbir Kapoor on The Odyssey, Ramayana Talking to Screen Rant , Nitesh shared that he believed Homer might have been inspired by the Ramayana, given the parallels in the stories. “Ramayana is the oldest epic, and I believe Homer was inspired by Ramayana in some way; having written those bits in Odyssey. And yes, I did notice those equivalents and I felt very happy that our greatest epic has got a tribute in another epic which belongs to the West side, and it's going to make it very easier for the people to also connect with what we were trying to bring to the West also,” he shared.

Meanwhile, Ranbir pointed out that the Ramayana was written thousands of years ago, but called the parallels a sweet coincidence, particularly in the bow-lifting scene. “To be honest, it's written in our text 4,000 years ago. So actually, when I saw Odyssey, I thought, 'That's from Ramayana.' Exactly. But yeah, sweet coincidence. I love The Odyssey . I love Christopher Nolan. But yeah, doing Ramayana had a very different feeling,” shared the star. He also shared that he had ‘goosebumps’ while performing the scene, and could feel a ‘weird current going up and down’ when he lifted the bow.

Notably, During the climax of The Odyssey, Odysseus (Matt Damon) has been away for too long and presumed dead. Penelope (Anne Hathaway) is willing to finally select a suitor, but only if they pass the test she has set for them. The suitors must not just string a bow that only her husband has been able to, but they must also fire an arrow through 12 axe heads to win her in marriage.

As per the latest buzz, While this scene is a setup for something far more than it seems on the surface, it was hard for the Indian audience not to draw parallels to Sita's swayamvar. In Ramayana, suitors are called to Mithila by King Janaka to seek his daughter Sita’s hand in marriage. Suitors must be able to lift a bow called Shivadhanush, which only she has managed to lift so far. Rama not only lifts it, but he also breaks it by mistake while stringing it. Sai Pallavi plays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana in Ramayana.

title: Two deer killed by suspected poachers in Rajasthan's Barmer; villagers stage protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
Two deer were allegedly killed by poachers in Rajasthan's Barmer district, triggering protests by villagers demanding the immediate arrest of those responsible, officials shared.

Adding to this, Villagers alleged that the poachers were using an iron container filled with stones to produce sounds to attract deer. (Representative Image/Unsplash) The incident occurred on Friday night near Nehron Ki Nadi and Bisarniya villages in the Dhanau police station area.
Meanwhile, According to villagers, the suspected poachers killed two deer and allegedly tied the legs of one carcass before hanging it upside down from a tree.
Notably, The suspects were as per reports chasing a third deer when they reached a cattle enclosure belonging to Kanwararam Choudhary.
As per the latest buzz, Villagers alleged that the poachers were using an iron container filled with stones to produce sounds to attract deer.
In further updates, The noise disturbed cattle in the enclosure, alerting villagers, who raised an alarm. The suspects fled under the cover of darkness.
On top of that, Following the incident, villagers gathered and began a sit-in protest, demanding the arrest of the accused and stronger measures to protect wildlife.
On receiving information, a Forest Department team, Dhanau police personnel and Chohtan Circle Officer Jetharam reached the spot and initiated an investigation.

title: How far should films go in depicting violence? Experts weigh in on its impact on kids
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
“There are a few emotions that are very easy to provoke the audience with. Violence is one of them, and sex is another.”

Adding to this, Recent cases of children and young adults involved in violent incidents reignited debate over violence in films. This observation by Aamir Khan in an old interview resurfaced on social media when Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Animal was rolled out in 2023. Among the many aspects of the movie that sparked debate, its graphic violence became a major talking point online. However, Animal was far from the only movie to face criticism over its portrayal of violence. Over the past five years, several blockbusters across movie industries have been called out on social media for not just depicting extreme violence but also seemingly glorifying it on the big screen. The Dhurandhar duology, which emerged as the highest-grossing Indian films of 2025 and 2026, is among the latest and biggest examples.
Meanwhile, Violence in cinema has always been a subject of debate, but the two recent troubling real-life instances have once again brought the conversation into focus.

Notably, In Haryana's Panchkula, an eight-year-old boy allegedly assaulted a six-year-old girl inside a school classroom, repeatedly hitting her with an object that appeared to be a brick. In another disturbing incident in Andhra Pradesh, a 21-year-old allegedly entered a Class 10 classroom carrying a chainsaw and attacked a girl student, leaving two injured.

As per the latest buzz, While there is no direct link between these incidents and what we see in films, the graphic nature of these cases has once again raised questions about how far filmmakers should go when depicting violence on screen. For instance, in Dhurandhar, Akshaye Khanna's character, Rehman Dakait, is seen smashing a man's face. In Animal, Ranbir Kapoor's character enters a college classroom carrying a rifle to intimidate students.

In further updates, The debate is not limited to Hindi cinema. When Rajinikanth's Jailer was rolled out in 2023, its graphic sequences, including scenes involving torture and acid, drew criticism from some viewers. Similarly, Allu Arjun's smash hit Pushpa 2: The Rule, the highest-grossing Indian movie of 2024, drew criticism for its graphic climax sequences, with some viewers finding the brutality on screen hard to digest.

On top of that, With screens becoming an increasingly unavoidable part of children's lives, monitoring the content they consume has become important. Experts point out that younger children may not always have the ability to distinguish between fiction and reality and, hence, they can’t fully understand the consequences of imitating what they see on screen.

Dr Subhrajit Parida, consultant, paediatrics and neonatology, Manipal Hospital, Bhubaneswar, explains that children can imitate the behaviour of characters they admire, particularly heroes who are often rewarded for their violent actions.

title: Delhi High Court rules Doosra infringed Sourav Ganguly's personality rights, directs makers to deposit Rs. 2 crores
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The ruling comes in connection with a lawsuit filed by Sourav Ganguly along with Luv Films over the unauthorised use of his identity and life events in the movie. The Court has also restrained the makers from releasing Doosra on OTT platforms or through any other medium.

Adding to this, According to the Court's observations, elements of Ganguly's personality and incidents from his life are closely connected to the movie's narrative. This makes it difficult to remove the portions in question from the final cut. The Court, therefore, directed the makers to include prominent disclaimers to clarify the nature of the movie's association with the former cricketer.

Meanwhile, The disclaimers must explicitly state that Ganguly did not give consent for the commercial use or depiction of his persona in the movie. They must also clarify that the project does not have any official association or authorisation from him.

Notably, The ruling brings attention to the legal issues surrounding the use of public figures' identities and personal histories in films and other commercial projects. Personality rights generally protect individuals against the unauthorised commercial exploitation of aspects such as their name, image and likeness.

title: Hansal Mehta denies cricket body's claims of match disruptions over Ranveer Singh's Pralay shoot in Mumbai, says team had Azad Maidan clearance
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Hansal Mehta has responded to the row over the shoot of Ranveer Singh-starrer Pralay at Mumbai's Azad Maidan, saying the team had secured the required permissions. The row began after the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) raised objections to the six-hour shoot, claiming it forced the postponement of inter-school cricket matches. The association has questioned why a ground used by young cricketers was made available for a commercial movie shoot.

Adding to this, Pralay shoot row: Hansal Mehta rejects MCA's claims, says team had permission to movie at Azad Maidan. Hansal, meanwhile, maintained that the production had secured all the required permissions before filming at Azad Maidan. In conversation with Mumbai Mirror, he also criticised the hurdles filmmakers face while shooting in Mumbai, saying, “But I would like to underscore that Mumbai has been rendered a no-go zone for movie shoots because of bureaucratic hurdles. And people like you fuel the fire.”

Meanwhile, The MCA shared it had written to the Maharashtra government's Sports Department, seeking an explanation for allowing the Pralay shoot at Azad Maidan. As per the report, the association shared it was not consulted before the permission was issued, even though it is responsible for maintaining the ground and its pitches. The shoot required a large set to be put up and artificial grass to be laid, which left the MCA with no choice but to reschedule Under-14 and Under-16 inter-school matches already on the calendar.

Notably, MCA Apex Council member Nadim Memon shared Azad Maidan was already losing space to activities unrelated to sport. A section of the ground had been taken over for the Aqua Line Metro work, but the contractors had not moved out despite repeated reminders. The Mumbai Police also continued to occupy the premises instead of returning to their original location. He questioned why a movie shoot was now being allowed when the ground was already dealing with these issues. He accused the Sports Department of giving commercial bookings priority over the needs of young sportspersons and shared its decisions were affecting the cricketing culture that Azad Maidan has supported for years.

As per the latest buzz, Nadim shared this was the first time a movie had been shot at the ground and questioned the disruption caused to players and ongoing tournaments. He shared, “This is the first time a movie shoot has taken place at Azad Maidan. Large sets were erected, and artificial grass was laid for the shoot of Pralay. This is not a movie-shooting venue but a cricket ground where players hone their skills to progress to the international level. Our ongoing tournaments were disrupted because of the shoot. Who will take responsibility for this loss? You cannot commercially exploit a cricket ground by allowing a commercial movie shoot.”

In further updates, The report shared that the Maharashtra government had allowed Light Rays, the production house behind Pralay, to use 5,000 square yards of Azad Maidan for a six-hour shoot. The company paid ₹ 40,000 for the booking and deposited another ₹ 40,000 as security, which is refundable. The permission was signed by Sports Department Under Secretary Ashok Damayyawar on October 30 and sent on November 2. It came with conditions, including no vehicles on the pitches and no cooking or digging on the ground. The production was also required to obtain an NOC from the MCA. The association, however, says it was not consulted before the department approved the shoot.

On top of that, Deputy Director of Sports, Mumbai Division, Navnath Fartade, defended the decision, saying a government resolution allows Azad Maidan to host non-sporting events for up to 30 days in a year. The MCA is concerned that allowing commercial shoots at the ground could lead to more such bookings and leave even less room for cricket. Azad Maidan regularly hosts inter-school and age-group tournaments, coaching sessions and club matches. The association wants the Sports Department to prioritise these activities and ensure that young players do not lose access to the ground due to commercial events.

Ranveer Singh is leading the movie Pralay, a survival thriller set in a post-catastrophic Mumbai. Set in a post-apocalyptic world, the movie follows the zombie threat as people struggle to survive in a city pushed to the edge. Directed by Jai Mehta, the movie is being mounted on a large scale for a theatrical rollout.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 2: Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash film overtakes Adipurush with ₹221 crore haul
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana Part 1 was rolled out in theatres on November 5, receiving mixed reviews and decent box-office numbers. The movie, which had a lower opening than Om Raut’s Prabhas, Kriti Sanon, and Saif Ali Khan-starrer Adipurush, seemed to recover on its second day. The Ranbir Kapoor , Sai Pallavi, and Yash-starrer has now overtaken the previous Ramayana adaptation.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash play Rama and Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window earnings Ramayana grossed ₹ 127.50 crore rupees on its opening day, compared to Adipurush's ₹ 128 crore rupees, despite the latter not having as wide an opening as the Nitesh movie. While the movie saw a dip in collections in India on its second day, bringing in ₹ 48.05 crore rupees net versus the ₹ 64.85 crore rupees opening, the movie managed to outpace Adipurush in worldwide collections.

Meanwhile, Ramayana collected ₹ 35 crore rupees from overseas on its second day, taking its overseas gross to ₹ 86.25 crore rupees, according to the trade website Sacnilk. Adding to that, the ₹ 134.80 crore rupees gross collection from India in two days takes its two-day worldwide haul to ₹ 221.05 crore rupees. Adipurush had grossed ₹ 215.78 crore rupees worldwide in two days. Ramayana, however, had a much wider rollout than Adipurush , with 23,316 shows in India alone, compared to 16,120 for the latter movie.

Notably, Compared to other juggernauts, despite the difference in genre, Ramayana is lagging behind Aditya Dhar’s Dhurandhar: The Revenge. The Ranveer Singh-starrer had grossed ₹ 358.86 crore rupees in two days. It is also behind Ranbir’s previous movie, Animal, with Sandeep Reddy Vanga, which grossed ₹ 236.01 crore rupees in two days. But with the movie now entering its first weekend, and Sunday being Diwali, it remains to be seen how much it collects before facing a weekday slump.

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari , who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. It is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. Ranbir plays Ram, Sai plays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana in this adaptation of the Indian epic. It also stars Ravi Dubey, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta in key roles.

title: Farah Khan admits film industry insiders were unsure of Shreya Ghoshal for Main Hoon Na songs
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Shreya Ghoshal has sung some of the most melodious songs in Bollywood over the last two decades. The singer won her first National Award as a playback singer for her debut with Devdas itself, at a very young age. Filmmaker and YouTuber Farah Khan visited Shreya's Mumbai residence for her latest vlog, where they chatted about their long correspondence, which began with the rollout of Main Hoon Na. The 2004 rollout also included songs sung by Shreya.

Adding to this, Farah Khan and Shreya Ghoshal recalled memories of the making of Main Hoon Na. Farah recalls how many doubted Shreya But at the time the songs were being recorded for the Shah Rukh Khan-starrer, Shreya was a brand-newcomer, and her songs from Devdas weren't rolled out. Farah and Shreya recalled memories from that time during their conversation. Farah opened up that several people from the movie industry had even told her not to work with such a young singer, questioning her ability to pull off the songs. But Farah, as well as music composer Anu Malik, firmly believed in Shreya’s talent and went ahead with her.

Meanwhile, Shreya shared, “When I saw Sushmita on screen… how beautiful she looked, and I was wondering whether I had done justice to the songs.” Farah added, “You sang Main Hoon Na (title track) also very well, that little portion for Amrita Rao… and after hearing that, we gave you the Sushmita track in the movie. So many people called me and asked why I was taking this new girl, that I was making a big mistake! But I shared that I wanted a fresh voice.”
Notably, Shreya Ghoshal sang two tracks for the 2004 Bollywood movie Main Hoon Na, composed by Anu Malik with lyrics by Javed Akhtar. They were the title track, and the song Tumhe Jo Maine Dekha.

As per the latest buzz, Main Hoon Na, rolled out in 2004, marked Farah Khan’s directorial debut and starred Shah Rukh Khan, Sushmita Sen, Suniel Shetty, Amrita Rao and Zayed Khan. The movie follows Major Ram, who goes undercover as a college student while working on a military mission. Alongside its action and romance, the movie also focuses on family relationships and Ram’s bond with his half-brother Lakshman. It became a commercial success and remains one of the popular Hindi films of the 2000s.

title: CJP protest LIVE: CJP calls out to ‘cockroaches for Kerala’ ahead of 4pm anti-SIR protest in Kochi
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

CJP protest live updates: The Kochi march will be CJP's first major protest since some of its leaders were arrested in Delhi last month while attempting to hold a demonstration at Jantar Mantar. CJP protest live updates: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will hold a protest march in Kerala's Kochi today, demanding the withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Titled “Jantar Mantar at Kochi”, the demonstration will take place at Rajendra Maidan from 4 pm, the group shared in a post on X. ...Read More

Adding to this, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and star-activist Prakash Raj are among those scheduled to attend. The stir will also be joined by CJP national leader Afreen Nawaz and its South India in-charge Vijay Reddy Mallangi. CJP's first major protest after Delhi crackdown The Kochi march will be CJP's first major protest since some of its leaders were arrested in Delhi last month while attempting to hold a demonstration at Jantar Mantar against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR exercise. CJP co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested after entering Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The Delhi Police had denotified the site as a designated protest venue last month. Dipke was later detained ahead of a Tiranga March revealed by the party in Delhi. The Delhi Police crime branch also of late questioned CJP leaders in connection with cases linked to protests in the national capital. BJP vs CJP over ‘foreign funding’ Union minister Jitendra Singh launched an attack on the CJP earlier this week, alleging that activists were receiving funds from anti-India organisations operating within and outside the country. In conversation with the media in Bengaluru, Singh claimed there was sufficient evidence to show that Dipke was receiving funds from unauthorised sources. CJP leaders responded by asking Singh, “Why were you negotiating with us then?” They were referring to meetings between group leaders and Singh, along with Union minister JP Nadda, during the CJP's protest against the government over the NEET issue earlier this year. Ranka asked, "Why were you negotiating with us then?" Saurav Das hit back at the minister, calling the allegation “baseless”. He shared, “The question of evidence is something we have been raising from day one, even before the first protest took place on June 6… Our first press conference was held on June 3, and ever since then, we have been asking the same question: What is the basis of your so-called allegation? So far, no evidence or justification has been provided…”

title: Hanuman Ansh OTT release: After its ₹342 crore box office run, devotional film based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba to arrive on SonyLIV
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Hanuman Ansh , the sensational movie about the life of Neem Karoli Baba, is finally coming to OTT. On Friday, director Vishal Chaturvedi revealed via a joint Instagram post that Hanuman Ansh will stream on SonyLIV from November 27! The devotional movie, made with a shoestring budget and no stars, has emerged as one of the biggest ticket-window success stories in Indian cinema history. The movie crossed the ₹ 300 crore rupees mark at the domestic ticket-window, a staggering feat given the movie was mounted on a mere ₹ 2 crore rupees budget.

Adding to this, Shobhinaw Satyaa plays the titular role in Hanuman Ansh. When and where to watch The announcement for the OTT rollout of Hanuman Ansh read, "A divine force. An extraordinary story. A movie loved by the nation, now coming home. Hanuman Ansh, arriving on Sony LIV on 27th November!"
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sony LIV (@sonylivindia)

Notably, Hanuman Ansh tells the story of Lakshminarayan, a young man who loses his mother and begins searching for answers about God, life and death. His search takes him across North India, where he tries to make sense of human suffering and the larger questions of existence. This spiritual journey eventually leads to his transformation into Neem Karoli Baba, whose teachings continue to inspire devotees around the world.
As per the latest buzz, The movie stars Shobhinaw Satyaa in the lead role alongside Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi, Gulshan Pandey and Bhagvandas Patel.

In further updates, The movie collected ₹ 342.44 crore rupees net and ₹ 452.86 crore rupees worldwide, according to figures shared by Sacnilk. The movie had a slow start and was actually written off after its first two weeks in theatres. Hanuman Ansh opened at a paltry ₹ 10 lakh and had collected barely ₹ 1.50 crore rupees in its first two weeks. However, after that, positive word of mouth took over, and the ticket sales shot up. Since its fourth week, Hanuman Ansh collected over ₹ 60 crore rupees in net at the Indian ticket-window each week. In its eighth week, Hanuman Ansh crossed the ₹ 300-crore rupees mark at the domestic ticket-window, something fewer than 25 Hindi films have managed before it. It spent over 80 days at the ticket-window, a momentous feat in itself.

On top of that, Hanuman Ansh managed to surpass the lifetime ticket-window hauls of several pan-India films, including Vijay’s Jana Nayagan ( ₹ 324 crore rupees), Yash’s Toxic ( ₹ 341 crore rupees) and Ram Charan’s Peddi ( ₹ 342 crore rupees).

title: Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu bungalow Jalsa among locations named in bomb threat email: Report
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The threat comes amid heightened security around the star following an earlier alert and the recent firing incident involving Tiger Shroff in Juhu.
Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan’s bungalow named in bomb threat email

Meanwhile, According to ANI, Mumbai authorities received a bomb threat email that as per reports mentioned the Bombay High Court, Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Mahalaxmi Racecourse and Amitabh Bachchan’s Juhu bungalow, Jalsa. Following the threat, security personnel immediately initiated searches at the premises identified in the email.

Notably, Bomb Detection and Disposal Squads (BDDS) carried out thorough inspections of the locations. However, police officials verified that nothing suspicious was discovered during the searches, bringing some relief amid the security alert.
As per the latest buzz, Amitabh Bachchan’s security heightened following earlier threat

In further updates, This is not the first time Bachchan’s residence has been mentioned in a bomb threat. On Friday, October 23, the Mumbai mayor’s office as per reports received a similar threat email that named the star’s Juhu residence, the mayor’s office and Mahalaxmi Racecourse. The racecourse is also scheduled to host singer-star Diljit Dosanjh’s performance on November 27.

On top of that, Following the earlier alert, security arrangements outside Jalsa were strengthened on October 25, when Bachchan continued his customary Sunday meeting with followers. The star also maintained the tradition on November 1, but with additional precautions. He greeted admirers from behind a transparent bulletproof enclosure, accompanied by his son Abhishek Bachchan, while security personnel monitored the gathering.
The latest threat comes amid increased attention on the safety of Bollywood personalities following a firing incident in Juhu earlier this month.

title: Salman Khan says fans' focus should be on Rama and Sita in Ramayana, not on ' ₹4000 crore budget or VFX'
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana Part 1 is not only the most anticipated movie of the year but also the most expensive movie in Indian history. Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana rolled out worldwide on a grand scale on November 5. Star Salman Khan has now spoken about the rollout of Ramayana and addressed the much-discussed ₹ 4,000 crore rupees budget of the movie franchise.

Adding to this, Salman Khan has shared his stance on the narrative surrounding Ramayana rollout. What Salman shared At the trailer launch of his soon-to-release movie Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, Salman Khan was asked about Ramayana. The star shared, "I just think Ramayana ka charcha Ramayana pe hona chahiye na ki VFX and cost of production par (I think the discussion on Ramayana should be on the scripture and not on the VFX or cost of production). I think this narrative ki 4000 (budget of Ramayana) aur VFX, VFX, VFX. I just don't think ki that is correct.

Meanwhile, He stressed, "I just think ki Ramayana ka charcha Ramayana ke upar hi hona chahiye - Rama, Ravana, Sita. (The focus should shift on the characters- Rama, Ravana and Sita)." Salman also shared that Lord Ram was a good son, a good husband, a good father and a good warrior. The same qualities also applied to his character in Maatrubhumi, shared the star.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Movie Talkies (@movietalkies)

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Hindu epic. The ambitious project features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana and Sunny Deol as Hanuman.

In further updates, Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu and his battle against the asura king Ravana after the latter abducts his wife, Sita.

On top of that, The movie also stars Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutta. The movie has already crossed the ₹ 100 crore rupees mark in India within two days of rollout.

Maatrubhumi is directed by Apoorva Lakhia and produced by Salman Khan under his Salman Khan Films banner. It also stars Chitrangada Singh, Mukesh Rishi, Ankur Bhatia, Abhilash Chaudhary, Abhishree Sen, Zeyn Shaw, Javed Khan and Vipin Bhardwaj. The movie will be rolled out in theatres on December 4.

title: Ramayana actor whose portions as Sumantra were edited out of film says he is still grateful for the experience
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The most anticipated movie of the year, Ramayana , has finally rolled out in theatres. Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Nitesh Tiwari's movie is an adaptation of Valmiki's epic and also draws from other sources of the story, including Tulsidas' Ramcharitmanas. Despite being divided into two parts, the movie has not been able to include each and every character that was part of the epic. One such character was of Sumantra, played by star Satyen Chaturvedi.

Adding to this, Satyen Chaturvedi shared that being considered for a character from our epic was enough. What the star shared In Ramayana, Sumantra was the trusted advisor and primary charioteer to King Dasharatha and later Lord Rama. Star Satyen Chaturvedi shot for the movie as Sumantra, but unfortunately, his scenes were not part of the final edit. Still, he has no regrets. The star took to his Instagram to share pictures from the shoot days and shared that he is still ‘grateful’ for the experience. He wrote, “Not every scene an star shoots makes it to the final screen, and that’s part and parcel of our journey. My portions as Sumantra in @iamnamitmalhotra Ramayana, directed by @niteshtiwari22 , have been edited out.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Satyen Chaturvede (@satyen.chaturvedi)

Notably, He added, “Nevertheless, being considered for a character from our epic and getting the opportunity to be part of a movie of this magnitude has been an incredible experience. A heartfelt thank you to @mukeshchhabracc for considering me for this role. The scenes may not have made it to the screen, but the memories and the experience will always remain. Grateful to have been a part of this magnificent journey. Thank you, Universe. Jai Shree Ram.”

title: Ajay Devgn purchases 2-acre agricultural land in Karjat for Rs 1.6 crores
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:
The latest acquisition adds to his existing real estate portfolio, which includes a Juhu bungalow and five commercial office units in Oshiwara.

Adding to this, The transaction was registered on October 29, 2026. As per the sale deed, Rashid Hasanmiya Patel has been named as the seller, while the purchaser is listed as Ajay alias Vishal Veeru Devgan, the star's full name as recorded in the document. The land measures 0.829 hectares, which is equivalent to around 2.05 acres.

Meanwhile, The purchase price works out to approximately Rs 78 lakhs per acre. According to the registration details, Devgn paid stamp duty of Rs 9.6 lakhs, along with a registration fee of Rs 30,000. This takes the total transaction-related expenditure to approximately Rs 1.70 crores, excluding other incidental charges. The sale deed also states that the payment was made through banking channels in multiple instalments.

Notably, The latest acquisition adds to Ajay Devgn's reported residential and commercial property holdings across Mumbai. Over the years, the star has made several investments in real estate, including residential properties and commercial office spaces.

As per the latest buzz, One of his major reported acquisitions was a bungalow in Juhu, which he purchased jointly with his mother, Veena Devgn, for Rs 47.5 crores in 2021. Spread across 474.4 square metres, the property was subsequently leased to Florian Hurel Salon Private Limited in August 2026. The five-year lease agreement is expected to generate rental income of approximately Rs 10.61 crores.

In further updates, In 2023, Devgn also purchased five commercial office units in the Signature building in Oshiwara, Andheri West, for a combined amount of Rs 45.09 crores. Located on the 16th and 17th floors, the offices have a combined built-up area of approximately 13,293 sq ft and include 14 parking spaces.

On top of that, The star has also leased out portions of his commercial property portfolio. In September 2024, he rented out a 3,455 sq ft office space in Signature Tower to Kabir Khan Entertainment for a monthly rent of Rs 7 lakh. Later, in May 2025, another office measuring 2,545 sq ft was leased to Bombay Design Centre Private Limited for an initial monthly rent of Rs 5.47 lakhs. The five-year agreement is expected to generate approximately Rs 3.3 crores.

title: Vidyut Jammwal says Tiger Shroff is stressed after firing incident, reveals actor is trying his best to move on
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Vidyut Jammwal was among the first to post a video in support of Tiger Shroff after shots were fired at the star near a football ground in Juhu, Mumbai. In the video, Vidyut called out people for not coming to Tiger's aid, attempting to nab the shooters or doing anything beyond recording the incident. In a recent interaction, Vidyut spoke about his conversation with Tiger after the incident and revealed what prompted him to share the video.

Adding to this, Vidyut Jammwal shared that Tiger Shroff is trying his best to move on. 'Tiger is stressed' Speaking on Ranveer Allahbadia's podcast, Vidyut shared he advised Tiger not to limit himself or stop playing football following the firing incident. When asked how Tiger was doing after the incident, Vidyut shared, "He is happy, stressed for sure. I was also telling him that not many people have had the experience of someone shooting at their faces. This happens in the army. So, it cannot be a normal experience. Nobody can fathom that experience, nobody can say that this is how you should be. He is stressed, and he has every reason to be. I told Tiger that he has to be stressed because there has been an attempt to murder him, so it cannot be a normal experience. So, he is good and trying his best to get out of this."
Meanwhile, When asked why he had posted the video, Vidyut shared that he was upset because nobody came to Tiger's aid, even though several people recorded the incident.

Notably, He shared, "We were chatting and when he told me that whole experience that he experienced - isolating himself from everybody around. It ticked me off. My first thought was, this is the problem with our country. That nobody does anything. Now, you will have a reason that he had a gun...my thought was somebody should run, where will our heroes come out from? I told Tiger that his driver should have crushed him, some rickshaw guy should have come out. I was not expecting everyone to run away. One hero. My question was, why did nobody run? There were 100 cameras. Everybody had a video, but there was no attempt to do anything. That ticked me off and that was the reason I posted the video."

As per the latest buzz, On October 18, unidentified gunmen opened fire at Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area as he was leaving after playing football. As per the latest buzz, three men arrived on a motorcycle and fired multiple rounds at his vehicle before fleeing. Tiger escaped without any gunshot injuries, while his driver and a bystander sustained injuries and were taken to hospital. The police has arrested a total of 13 people in connection with the case.

title: Salman Khan denies that Indian government pressured him to change Maatrubhumi script, says film has nothing against China
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Apoorva Lakhia’s Salman Khan -starrer Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace has undergone a major overhaul since it went into production in 2025. Initially titled Battle of Galwan, the movie was supposed to explore the 2020–2021 China–India skirmishes. Amid chatter that the Indian government pressured the movie team to change the story, Salman shut down these rumours at the trailer launch event in Mumbai on Friday.

Adding to this, Salman Khan at the trailer launch of his soon-to-release movie Maatrubhumi in Mumbai. (AFP) Salman Khan shuts down rumours about Maatrubhumi At the press conference during the Maatrubhumi trailer launch, Salman was asked why he would star in a movie about war with China after starring in a movie about cross-border unity, such as Bajrangi Bhaijaan (2015). He responded, stating that not only was the perception about the movie untrue, but the Indian government hadn’t pressured them to change the script.

Meanwhile, “This narrative that we are going against China or that our government has pressured us to change the script or rewrite it…this is all nonsense. It’s not true at all,” he clarified, further explaining, “We have made a movie about soldiers and what they and their families go through. We have shown that side and this side too. So, there are no negative forces here. Only their circumstances are such. And for these soldiers, the nation comes first. They like each other, but when a situation arises, both sides try to resolve it.”

Notably, He did, however, admit that Apoorva had a different idea for the movie at first. “Our director had a different version at first….” he shared with an awkward pause, nodding his head. As the actors around him laughed and the director agreed, he added, “There was,” without elaborating. Salman made it clear that Maatrubhumi was not a biopic, but it was only inspired by a line his father, Salim Khan, once told him. “In war, a bullet reaches its target; it reaches the mother’s heart.”

As per the latest buzz, When another reporter asked him if his movie was against China, Salman replied, “I just wanted a movie which is man on man, that’s all. Yes, there are Chinese and us in it, which created the perception that it would ruin our relationship. I don’t believe that Salman Khan has made a movie here, be it for, against, or anything. I don’t think the Chinese will now say, Salman Khan has made this movie; let’s attack them. If Jackie Chan makes a movie, I don’t think our army would attack them for it.”

In further updates, Maatrubhumi is directed by Apoorva Lakhia and produced by Salman Khan under his Salman Khan Films banner. It also stars Chitrangada Singh , Mukesh Rishi, Ankur Bhatia, Abhilash Chaudhary, Abhishree Sen, Zeyn Shaw, Javed Khan and Vipin Bhardwaj. The movie will be rolled out in theatres on December 4.

On top of that, Despite having a Master's degree in Journalism and over a decade of experience in print and digital media as a field reporter and sub-editor at organisations such as The Times of India and Reader's Digest, Neeshita Nyayapati remains a movie buff first and a Chief Content Producer second. She fell in love with movies in childhood and believes nothing matches the magic of watching a good movie that moves you with a warm tub of popcorn in hand. Her love for writing about cinema follows that. Come Friday, you'll find her at her happy place, the movies, catching the latest rom-com or masala offering, for reviews or otherwise. As for the rest of the week, she's here reporting the juiciest news in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada and Hindi or bringing out the best of celebs in interviews. While her niche is Telugu cinema, Neeshita likes to dabble in a little bit of everything to stay up to date. From movie announcements to scandals and hard news angles, she has explored it all. A good book, a comforting cup of hot chocolate, puppy kisses and a stunning beach view are all she needs to unwind. Her passion for biking and travelling has taken her to various places across the country. title: Dilwali Diwali review: This sweet and nostalgic film starring Manoj Pahwa will tug at your heartstrings
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The West has a tradition of bringing out a festive movie pretty much every Christmas, one that captures the cheer and spirit of the season. Why shouldn't we have something similar for Diwali ? After all, it's one of the biggest festivals on our calendar, and there's no dearth of stories rooted in the emotions it brings with it. Interestingly, Indian OTT platforms seem to be warming up to the idea of creating their own Diwali specials. Which brings us to Dilwali Diwali.

Adding to this, Dilwali Diwali is available to watch on Netflix. The premise Directed by Ritesh Menon, the movie revolves around the Sikkas. A video call from their son Ansh ( Mihir Ahuja ), who is settled abroad, sends them scurrying back to their posh home in an upscale residential building. He announces that he is coming home for Diwali, and the news sets the family in motion. Soon we discover that the Sikkas had traded their old life and familiar neighbourhood for this swanky house that their son bought for them. What seemed like an upgrade has come at the cost of something far more valuable: a sense of belonging. What happens next, as secrets tumble out from both sides, forms the rest of the story.

Meanwhile, Running for just about an hour, the movie is like that Diwali sweet you pick up during a festive visit: not enough to satiate your hunger, but certainly enough to leave you smiling. The screenplay is decidedly straightforward, with little dramatic twists or narrative surprises. But sometimes, simplicity is the point. The premise taps into an emotion that is relatable, particularly for those who live away from home and know what it feels like to miss the familiar chaos and togetherness of festivals. It also gently nudges us to think about the little compromises families make in the name of giving their loved ones a better life, and whether material comforts can ever replace the warmth of a community.

Notably, What makes this one a good watch is the cast. Manoj Pahwa and Neelu Kohli shoulder the movie on their experienced shoulders. As the conflicted parents who can’t get themselves to tell their son that the new house belongs to a world they don’t identify with, they are simply on point. They have an easy chemistry. Complimenting them perfectly is Mihir as the son. Aurra Bhatnagar as Mahi is also fine.

As per the latest buzz, Overall, Dilwali Diwali is a small, feel good watch. It reminds you that the best part of any festival is not necessarily the house you celebrate it in, but the people and memories that make it feel like home. Go for it.

In further updates, Rishabh Suri is an Assistant Editor, movie critic, and professional overthinker of plot points. He writes for HT City, keeping pace with an industry where news cycles expire long before the popcorn gets cold. He completed his graduation in English Honours from Kirori Mal College, followed by a Master’s degree in English Literature-effectively training his brain to over-analyse classic texts before applying those exact same skills to 3-hour Bollywood blockbusters. He got into the profession when he had barely graduated from college and has been at HT ever since. At HT, Rishabh reviews films with a simple rule: skip the dense academic jargon and get straight to the point. Beyond reviews, as Assistant Editor, he helps navigate the broader circus of showbiz, tracking everything from OTT shifts to sudden ticket-window panics. In a beat driven by loud PR machinery and carefully scripted answers, Rishabh prefers cutting through the noise to focus on how stories get made and why trends shift. When he isn’t writing against a deadline, he is usually sitting in a dark theater, compulsively memorising dialogues. title: Salman Khan announces December 4 release date for his much-delayed movie 'Maatrubhumi'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Mumbai, Superstar Salman Khan on Friday opened up that his much-delayed war drama movie "Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace" will finally make its debut in theatres across the country on December 4.

Adding to this, Salman Khan announces December 4 rollout date for his much-delayed movie 'Maatrubhumi' Salman, who headlines the Apoorva Lakhia-directed movie, based on the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between Indian and Chinese troops, shared the rollout date at the movie's promotional event here.
Meanwhile, Asked about the delay in the movie's rollout, Salman shared the team wanted to ensure that the visual effects were up to the mark.

Notably, "Today, there are a lot of VFX experts out there who examine each and every shot of a movie. So, with this movie, we don't want to give anyone an opportunity to zoom in on a scene and criticise its VFX. We want this movie to visually blow everyone's mind. It is a beautifully shot movie," the superstar told reporters.

As per the latest buzz, "We thought we would be able to complete the movie in 45-50 days, but madam got injured, and it took her time to recover. We were earlier supposed to rollout the movie in either January or June, but it was then pushed to August. Now, we will rollout it on December 4," he added.

In further updates, The movie, which was earlier titled "Battle of Galwan" before being rechristened "Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace", is inspired by the military standoff in eastern Ladakh in May 2020.

On top of that, Clashes at the Galwan Valley in June that year resulted in a severe strain in ties between India and China. Twenty Indian Army personnel laid down their lives in the Galwan Valley clashes.
Salman essays the role of Bikkumalla Santosh Babu, who laid down his life along with 19 other soldiers of the 16 Bihar Regiment during the clash.

title: Delhi HC asks Doosra makers to add disclaimer, give ₹2 crore bank guarantee in Sourav Ganguly case
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

There is a new development in Sourav Ganguly's legal battle over the movie Doosra. As per PTI, the Delhi High Court has asked the movie's makers to add a disclaimer and give ₹ 2 crore rupees bank guarantee on Sourav’s plea over personality rights violations. The cricketer had accused the makers of commercially exploiting his identity, personality and iconic moments from his cricketing career without his permission.

Adding to this, Sourav Ganguly had accused makers of Doosra of commercially exploiting his identity. The dispute also involves movie production and distribution company Luv Films, which had acquired the rights to make an authorised biopic on Ganguly, titled Dada : The Sourav Ganguly Story, starring Rajkummar Rao.

Meanwhile, The row began ahead of the theatrical rollout of Doosra: India's Other Freedom Struggle on October 23. Ganguly and Luv Films LLP filed a lawsuit against the movie's makers, alleging that it used elements of the former cricketer's identity and career without authorisation. Luv Films also argued that the movie interfered with the rights granted to it under its agreement to make an authorised biographical movie on the cricketer.

Notably, The former cricketer's legal team particularly objected to the movie's portrayal of India's historic 2002 NatWest Series final against England at Lord's. Sourav's shirtless celebration on the Lord's balcony, after India defeated England to win the final, remains one of the most iconic moments of his cricketing career.

As per the latest buzz, According to cricketer's counsel, the second half of Doosra heavily focuses on the NatWest Series final and uses moments associated with the former cricketer to promote the movie.

In further updates, The makers have maintained that Doosra is not a biopic on Ganguly but a fictional story about a middle-class girl from Rajasthan who finds inspiration in the cricketer's achievements. Their legal team also argued that they had obtained the necessary permissions from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) to use footage from the 2002 NatWest Series. They further contended that Ganguly's personality rights do not give him ownership of cricket match footage.

On top of that, In earlier hearings, the Delhi High Court declined Ganguly's request to stop the theatrical rollout of Doosra. However, it sought a response from the filmmakers and directed them to arrange a screening of the movie so that the court could examine the objections.

During the October 29 hearing, the court asked Ganguly to identify the specific portions of Doosra that allegedly infringed his personality rights, along with the reasons for his objections. The court also sought details of the disputed scenes, including their timestamps, to examine the allegations.

title: Unaccustomed Earth trailer: Freida Pinto, Siddharth explore lost love and second chances in show based on Jhumpa Lahiri's book
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

It is always special when a beloved book gets a new life on screen. This time, Jhumpa Lahiri's internationally acclaimed 2008 short story collection, Unaccustomed Earth, is being adapted into an eight-episode series. Starring Freida Pinto and Siddharth , the show brings together characters and stories from the original collection, weaving them into a continuous narrative.

Adding to this, Unaccustomed Earth stars Freida Pinto and Siddharth in lead roles. Unaccustomed Earth trailer The trailer introduces Freida Pinto as Parul Chaudhary, a married Indian-American woman and mother who begins to realise that she has been sleepwalking through life. After being diagnosed with cancer, she returns from Mumbai to her old life at Cambridge, US. The change brings her face-to-face with memories of her past, including an old love played by Siddharth, whom she had lost to an arranged marriage. As the two reconnect, old feelings resurface, setting off a series of events that complicate Parul's personal life and relationships.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the show, Freida shared it would immerse audiences in the traditions, food and culture of an Indian-American Bengali family. She explained how the series explores a community that has rarely been represented on television in such a detailed manner.

Notably, She shared, “It’s the kind of South Asian American community that we’ve never seen on television. We haven’t seen it before through this very holistic, culture-embracing way, while also dealing with the complexities of what it is to be this tight-knit community. Every character has something universal. From the perspective of Parul’s character is the question, ‘How far would you go to live the dream that you really want to live? And are you up for the consequences?’”

As per the latest buzz, The eight-episode family drama is created and written by Madhuri Shekar, known for her work on 3 Body Problem and The Nevers. Apart from Freida Pinto and Siddharth, the ensemble cast includes Sarayu Blue, Indraneil Sengupta, Adi Roy and Iyla Sundarsingh McKaig.

In further updates, Produced by John Wells Productions and Warner Bros., the series is executive produced by Shekar, John Wells, Ritesh Batra, Jhumpa Lahiri, Nisha Ganatra, Erica Saleh, Erin Jontow and Celia Costas. Batra, known for directing Irrfan Khan's critically acclaimed movie The Lunchbox, will also direct and executive produce the first two episodes.

On top of that, Before Unaccustomed Earth, another of Jhumpa Lahiri's celebrated literary works made it to the big screen. The Namesake (2006), directed by Mira Nair and starring Irrfan and Tabu, was widely acclaimed.
Unaccustomed Earth will premiere on Netflix on December 17.

title: Mahesh Bhatt says he was in tears watching son-in-law Ranbir Kapoor in Ramayana, feels actor ‘touched the God in him’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramayana is receiving praise from all quarters, but for star Ranbir Kapoor , some of the most special appreciation has come from his family. Ranbir's father-in-law and filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt lauded the movie, particularly Ranbir's portrayal of Lord Rama. During a recent interaction, Mahesh recalled how he almost broke down while watching the scene in which Rama is sent into exile.

Adding to this, Mahesh Bhatt lauded Ranbir Kapoor's portrayal of Lord Rama in Ramayana. ‘I tried hard not to cry’ In conversation with Variety India, Mahesh shared, "Just before the interval, Rama was sent into exile for 14 years. I felt my throat close. I tried hard not to cry. I had gone [to watch the movie] with young filmmakers and writers, and people in the hall knew they were sitting with Ranbir Kapoor’s father-in-law. When the lights came on, I tried to hide my tears. I couldn’t. Nor could I say much. Great experiences make you silent."

Meanwhile, Mahesh also lauded the movie's director, Nitesh Tiwari, for his sensitive portrayal of Rama and Ravana. He lauded Yash's performance as Ravana and shared Ranbir's portrayal of Rama brought out a side of the star that his previous films had not explored. He shared, "Yash mesmerized me as Ravana. Nitesh Tiwari reins in all that power; it could so easily have become too much. I was still under its spell when Ranbir entered, and the movie did not immediately rise for me with his arrival. Then he walked towards the camera and folded his hands. I saw him touch something in himself that his other films had never asked him to. I felt he had touched the God in him. As the family gathered around Rama, the epic came close. Arun Govil was heartbreakingly total."

Notably, On Thursday, Alia Bhatt had shared pictures of their daughter Raha from the sets of Ramayana and penned a heartfelt note for Ranbir. Praising his dedication to the movie, she wrote, “You poured everything into this one and somehow still had all of it left for her. So proud of you Ranbir and of every single person who brought their heart and soul to this incredible experience at the movies. Some stories are bigger than all of us & Ramayana is one of them.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Alia Bhatt 💛 (@aliaabhatt)

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman.

On top of that, The ensemble cast also includes Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, and Kajal Aggarwal. Sunny Deol is set to play Lord Hanuman in Part 2. Produced by Namit Malhotra, the ambitious project has a combined budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees for both instalments.

title: Gaiety-Galaxy made stars feel like SUPERSTARS; where are they now? Bollywood's RADIO SILENCE raises eyebrows as Manoj Desai pays FULL salaries despite ZERO revenue for 2 months
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Many expected the theatre to resume operations within a week or two. However, what has astonished movie lovers and industry members alike is that nearly two months have passed, and the issue remains unresolved.

Adding to this, Gaiety-Galaxy has always been synonymous with the quintessential big-screen experience, where audiences whistle, clap, cheer and hoot to their hearts' content, especially during mass entertainers. Two such films, Drishyam The Conclusion and Jailer 2 , were rolled out last month, but sadly, neither could be screened at the iconic complex. The of late rolled out Ramayana , too, missed out on a rollout at Gaiety-Galaxy. One can only imagine the frenzy that would have erupted in the auditoriums during the entry sequences of Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sunny Deol.

Meanwhile, An industry insider commented, “Manoj Desai (executive director of G7 and also Maratha Mandir) and his team are trying their best to get the issues sorted. But since it’s a government-related procedure, it's taking time and no one knows how much more time will be taken to get the issue sorted. Meanwhile, Manoj Desai is keeping the morale high of the employees. He is paying full salaries to his employees even though he has not collected a single paisa since September 7 from G7. The employees are grateful for getting their wages, especially in these festival times. But they miss the theatre and can’t wait to get back and serve the patrons.”
Notably, However, what has particularly astonished the industry insider, as well as several followers of Gaiety-Galaxy, is the complete lack of support from Bollywood celebrities.

As per the latest buzz, The insider thundered, “So many actors learned that they became stars when they saw the films getting an insane response in Gaiety-Galaxy. They have visited the theatre to check theatre reactions and to promote their films and themselves. They also proudly shared videos of followers hooting, whistling and dancing during the movie at Gaiety-Galaxy. And now, not a single one of them has posted anything about the theatre. Agreed that they’ll reason that the cinema complex is shut due to non-renewal of license and they fear being trolled over it. But at least they can write ‘Missing Gaiety-Galaxy’ or ‘hope the issues are resolved soon’. This may hopefully bring attention to the theatre and may speed up the process. Alas, there’s radio silence.”

In further updates, Meanwhile, as the closure approaches the two-month mark, the uncertainty continues for the management, employees and countless moviegoers who have made Gaiety-Galaxy an inseparable part of their movie-watching experience.

On top of that, Gaiety-Galaxy was established on November 24, 1972. Ramesh Sippy’s much-loved Seeta Aur Geeta (1972) was the inaugural movie. G7 multiplex originally started with just 3 theatres – Gaiety, Galaxy and Gemini. Gaiety and Galaxy are the biggest screens, consisting of a stall and balcony. While Gaiety is the bigger one, comprising nearly 1000 seats, Galaxy has around 800 seats. Gemini, with just one class, has around 240 seats.

In the late 90s, the management added 4 more theatres. Grace, the preview theatre, which is not open to the public, was constructed above the balcony of Gaiety. Gem, located next to Galaxy’s stall and Glamour, constructed between Galaxy’s stall and the balcony, and has just around 45 seats. And finally, there’s a 105-seater Gossip. This cinema hall also has a separate entrance at the back.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 2 (updated live): Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film sees drop after big opening day, crosses ₹80 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana did not have the earth-shattering start at the ticket-window that its makers had hoped for. However, the movie still did great business, setting a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. But the true test begins now, on its first Friday. The movie is likely to see a drop in collections on its second day before the Diwali weekend picks up the pace again. It remains to be seen whether positive word of mouth will offset that drop, and by how much.

Adding to this, Ramayana stars Yash as Ravana alongside Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama. Ramayana ticket-window update Ramayana began with houseful shows on day 1, netting ₹ 64.85 crore rupees net in India on its opening day. The figure was low given the movie’s scale, but it was still the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. On Friday, Ramayana began on a slower pace in the morning shows. By 4 PM on day 2, the movie had collected ₹ 19.23 crore rupees net in India, taking its two-day haul to over ₹ 84 crore rupees . The movie should aim to cross the ₹ 100-crore rupees barrier by the end of the day and hope for a strong weekend to bounce back and regain momentum.

Meanwhile, What is worrisome for the movie is that its earnings have come largely on the back of some good performance by the Hindi version. Despite Yash ’s presence as Ravana, the Kannada version has started extremely slowly. It collected just ₹ 7.50 crore rupees on day 1 and has lacked pace on day 2 as well. Of the other versions, Telugu has fared well, while Malayalam and Tamil are just filling the ranks. The makers would hope that positive critical reviews and audience reactions will lead to increased footfall in the days to come.

Notably, On its opening day, Ramayana beat the opening-day hauls of blockbusters such as Pathaan ( ₹ 57 crore rupees), Animal ( ₹ 63 crore rupees), and Drishyam 2 ( ₹ 62 crore rupees). However, it also missed out on Bollywood’s all-time day-one record, set by Ranveer Singh’s Dhurandhar 2 ( ₹ 102 crore rupees), and fell short of Adipurush as well ( ₹ 86.75 crore rupees). The trend continued on the second day. By the end of day 2, Adipurush had collected ₹ 151 crore rupees net in India. Ramayana is almost certain to miss the mark. However, it must be noted that Adipurush’s first two days in theatres were a Friday and a Saturday, while Ramayana’s first two days included a working Thursday and Friday.

As per the latest buzz, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.
